title: throughput-sla-convergence-orchestrator-and-util-snapshotter
body:
throughput-sla-convergence-orchestrator-and-util-snapshotter

Motivation: Dedicated capacity currently relies on static commitments or reactive scaling which causes oscillation between over-provision and underutilization. This PR introduces a Convergence Orchestrator that gradually aligns tenant reservations to sustained observed throughput while preserving short-duration burst headroom via a multiplexer guard. It also adds a Utilization Snapshotter that emits compact occupancy deltas used by the orchestrator and the consoles/alerts.

Summary of changes: 
- Convergence Orchestrator: controller that computes a target reservation fraction based on exponentially-weighted sustained throughput, a conservative safety multiplier, and a configurable hysteresis window. Includes safeguards to avoid starvation when traffic patterns shift abruptly.
- Multiplexer Guard: logic that preserves a small burst allowance above the converged reservation so latency-sensitive requests get occasional headroom without impacting long-term guarantees.
- Utilization Snapshotter: lightweight service that samples per-tenant occupancy and tokenized throughput every 30s, emits compact delta metrics and a rolling 5-min histogram. Designed for low overhead and export to both Prometheus and the internal telemetry pipeline.
- Config and runtime flags: new config fields under dedicated.autoscale: convergence_window_sec, safety_multiplier, burst_multiplier, snapshot_interval_sec, snapshot_histogram_buckets. Default values chosen to be conservative.
- Telemetry and dashboards: new metrics (tenant_reservation_target, tenant_snapshot_util_p50/p90/p99, tenant_burst_allowed) and a dashboard tile.
- Tests and e2e: unit tests for convergence math, integration harness to validate no-regression in steady throughput, and a small canary job used during rollout.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-1984)
- [x] Unit tests added for convergence math and snapshot aggregation
- [x] Integration test validating no oscillation on synthetic peaky workloads
- [x] Telemetry and dashboard added
- [x] Feature-gated rollout with canary enabled

Design notes and safety: 
The orchestrator uses an EWMA over a 5m window (configurable) to derive a sustained throughput estimate. The target reservation is sustained_throughput * safety_multiplier. The burst allowance is burst_multiplier * sqrt(target_reservation) (heuristic chosen to scale sub-linearly with reservation) and strictly capped by a global per-pool burst budget. All changes are gated behind dedicated.flags.enable_sla_convergence. If the orchestrator is disabled, existing reservation logic is unchanged.

Rollout plan: 
1) Merge feature-flag guarded code to main behind disabled-by-default flag.
2) Enable in Canary fleet for 48 hours, monitor tenant_reservation_target drift and tenant_snapshot_util_p90.
3) Gradually enable on 10% of Dedicated fleets for 72 hours, validate no increased latency tail.
4) Ramp to 100% with monitoring and progressive rollback window.

Testing performed: 
- Unit: convergence math edge cases (zero traffic, sudden spike, gradual ramp).
- Integration: two-week synthetic run comparing static reservations vs orchestrator in a dedicated cluster; observed 12% reduction in average spare capacity with <1% increase in 99th latency.
- Load: canary run with 200 tenants, random sine-wave traffic; orchestrator converged within configured window and respected burst budget.

Files touched (high level): 
- services/dedicated/orchestrator/convergence_controller.go
- services/dedicated/orchestrator/multiplexer_guard.go
- services/dedicated/snapshotter/snapshotter.go
- pkg/telemetry/metrics_definitions.yaml
- infra/helm/dedicated-values.yaml (feature flags and defaults)
- web/console/src/pages/dedicated/tiles/tenant-util.tsx (dashboard)
- integrations/test/harnesss/dedicated_convergence_test.go
- api/openapi/dedicated.yaml (document new config schema)
- charts/observability/dedicated-dashboard.json

Backward compatibility: All config changes are optional and feature-flagged. No migration required for existing Dedicated customers.

Config knobs (defaults included): 
- convergence_window_sec: 300 (5m)
- safety_multiplier: 1.15
- burst_multiplier: 2.0
- snapshot_interval_sec: 30
- snapshot_histogram_buckets: "[0,0.5,0.75,0.9,0.99,1.0]"

Operational runbooks and alerts added: 
- Alert: tenant_reservation_target_delta > 50% sustained for 10m -> auto-disable orchestrator for tenant (TTL 30m)
- Alert: tenant_snapshot_util_p99 increases by >20% post-rollout -> rollback flag for pool
- Dashboard tile: reservation convergence trend, burst spend, per-tenant util histogram

Introduce a throughput SLA convergence controller and a lightweight per-tenant utilization snapshotter. Adds new config knobs for convergence window and safety multipliers. Improves steady-state reservation accuracy and provides new metrics for SLO observability. Requires rollout with feature-flag enabled for dedicated fleets.
Liam: Please justify the burst_multiplier heuristic; is sqrt arbitrary?
Author(Aisha): The sqrt was chosen to provide sublinear scaling; we evaluated linear vs sqrt on historical tenants and sqrt reduced worst-case pool burst spend by ~18% while keeping p99 latency similar. Added comment and benchmark in code.
Priya: Concerned about telemetry cardinality from snapshotter.
Author: Snapshotter emits a compact delta metric plus a 5-min rollup histogram rather than per-second points. Also added sampling at tenant-level when tenants > threshold and a sampling config.
Diego: Suggest adding a stronger safety floor for small tenants to avoid under-provisioning.
Author: Added min_reservation_floor config and updated math to apply floor for tenants with sustained_throughput below 1 tps.
Liam: CI flake on integration test, rerun passed.
Approvals: Liam approved on 2026-01-30; Priya approved on 2026-02-01; Diego approved with minor comments resolved.
CI pipeline: build (pass), unit-tests (pass), lint (pass with minor formatting warnings auto-fixed), integration (first run flaky - timed out on harness, rerun passed), e2e-canary (pass), telemetry-export-smoke (pass). Total duration ~42m. One flaky integration test (harness network) documented and filed as ENG-2041.
Merged by Eleanor Park via squash on 2026-02-02. Merge commit includes condensed change log and rollout instructions. Feature flag default remains disabled until canary validation. Post-merge actions: created canary job and scheduled monitoring for 72h.
If tenant_reservation_target_delta alert fires, manually toggle dedicated.flags.enable_sla_convergence for the affected pool to false and open an incident under SUP-5423. Watch tenant_burst_allowed spend for unexpected depletion. Use /tools/convergence/debug to pull last 5 snapshots for a tenant.

title: Introduce lightweight CI emulator and shared cache protocol to speed local dev feedback
body:
Introduce lightweight CI emulator and shared cache protocol to speed local dev feedback

Summary: This PR introduces a small cross-platform CI emulator (ci-emu) and a tiny shared cache protocol that together let engineers run a faithful, fast subset of our GitHub Actions pipelines locally or in ephemeral CI. Motivation: developers today wait multiple minutes for CI feedback from full workflows. The emulator reproduces job ordering, environment variable injection, matrix selection pruning, and artifact/cache lookup semantics but runs tasks locally (or in a remote dev runner) with a fraction of the overhead. The cache protocol is intentionally minimal (versioned headers + content-addressed blobs) to allow safe sharing between ephemeral runners and local dev without requiring a centralized service. Goals: 1) reduce round-trip time for lint/test/fast-integration by ~3-5x for most changes, 2) shrink the need to run full matrix jobs during early iteration, 3) keep production release pipelines untouched and gated. What changed (high level): - tools/ci/ci-emu/ : new Go-based emulator binary and small config loader (cli + library) - infra/ci/cache-protocol.md : spec for the cache protocol (HTTP headers, blob layout, simple attestation) - .github/workflows/ci-lite.yml : new lightweight workflow that calls the emulator in remote runner mode for ephemeral CI - scripts/ci/patch-workflow.sh : helper to run emulated subsets locally with the same env as Actions - ci/pinning/actions-versions.json : added pins for a couple of actions used by the emulator to reduce runtime surprises - docs/dev/ci-emulator.md : onboarding and troubleshooting guide Design notes: - ci-emu intentionally executes user-defined commands (make test, ./scripts/run-lint) in separate processes and captures stdout/stderr with timestamps so output ordering mirrors Actions logs. - The cache protocol uses a small JSON header with schema v1 and a content-addressed blob (sha256). Servers can implement it behind any transport; our implementation includes a tiny in-repo file-backed store for dev and a simple ephemeral s3-compatible example for CI. - Security: the emulator does not attempt to expose secrets; it only replays env vars provided by workflows. We added a whitelist for envs and a --allow-secrets flag for opt-in scenarios. - Non-goal: this change is not a full replacement for Actions; production release, E2E, and long-running matrix jobs still use the existing workflows. Commits summary: - Add ci-emu CLI + library (portions of the runtime runner moved from dev-scripts) - Add cache protocol spec and local file store implementation - Introduce ci-lite workflow and hook into dev docs - Add tests for emulator behavior and basic protocol conformance - Fix linting issues surfaced by running emulator pipelines Files changed (high level): - tools/ci/ci-emu/main.go (new) - tools/ci/ci-emu/runner/*.go (new) - infra/ci/cache-protocol.md (new) - .github/workflows/ci-lite.yml (new) - scripts/ci/patch-workflow.sh (new) - docs/dev/ci-emulator.md (new) - ci/pinning/actions-versions.json (modified) - scripts/ci/emulator-integration-test.sh (new) - workspace/config/dev-cache-store.go (new) - Makefile (changed) CI results and iteration: - Initial CI run: lint failed (golangci-lint rule for error wrapping). I pushed a follow-up fix in the same branch. - Unit/integration tests for ci-emu passed locally and in CI on the second run. - E2E matrix jobs were left unchanged and continued to pass in parallel. - Final CI status: all checks passed, coverage slightly increased for the runner package. Review conversation (condensed): - Ethan Liu: requested clearer separation between emulator env and production secrets; asked for a safe default to avoid accidental secret leakage. Response: added env whitelist + --allow-secrets opt-in and documented in dev guide. - Priya Kapoor: asked for a migration plan for maintainers to adopt the lightweight workflow. Response: added docs/dev/ci-emulator.md with suggested adoption steps and a checklist. - Marco Alvarez: requested tests for cache protocol version negotiation; added protocol unit tests and a test harness simulating two store backends. - Automation: added a small gating job that ensures ci-lite.yml does not run on release branches by mistake. Risk and rollout: - Opt-in for teams: new ci-lite workflow will not replace existing CI; maintainers can enable it by adding a small file in .github/ci-enabled/<team>. - The cache protocol is v1 and includes a schema version in headers to allow future incompatible changes. - No production behavior change expected; all release automation and deploy flows remain on the main workflows. Backwards compatibility: - No breaking changes to public APIs or release mechanics. - Developers can continue to run existing scripts; ci-emu is an additional option. Follow-ups and TODOs: - Evaluate telemetry for emulator adoption (ENG-1010) and add anonymous opt-in usage pings. - Add a minimal VS Code extension snippet to invoke ci-emu from the editor. - Explore using the cache protocol for model-metadata artifacts in Dedicated test harnesses. Merge and deployment: - Merged to main via squash on 2026-02-21 after approvals from the reviewer group. - Release note added to the changelog-dev internal doc. Links: linear tickets ENG-998, ENG-1010. Related PRs: refactor of dev-scripts (will follow in a separate PR).
Adds a lightweight local CI emulator (ci-emu) and a small, versioned cache protocol for ephemeral runners to speed developer iteration. No runtime behavior changes to production workflows; opt-in for devs and repo maintainers.
Opt-in developer feature; no changes to production release workflows.

title: Key rotation procedure + audit evidence checklist (KMS/Private)
body:
Key rotation procedure + audit evidence checklist (KMS/Private)

Summary: Adds customer/operator-facing documentation for key rotation in Redwood Private/Dedicated contexts, plus an audit-friendly evidence checklist that maps cleanly to common SOC2/ISO narratives. This PR is intended to reduce back-and-forth during enterprise security reviews by making our rotation steps and evidence artifacts explicit and repeatable.

Context / why: Regulated customers (and prospects) are asking for (a) a clear rotation procedure (including rollback criteria) and (b) the exact evidence they can expect to produce/receive (who approved, what changed, when it happened, what logs prove it). This doc set aligns with the ongoing KMS hardening effort and the rotation strategy in ADR-008.

What’s included: 1) New page: “Key rotation procedure (KMS envelope encryption)” covering prerequisites, roles/responsibilities (Customer vs Redwood), staged rollout, dual-read window, cutover, verification, and rollback. 2) New page: “Rotation evidence checklist” that can be used as a runbook attachment and as audit evidence. Includes templates for a rotation log entry, required screenshots/exports, and pointers to audit log event types. 3) Updates to navigation + cross-links from the Private KMS Operator Guide and Security FAQ sections to reduce discoverability issues.

Audience: Private operators, SRE/on-call, Security/GRC reviewers, Sales/SE support during enterprise security reviews.

Notes on scope: This is documentation-only and does not introduce new technical behavior. It references implementation behavior that is landing in the core repo (dual-read support, audit log events, healthchecks). Where behavior differs between Hosted vs Private, we call it out explicitly.

References: - ADR-008 (Key rotation strategy: dual-read window + cutover criteria) - Linear: ENG-4826 (evidence artifacts), PM-913 (customer expectations), ENG-4821 (initiative epic) - Support: SUP-19405 (customer evidence request / cutover questions)

Content highlights (key decisions captured in docs): - Rotation cadence: documented as customer-driven (typical quarterly/annual), with Redwood providing a repeatable procedure + evidence artifacts; the doc avoids committing to a universal cadence but includes guidance and defaults used in regulated deployments. - Dual-read / dual-decrypt window: documented as the recommended approach to avoid hard cutovers; includes a minimum observation window and explicit cutover criteria (error-rate and decrypt-mismatch signals). - Rollback: explicitly documented; includes triggers (e.g., elevated KMS errors, decrypt mismatches) and the fastest safe rollback path (toggle to prior key version + keep dual-read during investigation). - Evidence: checklist enumerates approvals, change tickets, timestamps, config diffs, audit log exports, and validation outputs from installer preflight (Private).

Screenshots/examples: Redacted examples are included (ARNs, tenant IDs, regions). Please flag anything that looks too close to production formatting.

Test plan: - Local docs build: `pnpm install && pnpm build` - Link check: `pnpm lint:links` - Preview reviewed in Netlify: see CI checks.

Checklist: - [x] Reviewed with Security (terminology + evidence expectations) - [x] Reviewed with SRE (rollback triggers + operational steps) - [x] Reviewed with Product (customer-facing positioning) - [x] Added cross-links from Private KMS operator guide - [x] Added “last reviewed” footer + owners for ongoing maintenance

Follow-ups (not in this PR): - Once PR redwood/pr-18541 lands, update evidence page to include final audit log event names/fields (placeholders included). - Once dashboards ship (observability-pack/pr-844), add a “Verification dashboards” subsection with canonical panel links per environment.

Kira Thompson (author) 2025-11-09: Done. Evidence checklist is now linked at the top and the responsibilities table is added under “Prereqs and ownership”.

Marcus Lin (Security Eng) 2025-11-10: Please tighten language around ‘fallback’ during KMS outage so it doesn’t imply we can decrypt without KMS. We can degrade availability and preserve correctness, but we should not suggest bypassing KMS. Also, add a note that key disable/delete is treated as an incident and requires Security escalation.

Olga Petrov (Compliance) 2025-11-11: Evidence checklist looks good. Can we explicitly call out acceptable substitutes when a customer cannot share screenshots (e.g., export from SIEM / audit-log-exporter)? Also add a “Retention” line for what we recommend customers retain.

title: introduce-temporal-tilt-detector-and-daypart-smoothing-dashboard
body:
introduce-temporal-tilt-detector-and-daypart-smoothing-dashboard

Motivation: transient daypart and seasonal patterns were generating noisy token-cost alerts and paging on short-lived shifts. This PR implements a lightweight 'Temporal Tilt Detector' that combines a daypart-aware baseline (hour-of-day/week-of-day bucketing), an EWMA trend baseline, and a seasonal-trend decomposition stage to produce a bounded tilt_score per route/tenant. The tilt_score is emitted as a low-cardinality metric and as a span tag to enable correlated traces for root-cause. Changes include: (1) new telemetry exporter fields (tilt_score, daypart, rolling_baseline) and bounded aggregation keys; (2) trace enrichment for tilt tagging; (3) a Grafana dashboard "Daypart Tilt & Cost Smoothing" with panels for tilt, smoothed token-cost, raw vs baseline, per-tenant drift heatmap and suggested mitigation actions; (4) updated alert rules that use dampening (15m suppression window for small tilts) and hysteresis to avoid flapping; (5) incident-bot integration to defer low-severity pages automatically when tilt is transient and non-regressive; (6) unit + integration tests and a micro-benchmark to validate detector latency on median payloads. Design notes: to control cardinality we bucket daypart into 6 coarse zones and restrict tilt emission to aggregation keys {route, model_family, tenant_tier} by default with an opt-in fine-grained label. We include a sampling guard for high-cardinality tenants and aggregate sketches for rollups. See docs link: RFC https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-1987 for algorithm rationale. Checklist: [x] implement detector algorithm prototype; [x] exporter + trace tag; [x] Grafana dashboard; [x] alert rule changes; [x] tests and bench; [x] docs and quickstart example.
Ethan Liu: Overall great direction. Concern: tilt_score might create high-cardinality if we emit with fine-grained labels. Can we ensure default emission is aggregated?
Priya Natarajan: Alert dampening makes sense. Please add a runbook stanza that lists manual override steps and how to revert the suppression window quickly in case of regression.
Liam O'Connor: Performance: detector runs in the ingest hot path. Bench shows 1.6ms median, but I'm seeing P95 at 12ms in initial runs. Need to validate under burst (10k rps).
SRE Team (comment): Prometheus scrape and storage impact needs estimates. Provide expected cardinality delta and retention guidance.
Maya Patel: Addressed cardinality by defaulting daypart -> 6 coarse bins and emitting tilt only for aggregation keys {route, model_family, tenant_tier}. Added opt-in label 'tilt_detail=true' for customers who want per-call tilt. Sampling guard added for >1k unique tenants per minute.
Maya Patel: Added runbook section in docs with explicit steps to toggle alert dampening and suggested rollback play. Saved a sample Linear task for runbook follow-ups ENG-1999.
Maya Patel: Investigated perf: optimized hot-path by moving seasonal smoothing to async micro-batch when latency budget tight. Re-ran bench: median 0.9ms, P95 3.8ms under 10k rps synthetic load (see bench_results.md).
Maya Patel: Included a small cardinality impact table and retention recommendations in the RFC. Prometheus storage impact estimated <3% for default config; opt-in detailed mode increases cardinality and should be monitored.
Add Temporal Tilt Detector: emits tilt_score and daypart labels for coarse drift detection; new Grafana dashboard 'Daypart Tilt & Cost Smoothing'; updated tilt_deviation alert with dampening and incident-bot defer integration. Default config is low-cardinality and non-breaking.

title: Compact defaults matrix and fallback planner for cost-aware inference
body:
Compact defaults matrix and fallback planner for cost-aware inference

Motivation: many customers hit higher-than-expected unit costs because sensible batching, cache, and quantization defaults are either too aggressive for small tail workloads or too conservative for high-throughput tenants. This PR introduces a compact defaults matrix generator plus a fallback planner that simplifies autopilot behavior for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments and gives ops explicit, auditable rules for graceful degradation. Key changes: 1) defaults matrix builder that consumes workload sketches (p95 latency, seq length distribution, qps buckets) and emits a small set of presets (batch_size, prefill_budget, kv_cache_ttl, quant_profile) tuned by cost-latency tradeoffs; 2) fallback planner that maps SLOs and capacity tiers to ordered fallback strategies (scale, model-variant, quant-fallback, regional-failover) and exposes a deterministic evaluation function for rollouts; 3) telemetry and unit-econ calibration hooks (metrics + synthetic-sample harness) so we can measure expected unit cost delta before enabling a profile; 4) CLI and Console surface to preview and apply suggested defaults; 5) docs and canary rollout plan. Checklist: implements unit tests and integration smoke tests; adds example workload sketches; includes rollout playbook and rollback steps; updates docs. Rollout plan: staged canary on 10% of new Hosted signups -> 25% -> 100% across regions with observability gating on unit_econ_regression and latency_violation alerts. Related work: ENG-4321 (cost defaults), ENG-4390 (fallback routing policies), SUP-1209 (customer support case patterns). Notable limitations: profiler relies on representative replay traces; aggressive quant profiles are gated by quality regression monitors. Requested reviewers: runtime and SRE for safety; CLI/docs for UX. Links: Linear ENG-4321 (internal), Support ticket SUP-1209 (internal).
Evan Summers (2025-11-07): Can you add an explicit safety budget for prefill that caps memory usage per-GPU? Otherwise high prefill on bursty tenants may OOM. Response: added prefill_budget cap and unit test in commit 7.
Priya Nandakumar (2025-11-09): The planner looks good but we need an opt-out for Dedicated customers with strict isolation. Response: added a policy flag and Console toggle; documented in docs file.
Jorge Alvarez (2025-11-11): CI flaked on the telemetry integration — looks like a timing dependency. Response: added retry/backoff in test harness and moved to deterministic mock clock.

title: Shadow traffic: telemetry events + ingestion hooks (v1)
body:
Shadow traffic: telemetry events + ingestion hooks (v1)

Context: Shadow traffic routing (ENG-5402) mirrors a sampled subset of prod requests to one or more shadow targets. To compute quality deltas (and to debug routing/scoring lag) we need a low-cardinality, privacy-aware set of telemetry events that (a) links the control and shadow inference outcomes, (b) can be ingested reliably in Hosted/Dedicated/Private, and (c) provides enough dimensions to slice by route/model/region without exploding metrics cardinality.

This PR introduces shadow traffic telemetry events and wires them into the ingestion pipeline (Kafka -> ingest -> warehouse tables) with initial dashboard stubs for internal dogfood.

What’s included: (1) New event schemas: shadow_pair_created (emitted when the mirror is scheduled), shadow_inference_completed (shadow target returned or timed out), and shadow_scoring_status (async scoring queued/completed/failed). Each event includes a stable shadow_pair_id and request_fingerprint (HMAC), plus required dimensions: tenant_id (hashed), route_id (low-card), control_model_id, shadow_target_id, deployment_mode, region, outcome, and timing fields. (2) Cardinality controls: disallow freeform tags in shadow telemetry, bucket user_agent, truncate prompt_length/response_length into fixed buckets, and explicitly drop prompt_id / conversation_id at emit-time. Route-level and model-level dimensions are included; anything higher-card must be attached via example sampling endpoints later (out of scope). (3) Ingestion pipeline hooks: adds validators/normalizers for the new events, forwards them through the existing ingest service, and creates the initial storage tables shadow_pairs_v1 and shadow_scoring_v1 (partitioned by day, clustered by tenant_hash + route_id). (4) Initial dashboards stubs: adds basic Grafana JSON stubs for shadow throughput, shadow target error rate, and scoring lag; these are intentionally minimal and will be expanded in observability-pack PR-391.

PII / data handling: This PR does not store raw prompts/responses. request_fingerprint is computed using an HMAC keyed per environment (see config), and tenant_id is hashed before leaving the data plane. Any headers included are allowlisted (content-type, accept, x-redwood-route) and explicitly exclude auth/cookie-like fields.

Testing: Unit tests for schema validation and normalization, golden tests for event-to-table mapping, and an end-to-end ingest test that emits a synthetic shadow_pair_created + shadow_inference_completed and asserts the warehouse row shape. Load testing / overhead benchmarking is tracked in ENG-5412.

Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag shadow_telemetry_v1 (default off). Dogfood tenants can enable via internal config. Fail-open: telemetry emission failures do not impact request path; ingestion lag only affects dashboards/metrics.

Follow-ups: (a) scoring payload references once redaction pipeline lands (ENG-5411), (b) additional aggregation views for confidence intervals, (c) tighten SLO alert thresholds once we have baseline dogfood data.

Notes for reviewers: please focus on (1) schema field choices and defaults, (2) cardinality guardrails, and (3) whether the ingestion mapping matches the query patterns we expect for Console drilldowns.
Adds v1 shadow traffic telemetry event schemas (pair + scoring status), ingestion mapping into analytics tables, and stub dashboards/alerts for dogfood/beta validation.
Nadia Rahman: Can we confirm we’re not emitting route_name anywhere? We’ve had issues when names include customer-provided slugs.
Caleb Johnson: Correct—route_name is dropped at emit-time; only route_id (UUID) is included. I also added a validator to hard-fail if route_name shows up in the event payload.
Allison Grant: The dashboard stubs look fine, but the scoring lag panel should use shadow_scoring_status rather than inference_completed. Otherwise we’ll misinterpret queue backlog as compute time.
Caleb Johnson: Good catch. Updated the stub query to compute lag from queued_at -> completed_at in shadow_scoring_v1. Left inference_completed for shadow target health panels.
Sean Gallagher: Please add a hard cap on emitted dimensions to protect metrics. Also, we need a way to detect when someone accidentally adds a high-card tag in the future.
Caleb Johnson: Added an allowlist-based dimension serializer + a unit test that asserts the final dimension set. Also wired a counter shadow_telemetry_dropped_fields_total when we drop unknown fields (for visibility).
Marcus Lin: HMAC key management: where is the secret stored for Private deployments?
Caleb Johnson: For Hosted/Dedicated it’s in our standard secrets store. For Private, it’s derived from the customer’s control-plane secret bundle; doc note added and defaults to rotate-on-upgrade. Implementation details also referenced in config comments; Security review tracked in ENG-5411 follow-up.
After merge, dogfood tenants should enable feature flag shadow_telemetry_v1 and validate: (1) shadow_pairs_v1 row counts match expected sampling rate, (2) no cardinality alerts triggered, (3) scoring lag panel remains stable under backlog. If cardinality alerts fire, see SUP-28510 notes and reduce dimensions before expanding sampling.

title: prioritized-runbook-queue-with-decay-and-responder-snooze
body:
prioritized-runbook-queue-with-decay-and-responder-snooze

Motivation: On-call queues accumulate runbooks and playbooks with varying usefulness over time. When multiple responders act concurrently, noisy low-value runbooks surface first and important but less-frequent playbooks are delayed. This change introduces a prioritized runbook queue that ranks candidate runbooks by a decaying relevance score, supports per-responder snooze windows, and exposes metrics and config for safe rollout.

What this PR does: 1) Implements a RunbookScorer service that computes a composite score from incident signal (severity, error-class frequency), recent successful mitigations, runbook age, and team-defined priority tags. Scores decay over time using an exponential half-life configurable per team. 2) Adds a prioritized queue layer to the incident-bot dispatcher that returns top-N runbooks for a responder instead of FIFO. 3) Adds responder-level snooze: when a responder marks a runbook as "snoozed" it is hidden for that user for a configurable backoff (defaults: 30m/2h/24h tiers). 4) Safe requeueing: runbooks that are requeued by agents get a temporary suppression boost if they repeatedly trigger for the same incident to avoid flapping. 5) Observability: Prometheus metrics (runbook_queue_size, avg_top_score, snooze_events_total, rescore_latency_seconds) and an OpenTelemetry trace span around scoring and dispatch. 6) Admin UI flags and feature-gates for gradual rollout (global, team-level, and user opt-out).

Checklist: - [x] Core scorer implementation and unit tests - [x] Prioritized queue integration and E2E smoke test against local emulated dispatcher - [x] Responder snooze UI endpoint + backend handling - [x] Metrics and tracing hooks - [x] Linear links and config knobs - [x] Feature gate + rollout plan - [x] Docs PR (linked)

Rollout plan: Stage 1 (canary): enable for internal oncall with runbook sampling, observe top-score distribution and alert on sudden queue-length regressions. Stage 2: enable team-by-team via console flag for teams that opt-in. Stage 3: wide rollout with 7-day monitoring window and automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Compatibility and fallback: If RunbookScorer fails or times out (>=250ms default), dispatcher reverts to FIFO and emits a metric runbook_score_failures_total. Feature is entirely opt-in via flags.

Notes: Tuning guidance included in the README. Linear tasks ENG-3121 and ENG-3178 capture follow-ups: telemetry dashboards and an A/B test to measure mean time to mitigation (MTTM) with prioritized ordering.

Aria Patel (author): Added scorer_test.go with mocked clock and parameterized half-life cases.

Evelyn Carter (reviewer): Two nits: 1) the default snooze tiers should be documented in config defaults; 2) prefer metrics namespace 'incidentbot_' for Prometheus to align with existing collectors.

Aria Patel: Updated values.incident-bot.yaml to include the snooze tier defaults and renamed metrics to incidentbot_runbook_* . Also added a short section in docs/runbook-priority.md.

Diego Ramos (reviewer): Suggest adding a safe guard so a maliciously crafted runbook cannot starve others by returning extremely high static score. Could we clamp scores per-runbook?

Default config keeps feature disabled. If enabling, monitor runbook_queue_size and mean top-score. Roll back by disabling the feature flag if queue length or MTTM regresses beyond configured thresholds.

title: introduce-presubmit-orchestrator-ci-telemetry-and-dep-hint-linter
body:
introduce-presubmit-orchestrator-ci-telemetry-and-dep-hint-linter

Context: As the repo has grown, presubmit hooks have accumulated ad-hoc ordering and duplicated setup costs across multiple language runners. This caused noisy flakiness in CI, slow feedback for small changes, and sprawl in scripts maintained across teams. Motivation: unify presubmit sequencing, surface CI-level telemetry (duration, cache hit/miss, matrix cardinality), and provide early guidance for dependency hygiene so engineers remove unnecessary devDependencies during PRs. Summary of changes: 1) Add a small Go-based presubmit-orchestrator (ci/orchestrator/) that defines ordered hook groups (setup, lint, unit, integration-smoke). It exposes a declarative manifest (ci/presubmit.yaml) that can be updated per-repo or per-path glob. 2) Introduce ci/telemetry-exporter: a lightweight helper that emits metrics (presubmit.duration_ms, cache.hit, test.flaky_count) to our internal telemetry endpoint and as a debug artifact in artifacts/ci-telemetry.json. 3) Dependency-hint linter (tools/dep-hint) that statically analyzes package manifests (package.json, go.mod, pyproject.toml) and heuristically flags devdeps that are not referenced by tooling paths in the patch. 4) Split lint runners into language-aware shards (ts-lint, go-lint, py-lint) and wire adaptive caching so only affected shards run by default. 5) Add a staged release hook that enforces a lightweight smoke test (release/smoke.sh) before promoting artifacts to the release pipeline. Migration steps: - No required action for developers. The orchestrator autodetects existing hook files and migrates them into the new manifest where safe; teams will get a migration PR in their subpackages if the heuristics are uncertain. - To opt out of telemetry, set ci/telemetry.yaml.disable: true in repo root. - Dep-hint linter can be disabled per-path with .dep-hint-ignore. Testing & validation: - Local unit tests for orchestrator and dep-hint included (ci/test/orchestrator_test.go, tools/dep-hint/tests/). - Ran presubmit smoke across core packages (redwood/, redwood-sdk-python/, redwood-helm-charts/) with representative patches. - Nightly run enabled for 48 hours in the feature branch to capture telemetry before merge. Rollout & safety: - Feature gated under repo-level flag ci.presubmit.orchestrator.enabled; turned on for main by this PR after a 7-day telemetry observation window. - Fallback: if orchestrator fails, the old scripts are executed (compat shim at ci/compat/). - Performance: median presubmit wall time reduced ~18% in observed workloads; cold-cache improvements from targeted shard execution reduced setup time by ~25%. CI details & history: - Initial run (workflow: presubmit/main) failed due to a flaky test in integrations/smoke (flake count: 1). Reproduced locally, added a small timeout backstop and retriggered. - Second run succeeded; telemetry exporter produced artifacts/ci-telemetry.json with aggregated bucketed latencies. - Lint stage produced actionable hints for ~27 open PRs across org (most common: unused jest-devtools and stale ts-node entries in package.json). Security considerations: - Telemetry exporter only sends aggregated numeric metrics and anonymized job tags; no source code or secrets. It is behind an allowlist and uses existing CI tokens with restricted scope. - Dep-hint linter is read-only and runs in CI; it does not modify manifests automatically. Implementation notes: - The orchestrator is intentionally small (~900LOC Go) to keep startup deterministic. It uses a manifest-driven model to allow future per-team tweaks without code changes. - Adaptive shard selection uses path globs and a cached mapping at .ci/cache/shard-map.json which is updated by a periodic job. - Added documentation in docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md and a migration guide docs/dev/dep-hint.md. Related: ENG-4287 (presubmit orchestration), ENG-4290 (ci telemetry), SUP-214 incident notes on flaky presubmits.
Introduces a presubmit orchestrator to centralize hook sequencing, adds a lightweight ci-telemetry exporter for pipeline metrics, and a dependency-hint linter that surfaces unnecessary devdeps. Improves presubmit latency and reduces noise in lint/test pipelines. No runtime API changes.
Liam O'Connor: Nice consolidation. Can we make the telemetry exporter opt-in at org-level? I don't want teams sending extra metrics by default.
Priya Nair: Agree. Added an explicit disable flag and documented the opt-out in docs/dev/ci-presubmit.md.
Maya Singh: dep-hint produced a bunch of false positives for packages that are only referenced by script paths. Can we refine heuristics?
Priya Nair: Refined heuristics to look for common script paths and added a per-path ignore file (.dep-hint-ignore); added tests to cover the cases you saw.
Ethan Park: The presubmit manifest looks good; please ensure the fallback path is resilient in case of panics.

title: compat(openai): partial-dispatch support for streaming tool_choice + graceful fallback and schema alignment
body:
compat(openai): partial-dispatch support for streaming tool_choice + graceful fallback and schema alignment

Context: OpenAI-style tool/function calling remains a major integration point for customer workloads. We observed two recurring issues in the compatibility shim: 1) long-running streaming responses where the model decides on a tool mid-stream (partial tool_choice) produced inconsistent framing and occasionally caused client disconnects; 2) when a tool schema in the compatibility catalog diverged slightly from the model's schema name/shape, the runtime fell back too aggressively to text output, losing structured output semantics. This PR introduces a targeted compatibility layer to make partial tool_choice streaming first-class and to perform tolerant schema alignment during handoff. Summary of changes: - Streaming protocol: emit explicit tool_choice.hint frames and tool_choice.commit frames in the OpenAI-framed event stream so downstream SDKs (TS/Python/Go) can render an in-progress tool invocation UI and then commit when the model decides. Hints are non-terminal and include a suggested tool id + partial args payload (encrypted/hashed if configured). - Fallback semantics: add a new policy 'graceful_invoke_fallback' which, if the selected tool is unavailable or schema-mismatched, continues streaming the tool invocation envelope (function-call style) instead of abruptly switching to plain text. This preserves structured output and allows clients to present a retry UI or queue the invocation. - Schema alignment: introduce schema similarity matching (name aliasing, field-level relaxed matching, and a best-effort mapping layer) at the dispatcher so small mismatches don't force a textual fallback. The mapping is conservative by default and opt-in via the compatibility config. - Backwards compatibility: the new frames are additive and ignored by older clients; we added a registry flag to disable hints for customers who want strict parity. - Tests & CI: unit tests for the dispatcher and decoder, integration test that reproduces the previous regression with partial tool_choice across a streaming boundary, and e2e with the TS SDK to assert the commit frame ordering. Motivation: these changes reduce incidents where user-facing apps lost structured tool call semantics mid-stream and improves developer experience for SDK consumers of the OpenAI compatibility layer. See linked Linear tickets. Checklist: - [x] Implement streaming frames and decoder support - [x] Add dispatcher-side fallback policy - [x] Add schema alignment utilities and docs toggle - [x] Add unit and integration tests - [x] Run CI and iterate on flakiness fixes - [x] Update compatibility docs and SDK adapters Notes: kept the compatibility opt-in for conservative customers and added telemetry events so we can measure invocation vs fallback rates. Rolling this out behind a feature flag in the control plane is planned to minimize blast radius.
Priya Nair: Can we make the hint payload size-bounded to avoid blowing up streaming memory? -> Diego: yes, limited to 4KB by default (configurable).
Jonas Meyer: The schema alignment looks powerful but risky; suggest opt-in and telemetry. -> Diego: added opt-in toggle and telemetry events 'compat.schema_align.attempt'/'compat.schema_align.applied'.
Evelyn Park: CI flakes in the integration test on arm64. -> Diego: added deterministic seeds and a retry wrapper in the test harness; CI stabilized.
Add explicit streaming frames for partial tool selection (tool_choice.hint / tool_choice.commit), a graceful fallback policy to preserve structured tool invocations when exact tool/schema matches are unavailable, and a conservative schema-alignment option behind a compatibility toggle. Opt-in by default; telemetry added.
Unit tests for dispatcher and decoder. Integration test that replays an LLM stream which switches to tool_choice mid-response. E2E with TS SDK asserting UI callback ordering. Load smoke test on staging to verify latency impact.

title: Cohort-aware Progressive Swap Controller for Model Version Lifecycle
body:
Cohort-aware Progressive Swap Controller for Model Version Lifecycle

Context and motivation: Rolling model versions safely at scale requires more than traffic splitting — it requires cohort-based swaps that respect downstream dependencies, per-cohort evaluation windows, and automated rollback when service-level guards fail. This PR introduces the Cohort-aware Progressive Swap Controller (CPSC), a controller in the rollout orchestration layer that performs swap-style rollouts by progressing model versions cohort-by-cohort rather than sample-level splits.

Goals: reduce exposure of regressions, preserve cold-start isolation, enable dependency-aware health checks (datastore schema, adapter compatibility), and provide deterministic swap semantics for auditability.

High-level design:
- Cohorts are lightweight tagged slices of users (by tenant, georegion, or feature flag).
- Swap phases: prepare (warm KV caches, prefetch embeddings), probe (low volume sanity queries), verify (metrics evaluation), promote (full cohort swap), and finalize (rotate canaries out).
- Safety gates: latency p99, error_rate, model-output-divergence against baseline (approx-match), and dependency liveness.
- Rollback: automated hysteresis back-off + dependency trust graph to determine rollback scope (single cohort vs global).
- Integrations: Redwood Model Registry (version pinning), Console UI hooks for cohort rollout visualization, and Linear/Jira links.

- 2 commit: implement probe/promote state machine and dependency checks

title: Evacuation timestamp synchronizer and soft-threshold hedge (hotfix)
body:
Evacuation timestamp synchronizer and soft-threshold hedge (hotfix)

Background: During a regional overload incident we observed two problematic behaviors: (1) concurrent node-level evacuations in the same cohort sometimes used slightly different evacuation timestamps, which allowed a small window where tenant leases were double-counted for eviction heuristics, causing unnecessary churn; (2) the soft-threshold path that should temporarily relax SLO enforcement while preserving KV prefix cache was too aggressive when combined with speculative prefetch, causing higher tail-latency for critical tenants. This PR introduces a lightweight cross-region evacuation timestamp synchronizer (best-effort, clock-drift tolerant) and a hedging mechanism that gates the soft-threshold relaxation when coordinated prefetch is active. The goal is to reduce false-positive evictions and preserve high-priority tenant latency during transient overloads. What this changes: - Introduces EvacTS protocol: a compact lease-synchronization envelope sent during evacuation orchestration that attaches a monotonic evacuation-id + origin-hash and a micro-timestamp (millis). Implemented as best-effort: nodes will accept and reconcile newer evacuation-ids from upstream controllers; older messages are ignored. This avoids races where two controllers start overlapping evacuations with different epoch anchors. - Adds a soft-threshold hedge: the SLO relaxer now consults a lightweight prefetch-state predicate. If prefetch activity for a tenant exceeds a threshold and eviction pressure is marginal, the relaxer defers full soft-mode and instead applies a graded limit (50%-80% of the intended relaxation) to protect tail latency. - Telemetry: emits evac_ts.accepted, evac_ts.rejected (by-staleness), soft_hedge.applied, and soft_hedge.skipped; updated dashboards with example alert queries included in docs/telemetry/playbooks.md - Backwards compatibility: EvacTS is backward-compatible: older nodes ignore unknown fields; controllers will fall back to existing behavior if no evacuationsync ACKs are observed. - Rollout plan: staged rollout to regional controllers (canary region -> 3 additional regions -> global) with a 1-hour observation window per stage. Fix severity: high (incident-driven hotfix). Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for EvacTS reconciliation - [x] Integration test for soft-threshold hedge under simulated prefetch load - [x] Added telemetry and dashboard snippets - [x] Manual canary runs in eu-west-1, eu-central-1 Notes and links: Linear ENG-4482 is the incident follow-up; SUP-1023 tracks a customer-facing symptom. See runbook link: https://linear.redwood.inc/ENG-4482 and dashboard gdoc snippets in docs/telemetry/playbooks.md
Diego Ramos (2026-02-18): Left a couple of nit comments on naming and a question about the reconcile timeout. Suggest using 'evacationEpoch' instead of 'EvacID' for clarity.
Maya Patel (2026-02-18): Reply: kept EvacID but added comment clarifying it's a monotonic epoch token; reconcile timeout is 250ms by default, configurable via controller flags.
Omar Nasser (2026-02-19): Concern: in high-churn regions, accepting remote evac IDs might delay local decisioning. Suggest bounding cross-region acceptance window to 2 seconds.
Maya Patel (2026-02-19): Addressed: implemented upper bound (maxCrossRegionSkewMs = 2000) and added unit test for skewed messages.

title: introduce-ci-dep-pruner-and-stage-aware-lint-orchestrator
body:
introduce-ci-dep-pruner-and-stage-aware-lint-orchestrator

Motivation: Our presubmit lanes have accumulated long-running lint shards and a growing transitive dependency surface that slows feedback and increases CI cost. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: (1) a lightweight Go-based dependency pruner (dep-pruner) run as a pre-merge check that detects and optionally removes unused devdeps/transitive entries from package manifests and (2) a stage-aware lint orchestrator action that re-groups lint shards into fast/medium/slow lanes with an adaptive fastpath for small PRs. Goals: reduce presubmit latency, shrink devdep churn, and provide a safe rollout path for lint reshuffling.
Summary of changes: - tooling: add tools/dep-pruner (Go) with CLI and a minimal heuristics engine (import scan + package-lock cross-check) and CI adapter to auto-suggest PR comments with diffs - actions: add .github/actions/lint-orchestrator (TypeScript) that inspects changed files and classifies lint shards; it can short-circuit slow shards for touch-limited changes - workflows: update .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml to add a new presubmit job "dep-pruner-check" and to wire the lint orchestrator into the lint matrix - docs: docs/contrib/ci-practices.md with developer guidance and rollback steps - helper: scripts/ci/prune-report.sh to surface pruning impact in CI artifacts
Checklist: - [x] dep-pruner CLI implemented with unit tests - [x] lint-orchestrator action implemented and unit-tested - [x] integration tests in CI to validate action gating - [x] rollout plan defined and smoke-tested in canary repos - [x] docs and troubleshooting added
How dep-pruner works (high level): - static import scan across changed packages + cross-validate against package-lock/npm-shrinkwrap - heuristics to avoid pruning packages that appear only in native build steps or dynamic requires - output: a suggested patch (npm ci edit/patch) and a compact report with removed/transitive candidates
Safety and rollout: - initial run mode is detection-only (false-positive rate < 2% in our samples) - auto-fix mode gated behind a Linear approval and only enabled for canary orgs - lint orchestrator respects explicit overrides via .ci/lint-config.yaml - we add a short cooldown (48h) window before auto-fix is allowed to merge
Metrics & results from canary run: - median presubmit time (fast-path) reduced from 4m20s to 2m55s (~32% improvement) - overall presubmit compute (GH runner minutes) down ~18% across canary repos - dep-pruner flagged ~412 devdeps as safe-to-prune across 6 repos (manual triage reduced to 28 auto-fix patches)
Testing: - unit tests cover parsing heuristics and false-positive detection - e2e runs on canary repos with diffed files to ensure lint shards are routed correctly - CI smoke: presubmit.yaml now includes a temporary job to run the pruner in simulation mode on all incoming PRs for 72 hours before enabling baseline gating
Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main in detection-only mode 2) Enable lint orchestrator fastpath for org:canary after 48h 3) Run dep-pruner auto-fix on canary during low-traffic window and ensure rollbacks are available 4) Gradual expansion to 25% of repos, then 100% Related: ENG-2314 (ci presubmit speedups), ENG-2350 (dep hygiene initiative). title: temporal-affinity-refill-and-scavenger-for-paged-kv
body:
temporal-affinity-refill-and-scavenger-for-paged-kv

Summary: Introduces a temporal-affinity driven refill strategy and a light-weight scavenger for the paged KV cache to reduce tail latency in continuous-batching workloads. The change combines a small per-block temporal score, a refill iterator that biases reuse toward recently accessed neighborhoods, and a background scavenger that reclaims cold blocks in low-contention phases.

Motivation: production traces showed frequent cold-evictions followed by immediate re-loads in chat-heavy workloads (p95 token latency spikes during bursty sessions). Existing LRU-like eviction was brittle under small working sets per shard; this PR aims to reduce re-fetch churn and improve p95 latency while keeping allocation fast and allocator lock contention low.

Design:
- Temporal affinity score: each block maintains a u8 score incremented on reuse and decayed on periodic ticks. Score affects refill priority but is cheap to read/write (atomic u8 ops).
- Refill iterator: when a request misses, the allocator first probes the local page neighborhoods ordered by temporal score to prefer reuse of recently-warmed blocks (improves KV cache hit-locality for streaming sessions).
- Scavenger thread: a low-priority background worker scans age-buckets and coalesces contiguous cold blocks for efficient reclamation. It only runs when heap pressure is below a configurable threshold to avoid interfering with latency-sensitive fast-paths.
- Fast-path admit/evict: a non-blocking admit path reserves a hot-slot for short windows to avoid ABA churn when multiple fibers are refilling the same keys. Contention fallback uses a short spin-and-yield policy.

Compatibility: no changes to on-disk layout or RPCs; config knobs exposed via runtime flags for decay interval and scavenger thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] Design doc (ENG-1987) and bench plan (ENG-2045)
- [x] Unit tests for refill iterator determinism
- [x] Stress test under continuous-batching harness
- [x] Benchmarks added and stable
- [x] Docs notes describing knobs and migration considerations

Testing and results:
- Unit and integration tests: all passing locally and in CI.
- Benchmarks (kv_batch_bench): p95 generation latency reduced by 18% on a 4-GPU dedicated worker under synthetic chat sessions with 60s bursts. Tail behavior improved: p99 reduced by ~12%.
- Memory churn: observed working set re-loads reduced by ~22% in flamegraphs; CPU overhead of scavenger measured at <1% on average.

Risks and mitigations:
- Increased metadata (per-block score): limited to +1 byte per block; accounted for in allocator sizing.
- Scavenger interfering with latency: runs only when allocator free-pages > threshold and its work budget is capped per tick.
- Contention on fast-path: fallback path in allocator uses adaptive backoff.

Commits: see commit list above.

Changed areas (high-level):
- src/kv/paged_cache.rs: adds temporal score field, refill iterator, and a small API for score bump/decay.
- src/kv/allocator.rs: fast-path admit/evict reservation logic and contention fallback.
- src/kv/scavenger.rs: new lightweight background worker and config.
- bench/kv_batch_bench.rs: synthetic harness to reproduce bursty chat sessions and measure p95/p99.
- tests/kv_refill_test.rs: deterministic scenarios for refill and eviction ordering.
- docs/notes/kv-refill.md: operational guidance and recommended knob values.

Review conversation (high level):
- Miguel Santos: "Nice approach; can we avoid extra cacheline bloat when score is unused?" Author: "We colocate the u8 into the block header and pad minimally; added microbench showing negligible throughput impact."
- Ethan Park: "How does this interact with cross-shard routing?" Author: "Refill iterator is per-shard and doesn't change routing semantics; added a test for cross-shard misses."
- Lena Hoffman: "CI benchmark variability showed one flaky run at 2am; re-run fixed it. Please add a guard in bench to retry transient net errors." Author: "Added retry and tightened benchmark harness determinism."

CI:
- Unit tests: pass
- Lint: pass
- Integration stress: pass
- Bench: stable across 5 runs (added retry)

Merge: Approved by Miguel and Ethan, merged via squash on main on 2026-02-23.

Release notes: "Paged KV: Add temporal-affinity reuse and a background scavenger to reduce re-load churn and improve tail latency for bursty streaming workloads. Config knobs available: kv.refill_decay_interval, kv.scavenger_min_free_pages."

Next steps:
- Monitor p99 in-prod for initial rollout and tune decay interval per region.
- Follow-up PR to expose per-tenant knobs and telemetry for temporal score distributions.

title: introduce-kms-sidecar-policy-enforcer-and-audit-attenuator

introduce-kms-sidecar-policy-enforcer-and-audit-attenuator

title: Introduce session-windowed latency sketches and invocation replaybench
body:
Introduce session-windowed latency sketches and invocation replaybench

Motivation: token-level and per-invocation metrics currently provide high-cardinality point traces that make it hard to understand session-level latency behavior (bursty tails, intra-session skew) without expensive trace rehydration. This PR adds compact, session-windowed latency sketches and a small invocation replaybench to synthesize representative token sequences for validation and alert tuning.

Goal: give SREs and platform engineers a low-cost, queryable summary of per-session latency distributions and a reproducible synthetic generator to exercise hot paths for alert calibration and dashboarding. This supports automated alert dampening and more robust long-tail detection without blowing up storage or cardinality.

What's included (summary):
- New runtime sketch collector: compact reservoir-backed, time-windowed latency sketches keyed by (tenant, route, session_id window). Sketches are optimized for low-allocation hot paths and expose percentiles + tail-mass estimates.
- Replaybench CLI + Python harness: generates synthetic invocations (token timing, token sizes, kv-cache states) from historical traces or randomized shingled bootstraps to validate SLOs and CI jobs.
- Minor server-side ingestion path: lightweight proto for session-sketch telemetry and conversion to rollups stored in the metrics pipeline.
- Grafana dashboard and alert rule examples: session-latency-overview dashboard with cohorting controls and a new alert template that uses session sketch tails for alerting instead of raw p95/p99 spikes.
- Tests: unit tests for sketch ingestion + deterministic replaybench integration tests.
- Docs: observability guide for using sketches + replaybench and recommended alert thresholds.

Checklist:
- [x] API for runtime to emit sketches with minimal allocations
- [x] Backfill connector: best-effort adapter to convert 24h of sampled traces into sketches (used for initial seeding)
- [x] Replaybench integration in CI (sanity only)
- [x] Dashboards + alert rule RFC example
- [x] Performance microbench: <5% added p50 CPU on the metrics emitter in high-throughput path

Implementation notes:
- The sketch uses a bounded reservoir with exponential decay for recency weighting and a separate compact q-digest to summarize tail mass. This lets us cheaply answer p50/p90/p95/p99 and estimate the % of tokens above a configurable latency bucket.
- Session windows are configurable: default 60s tumbling windows, configurable per-route. We attach a small 16-byte session window ID hash to metrics to keep cardinality modest.
- The replaybench emits sequences with token inter-arrival times and token lengths; the harness can replay against both the runtime (via a local loopback) and the sampling ingest path to validate histogram/sketch consistency.

Commits (high level):
- feat(telemetry): add session_sketch runtime collector and proto definitions
- feat(replaybench): initial replaybench CLI + python harness
- perf(telemetry): optimize sketch allocation hot path, add pooling and pre-sized buckets
- infra(metrics): add conversion adapter for historical trace -> sketch backfill tool
- docs(observability): session-latency guide + dashboard JSON
- test: deterministic replaybench integration test + unit tests for q-digest impl

Files changed (high level):
- src/telemetry/sketches/session_sketch.go
- proto/telemetry/session_sketch.proto
- tools/replaybench/README.md
- tools/replaybench/harness.py
- dashboards/session_latency_replay.json
- metrics/backfill/trace_to_sketch.go
- tests/telemetry/test_session_sketch.go
- tests/replaybench/test_replaybench.py
- docs/observability/session-latency.md

Review conversation (abridged):
- Ava Patel: "Nice direction — can we bound worst-case cardinality? The 16-byte hash is fine but let's add explicit eviction policies per-tenant."
  - Priya: "Added eviction policy (LRU with max windows per tenant) and a config knob; updated docs with knobs and recommended limits."
- Diego Morales: "Sketch design looks good; can we get an integration microbenchmark against high-throughput emitter?"
  - Priya: "Included microbench results under perf/benchmarks/session_sketch.md and reduced allocations by pooling; added automated perf run to CI (sanity only)."
- Sofia Chen: "Alerting change is significant; ops will need guidance on threshold calibration to avoid alert storms."
  - Priya: "Included replaybench presets that map historical cohort percentiles to suggested thresholds and a small RFC section in docs."

CI and checks:

- integration (sanity): pass (deterministic replay run against snapshot)

- perf microbench: pass (regression <5% CPU p50 on emitter)

Release notes:

Backward compatibility and migration:

title: heterogeneous-attention-fusion-with-staged-scheduler-and-continuous-batching-support
body:
heterogeneous-attention-fusion-with-staged-scheduler-and-continuous-batching-support

Motivation: reduce p99 latency regression for mixed-sequence workloads and improve throughput for production chat and retrieval runtimes by selecting optimal attention kernels at runtime and enabling continuous batching without sacrificing KV cache hit stability. Changes: Introduces a heterogeneous attention selection layer (HeteroAttn) that picks between a low-latency microkernel and a high-throughput Flash-like kernel based on sequence length heuristics and current queueing pressure; adds a staged scheduler that enforces a short-term reservation window for latency-sensitive requests and a batch-aggregation window for throughput requests; implements a cooperative KV cache eviction policy (staged LRU) that works with continuous batching to avoid repeated cache thrash during rollups; adds fused rotary/rope offset precomputation paths that avoid memcpy for common rotary patterns; integrates fp16 accumulation path with optional fp32 fallback for edge-case stability; exposes runtime knobs: ATTEN_SELECT_WINDOW_MS, KV_STAGED_WINDOW, CBATCH_MAX_WAIT_MS for tuned rollouts. Testing and validation: microbenchmarked on c6i-gpu clusters and internal perf-lab; added synthetic mixed-sequence workload harness and end-to-end chat replay traces. Results: median latency improved 6-9% on mid-sized seqs, p99 reduced up to 22% for mixed workloads, throughput increased 12% on long-sequence tails while KV miss rate decreased 18% under continuous batching. Rollout plan: staged canary on dedicated pool alpha -> 50% traffic after 72h, automatic rollback on p99 regressions >10% or error rate increase >0.5%. Backwards compatibility: no API changes. Known limitations: rare fp16 accumulation differences at extreme sequence lengths (documented and guarded by runtime flag), scheduler parameters tuned for our standard clusters; customers on small on-prem may require adjustments. Checklist: - [x] Benchmarks added to perf-lab harness - [x] Unit + integration tests for scheduler and KV policy - [x] Feature-flagged rollout - [x] Docs entry in runtime tuning guide - [x] Telemetry events for selection decisions
Ethan Park: Overall this looks good; two questions: 1) how stable is the fp16 accumulation path on long sequences? 2) we need a clearer metric in telemetry for selection reversions.
Maya Singh (author): FP16 path has guard to fall back to fp32 when accumulation overflow detected; unit test added for 32k token synthetic to assert no NaNs. Added selection_reversion_count metric and exposed in selection_events.
Sofia Ramirez: Could you add a small note in the docs about recommended KV_STAGED_WINDOW for Dedicated vs Hosted? Length of default felt tuned for large pools.
Maya Singh: Added docs entry and example per-cluster recommendation; default remains conservative and can be overridden per deployment.
Liam O'Connor: CI flake on cuda11.8 matrix, reran and passed; good to squash merge once e2e looks green.
Introduces heterogeneous attention kernel selection with staged scheduler and continuous batching support. Improves p99 and throughput for mixed-sequence workloads. Feature-flagged; not a public API change. See docs/runtime/tuning/hetero_attn.md for tuning guidance.

title: runtime: hybrid kernel fallback with KV-consistency gating and safe-mode thresholds
body:
runtime: hybrid kernel fallback with KV-consistency gating and safe-mode thresholds

Motivation: intermittent correctness regressions and rare kernel assertion OOMs during long-sequence continuous-batching workloads were being handled by an all-or-nothing safe-mode that fell back to FP32 CPU execution. That approach eliminated correctness incidents but caused large tail latency and cost spikes. This PR implements a hybrid fallback that trades small latency regressions for correctness while keeping most requests on the fast GPU path.

What this change does (single-line summary): Adds a gate that triggers a controlled fallback to compatible kernels (FP32 or CPU) when a set of runtime signals indicate likely correctness risk: KV cache checksum mismatch, kernel assert counter > threshold, or per-request token-level divergence above configured tolerance. The gate is conservative by default and behind a feature flag `hybrid_kernel_fallback` set to off in main; rollout configuration and safe defaults are included.

Key components in the diff (high-level):
- runtime/fallback/hybrid_gate.cc/h: new gate logic that aggregates signals, applies hysteresis and cooldown windows.
- runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.cc: exposes compatibility metadata and fallback candidates per model artifact.
- runtime/kv/consistency_checker.cc: lightweight KV prefix checksum hooks and sample counters.
- scheduler/continuous_batching_manager.cc: emits per-batch KV stability stats and integrates cooldown decisions.
- observability/metrics.yaml: new metrics: fallback_rate, kv_inconsistency_count, fallback_cooldown_seconds, fallback_latency_penalty.
- integration tests: tests/runtime/hybrid_fallback_integration_test.py: e2e scenarios with long sequences and simulated kernel asserts.
- docs/operational/fallbacks.md: rollout and runbook updates.

Commits (summary):
- 1/6 Add gate primitives and API for aggregated signals
- 2/6 Implement KV checksum sampler and lightweight counter
- 3/6 Hook gate into continuous batching manager and kernel selector
- 4/6 Add metrics and dashboards for visibility
- 5/6 E2E tests and deterministic replay harness
- 6/6 Docs and feature-flagging + rollout config

Testing and CI: Unit tests for gate logic and KV sampler were added. E2E integration tests were flaky at first due to nondeterministic replaying of kernel asserts; added deterministic random seeds and a 'test-only' bypass for timing. CI pipeline initially failed 2 runs on integration tests; failures traced to timing races in the test harness and fixed in commit 5. Final CI status: pass (build + unit + integration + lint).

Perf and correctness numbers from canary (10% traffic in staging for 48h):
- Correctness incident rate: down 93% (from 15 incidents to 1)
- Overall median latency: +0.8% (insignificant)
- 95th percentile latency: +8% (due to fallback tail) — mitigations: cooldown and batching-aware fallback reduce this in subsequent rollouts
- Token-level divergence (regression tests): eliminated for sampled workloads
- Unit-cost impact: +4% at 10% traffic; expected to be neutral at scale with further tuning of thresholds

Rollout plan: feature-flag off in main. Canary -> 10% for 48h (done) -> 50% for 72h (monitor fallback_rate and fallback_latency_penalty) -> 100% if no regression. Alert thresholds added: fallback_rate > 0.5% sustained triggers on-call, fallback_latency_penalty > 15% triggers rollback.

Back-and-forth in review (high level):
- Miguel Alvarez: requested stronger telemetry (per-model fallback_rate) and a new metric for 'fallback_reason' tag. Author: added per-model tags and expanded runbook.
- Sofia Chen: flagged potential double-accounting of KV checks when multiple batches mutate same KV; requested a cooldown hysteresis change from 30s->60s. Author: implemented 60s default but left param configurable.
- Derek Wong: requested an e2e test that simulates rapid switchback scenarios; author added an additional integration test and a 'no switchback' policy toggle.

Author notes and rationale: We prefer a conservative hybrid approach that preserves correctness without wholesale safe-mode fallbacks. The gate aggregates cheap signals that are already collected or cost <1% of request time. The tuning parameters (checksum sample rate, hysteresis windows, divergence tolerance) are exposed and documented. The default behavior offline is to be conservative; operators can enable a more aggressive mode for lower cost at their own risk.

Files changed count: 12. Notable small snippets included in runtime/kernels/kernel_selector.cc to avoid breaking ABI; kernel metadata additions are backward compatible. Integration tests added are deterministic and run in CI with fixed seeds.

Merge and deploy: Approved by reviewers after two rounds of changes. Merged via squash on 2026-02-22. Feature flagged off by default; ops aware via runbook and dashboard. Follow-ups: a follow-up PR will add automatic threshold tuning based on workload profiles (ENG-5410).

Related tickets: ENG-5321 (primary), ENG-5410 (follow-up auto-tuning), SUP-1983 (Customer-reported KV divergence incidents).
Introduces hybrid kernel fallback gating based on KV cache consistency and runtime error signals. Feature-flagged; rollout plan 10%->50%->100%. Adds observability metrics and alert thresholds.

title: proactive KV priming and decode-slip adjuster to reduce tail latency
body:
proactive KV priming and decode-slip adjuster to reduce tail latency

Motivation: reduce 95th/99th token latency caused by late KV cache population and stage slip (variable prefill->decode handover). This PR implements a predictive, lightweight KV priming path plus a decode-slip adjuster that dynamically shifts decode scheduling windows to absorb jitter between prefill micro-batches and decode slices. Key ideas: 1) small, speculative KV priming requests for hot key prefixes predicted from client routing heuristics and recent sequence templates; 2) micro-merge of adjacent KV priming fragments to reduce request spikes when multiple tiny prefill segments target nearby KV pages; 3) decode-slip adjuster that measures micro-latency drift and advances or delays decode worker wakeups to reduce stall probability; 4) runtime toggle flags to enable/disable priming per model/profile and conservative fallbacks to existing prefill pipeline. This avoids wholesale rework of prefill/decode handoff while gaining measurable tail improvements.
Miguel Santos: Nice approach — can you clarify predictor warmup cost? If priming causes net extra GPU work we'll lose overall throughput.
Asha Kapoor: Predictor is intentionally conservative; it first runs on small hashed prefix sketch (cost <1% CPU) and only enqueues priming when predicted confidence > 0.6. Priming uses lightweight 'kv-read-ahead' which hits the cache layer, not the model kernels, so GPU work is unchanged.
Claire Huang: Tests look good. Please add a guard for models with very short contexts (seq_len <= 32) to avoid noisy priming.
Asha Kapoor: Added short-context guard and unit test (see last commit).
Jon Park: Micro-merge window default seems tight for various workloads. Did you benchmark different window sizes?
Asha Kapoor: Yes — bench_kv_priming captures 2ms, 5ms, 10ms merge windows. Default set to 5ms after experiments (see benchmark_summary).
Workload: 70/30 mix of short (avg 64 tokens) and medium (avg 256 tokens) requests from production trace PRD-2025-09
Baseline (no priming, main scheduler): p95 token latency = 112ms, p99 = 204ms
With KV priming + slip adjuster (default config): p95 token latency = 88ms (-21%), p99 = 156ms (-23%), tail-stall events (stalls > 250ms) reduced by 62%
CPU overhead: +0.8% on control-plane worker nodes; memory: negligible for priming queue (bounded to 512 entries per instance)
Throughput: steady-state tokens/sec unchanged within noise (±1.5%), small improvement under bursty arrivals due to fewer re-schedules
Sensitivity: micro-merge window 2ms reduces p99 by ~18% but increases small number of extra priming requests; 10ms window gives marginal extra benefit at cost of additional priming hits (~+6%)
New feature is gated behind runtime config: runtime.features.kv_priming.enabled (default on for staged rollout).
Per-model override: model.config.priming_policy = {off|conservative|aggressive}. Conservative is default in our rollout.
Metrics to watch: kv.priming.predicted, kv.priming.enqueued, kv.priming.hit, scheduler.slip.shift, runtime.prefill.decode_stall_count
If tail regressions observed disable runtime.features.kv_priming.enabled or set per-model to off; rollback safe as priming path is orthogonal to core KV policy.
Introduces predictive KV priming and a decode-slip adjuster to reduce tail token latency. Default gated rollout with per-model controls. Improves p95/p99 in mixed short/medium workloads; watch kv.priming.* and scheduler.slip.* metrics.

title: Introduce SLO Tenor and Sticky Restore Conductor for safer regional restores
body:
Introduce SLO Tenor and Sticky Restore Conductor for safer regional restores

Context: Recent incidents showed oscillating regional restores where immediate reopen of circuits and aggressive rejoin caused repeat SLO violations. This PR introduces a new SLO Tenor concept (time-based soft window) plus a Sticky Restore Conductor to coordinate regional restores and reduce flapping. Goals: 1) reduce restore-induced SLO spikes by introducing a configurable tenor window that delays aggressive reconnection and reheats KV-preserve policies; 2) provide a sticky restore conductor that centralizes decisioning for per-region restores, with telemetry hooks for post-restore analysis; 3) add a deferred probe hedging mechanism to avoid simultaneous heavy probe storms during restores; 4) safe rollout with feature flag, metrics, and rollback path. Changeset summary: high-level design + implementation and tests. Checklist: [x] design doc (ENG-4821) updated; [x] unit + integration tests added; [x] telemetry + dashboards added; [x] feature-flagged behind slo_tenor.enable; [x] rollout plan and rollback notes included. How it works: SLO Tenor: a tunable duration attached to region-level restores that enforces a soft backoff before allowing full traffic rejoin; the conductor keeps a per-region state (sticky) that remembers last-restore epoch and prevents reopens within tenor unless explicit override; deferred probe hedge: when a restore is started, short randomized probe delays and gentle probe pacing are applied to avoid synchronized load on warm caches. Rollout plan: canary in us-east-1 with slo_tenor.enable=true and default tenor=60s; monitor 95/99 latency and token cost; after 72h expand across regions. Rollback: slo_tenor.enable=false or set tenor=0. Related: ties into SRE runbooks for regional failovers (SUP-9821).

title: ephemeral-health-gate: cohort-based quiet-window and auto-resolve for circuit stability
body:
ephemeral-health-gate: cohort-based quiet-window and auto-resolve for circuit stability

Motivation: We continue to see noisy circuit flips in islanded regions during transient backend blips which cause rapid reopen/close churn and SLO spikes for tail latency. This churn also propagates to downstream routing decisions and makes capacity autoscalers overreact. This PR introduces an ephemeral health gate that groups circuits into lightweight cohorts and applies a short consensus quiet-window before allowing reopen transitions. The feature is guarded behind a runtime flag (default: off) and is intended for staged rollouts to Dedicated/Private deployments.

What this changes: 1) cohort builder: lightweight hashing that groups circuits by region+model+capacity-class so that short-lived flaps are evaluated at cohort level instead of per-circuit. 2) consensus quiet-window: when a circuit transitions to open, reopening requires a quorum of cohort members to report healthy for a configurable quiet_window_ms to avoid single-node noisy reopen. 3) soft-lease on circuits: reopened circuits obtain a soft-lease which decays if the cohort health remains marginal — this prevents immediate re-eviction storm. 4) autosolve flow: a periodic reconciler reevaluates cohort health and will progressively restore circuits in small batches if conditions are met. 5) metrics + debugging: new metrics (cohort_health_score, cohort_quiet_window_hits, cohort_reopen_batches) and a console dashboard JSON to visualize cohort state and recent quiet-window events. 6) hotfix: fixes a race in circuit snapshot restore where metrics timestamps could be nil causing occasional panics during node restart.

Rollout plan: gated behind feature flag redwood.experimental.ephemeral_health_gate; staged canary in eu-west-1 on Dedicated for 48h, promote to remaining Dedicated clusters if cohort_health_score stays > 0.95 and no SLO regressions observed. If increased reopen churn is detected, the reconciler supports auto-rollback.

Compatibility and config: default behavior does not alter existing circuit semantics unless the flag is enabled. Config knobs added to runtime/config: cohort_size_hint, quiet_window_ms, reopen_quorum_pct, soft_lease_ms, and batch_restore_size.

Testing: added unit tests for consensus math and cohort builder, integration test simulating transient flaps and verifying cohort-level damping, and a canary script used during manual rollout.

Related: addresses recurring incidents documented in SUP-321 and complements ENG-1543 (staged fallback orchestrator).
Anjali Kapoor requested changes: please add detailed unit tests for quorum edge-cases and document behavior when cohort size is 1 (we should fall back to legacy semantics).
Author reply (Diego Martinez): added quorum edge tests and explicit single-member fallback; left note in docs and unit tests.

title: Reduce CI costs with test-slicing, sparse-checkout and dependency-minimizer
body:
Reduce CI costs with test-slicing, sparse-checkout and dependency-minimizer

Motivation: CI costs and queue times have grown with the test matrix and the monorepo size. This PR introduces three coordinated changes to reduce CI runtime and cache pressure: (1) test-slicing: split integration/unit suites into deterministic shards by changed modules, (2) sparse-checkout in CI runners to limit workspace files downloaded for each job, and (3) dep-minimizer: a lightweight analysis tool that prunes unrelated dependency versions from the effective dependency set used for install caches.

Summary of changes: Added a test-slicing executor (tools/test-slicer) with heuristics for affected-package detection and deterministic shard assignment. Updated .github/workflows/ci.yml to run lightweight changed-file detection as a short-circuit step and only spin up full runners when needed. Integrated sparse-checkout logic into the checkout step to reduce workspace size for long tests. Added infra/dep-minimizer which analyzes lockfiles and module imports to produce a reduced lock overlay used only for CI, keeping production lockfiles untouched.

Why this is safe: All changes are opt-in and guarded by repository config flags (ci.test_slicing.enabled, ci.sparse_checkout.enabled, ci.dep_minimizer.enabled). The dep-minimizer outputs a diagnostics report and cannot be enabled unless a repo admin flips the flag. Test-slicing preserves global test order determinism by seeding shard assignment with repository-wide salt and PR number.

Testing and CI: Local unit tests for the test-slicer and dep-minimizer are included. The workflow contains a smoke job that runs a full-suite against a preserved baseline when the config is changed. In this PR the smoke job was run twice against main and head to validate parity. CI run summary appears in checks_summary.

Compatibility notes: No library API changes. Developers will notice faster pre-merge feedback and smaller checkout times in CI. Teams that rely on full workspace integration tests should opt into slicing gradually; docs/ci/onboarding.md includes migration steps and troubleshooting.

Checklist: - [x] Adds test-slicing implementation and unit tests - [x] Adds dep-minimizer implementation and unit tests - [x] Adds sparse-checkout integration into CI - [x] Feature flags and safe defaults - [x] Migration docs and rollout plan in docs/ci/onboarding.md

Rollout plan: 1) Merge opt-in feature flags and tools; 2) Enable per-team via repo config for low-risk services; 3) Monitor per-route latency and CI cache hit-rate for 2 weeks; 4) Gradually enable wider.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of affected-file detection and shard determinism (see tools/test-slicer/README.md). dep-minimizer intentionally avoids rewriting production lockfiles; verify the overlay generation and diagnostics in infra/dep-minimizer/README.md.
