title: Introduce bandwidth provisioning floor and graceful surge compactor
body:
Introduce bandwidth provisioning floor and graceful surge compactor

Motivation: large tenants on Dedicated occasionally produce short high-throughput spikes that exhaust ephemeral headroom and cause downstream tail latency spikes. Existing burst token models and warm pools reduce long tail events but are either too coarse or slow to react for sub-30s surges. This PR introduces two orthogonal controls: (1) a configurable bandwidth provisioning floor that guarantees a minimal steady reservation per pool, and (2) a graceful 'surge compactor' daemon that temporarily compacts short-lived requests into a pacing envelope to avoid immediate allocation churn.

What this PR does: Implements a bandwidth_floor allocator that reserves a minimal baseline of GPU/slot tokens per tenant pool scaled by historical 50th-percentile throughput. Adds surge_compactor that intercepts short bursts (default 15s window) and paces allocations with a best-effort compaction ratio to preserve latency SLOs while avoiding over-committing transient capacity. Exposes configs: dedicated.config.bandwidth_floor.{enabled,fraction,min_tokens} and autoscaler.compactor.{enabled,window_secs,max_compact_ratio}.

Design notes: - Floor is additive to existing reservation logic and is applied during provisioning and refill cycles so it does not permanently increase cluster target size; it acts as a soft floor with decay. - Compactor acts inline in the allocation pipeline; it only delays and batches ephemeral requests rather than rejecting them. It emits decision telemetry for later tuning. - Both components are opt-in and default to off for safety.

Telemetry & observability: - New metrics: dedicated.bandwidth_floor.tokens_reserved, autoscaler.compactor.compaction_ratio, autoscaler.compactor.suppressed_requests, dedicated.pool.floor_decay_events. - Dashboards: added a compacting vs direct-allocation split on the Dedicated allocation dashboard. - Traces: compactor decision path annotated for p99 investigation.

Testing & validation: unit tests for allocator math, e2e regression harness that simulates 10–200 concurrent short bursts, and canary in 'staging-dedicated' with synthetic traffic generator. Load testing shows a 42% reduction in ephemeral headroom churn and median latency unchanged; 95th p99 improved under high microburst scenarios by ~8%.

Rollout plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag; configs default to disabled. 2) Enable floor in staging on a single tenant pool and observe headroom/latency metrics for 48h. 3) Enable compactor in canary with max_compact_ratio=0.5, monitor suppressed_requests and SLOs for 72h. 4) Gradually increase coverage and compile a tuning recipe for common workloads.

Compatibility & migration: No migration required. All changes are feature-flagged and backward compatible. If compactor causes unexpected behavior it can be fully disabled at runtime.

Security & perf considerations: Compactor is CPU-light but touches allocation hot-path; microbenchmarks show <2% added latency to allocation tail in no-op mode. We instrumented token accounting to ensure no double-counting of reservations.

Files changed: see list below.

- [x] E2E load test scenario and results attached
- [x] Telemetry + dashboard tiles added

title: staged-multi-arm-traffic-reconciler-with-timestamped-cohort-leases
body:
staged-multi-arm-traffic-reconciler-with-timestamped-cohort-leases

Summary: Introduces a staged multi-arm traffic reconciler that coordinates timed cohort leases and deterministic reconciliation to support multi-variant canaries, A/B experiments, and shadow-to-canary promotions with safe automatic rollback windows. Motivation: Current rollout controller optimizes single-path canaries but struggles when multiple concurrent arms (A/B/n) need coordinated swaps, timed lease expiry, and deterministic conflict resolution across regions and Dedicated clusters. This PR implements a lease-based temporal reconciler that: 1) assigns timestamped leases to cohort partitions, 2) uses a conflict-free reconciliation loop to avoid oscillation when multiple controllers observe different states, 3) provides a promotion API for shadow arms to be fast-swapped into serving lanes when metric gates pass, and 4) exposes fine-grained probe hooks for safety gates and automatic rollback triggers. Design highlights: - Lease model: cohorts receive monotonic timestamped leases (lease_id + expiry_ts). A reconciler accepts an action only when local time < expiry_ts and lease origin matches expected coordinator. - Deterministic reconciliation: deterministic tie-breaker (lease_id + origin priority) prevents flip-flop across regions when controller heartbeats cross. - Multi-arm state machine: supports an arbitrary number of arms, tracks per-arm telemetry windows, and allows staged promotion where arm B can be promoted to 30% then 60% with automatic safety holdpoints. - Shadow promotion: a shadow arm can be promoted into live traffic via promoteShadow API; traffic migrates through an atomic staged plan that respects session affinity and KV-cache compatibility checks. - Rollback orchestration: rollback plans are checkpointed; a heuristic auto-rollback triggers on SLO/mortality gates with a configurable grace window and therapeutical cool-down to avoid thrashing. Backwards compatibility: - Controller exposes a feature flag rollout.v2.multiaarm=false for gradual enablement. - Existing single-arm canaries remain on the legacy controller unless the flag is enabled for a rollout. Files changed (high-level): - pkg/rollout/reconciler.go: new reconciler core and lease reconciliation primitives. - pkg/rollout/lease_store.go: in-memory + persistent lease store adapters (etcd-backed adapter stubbed for testing). - api/v1/rollout.proto: adds MultiArmPlan, LeaseRef, PromoteShadow RPC. - internal/telemetry/metrics.go: adds arms_active, arm_promotion_latency, lease_conflicts_total. - console/src/components/RolloutTimeline.tsx: UI for multi-arm timelines and lease status overlays. - e2e/tests/multiarm_rollout.spec.ts: end-to-end scenarios including failover and auto-rollback. - docker/dev/rollout-integration.Dockerfile: lightweight image used by CI integration. Tests and validation: - Unit tests: comprehensive unit coverage for reconciler state transitions and tie-breaker determinism. - Integration tests: e2e scenarios emulate cross-region controller heartbeats with adjustable clock skew to validate deterministic outcomes. - Load tests: lightweight perf bench shows <3% overhead on control plane CPU at 10k rollouts/min. Migration and rollout plan: - Feature-gated behind rollout.v2.multiaarm. - Canary rollout to internal teams for 2 weeks; monitor arm_promotion_latency and lease_conflicts_total. - If lease_conflicts_total spikes >5% for 10m, automatic rollback to legacy controller (operational playbook included). Operational docs and runbook: - Added runbook section in docs/rollouts/multiarm-runbook.md explaining investigation steps, key metrics, and emergency disable flags. - Console changes include a lease inspector panel and hazard indicators when a plan exceeds staged time windows. Checklist: - [x] Core reconciler implementation - [x] Proto and API changes with backwards-compat stubs - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Console visualization and operator controls - [x] Runbook and migration notes - [x] Benchmarks and CI passing Known limitations: - Etcd-backed lease store adapter is stubbed; production adapter will be wired in a follow-up (ENG-10014) to avoid coupling with this PR. - KV-cache compatibility checks rely on a per-model capability vector that will be expanded in the model-registry follow-up. Related work: ENG-9821 (multi-arm rollout design doc), ENG-10014 (persistent lease-store integration). Release notes: Implements multi-arm staged traffic reconciler with timestamped cohort leases, shadow promotion API, and automatic rollback orchestration. Backwards-incompatible changes: none (feature gated).

title: Auto-stop/rollback canary rollouts on SLO breach (Hosted)
body:
Auto-stop/rollback canary rollouts on SLO breach (Hosted)

Context
We’re adding GA-grade safety mechanisms to Hosted canary rollouts: if the canary cohort regresses on key SLO signals, automatically stop the rollout and either pause or rollback depending on policy. This PR wires stop-condition evaluation into the rollout orchestrator loop and adds notification hooks so customers + on-call can see what happened.

What’s included
- Stop condition evaluation service (server-side) that continuously evaluates cohort metrics for the current step and emits a decision: CONTINUE | PAUSE | ROLLBACK.
- Policy-driven thresholds (initial defaults) for:
  - 5xx rate regression (absolute + relative)
  - timeout rate regression
  - p95 latency regression
- Minimum sample / warmup guardrails to avoid flapping on low traffic:
  - min_requests_per_cohort
  - min_eval_window_seconds
- Orchestrator integration:
  - Runs evaluator periodically while a step is in SOAKING state
  - On breach: transitions rollout state, persists reason, emits activity timeline event
  - Rollback path sets traffic split to baseline=100%, canary=0% and marks rollout ROLLED_BACK
  - Pause path freezes split at current % and marks step PAUSED
- Notifications:
  - Console event stream: `rollout.auto_paused` / `rollout.auto_rolled_back` with structured reason payload
  - PagerDuty routing via existing SRE notifier (gated to beta tenants; see notes)
  - Email/webhook fanout via control-plane notification bus (best-effort)
- Telemetry:
  - Metrics for evaluation duration, evaluation errors, and number of auto-pauses/rollbacks by tenant/route
  - Adds a “stop_condition” tag (bounded enum) for rollouts events (no high-cardinality rollout_id in metrics; rollout_id remains in logs)

Out of scope
- Quality gates as hard blockers (we allow optional manual quality signals but no automated eval integration here)
- Dedicated/Private wiring (schema is shared; enforcement is Hosted-only)

Implementation notes
- Evaluator queries cohort aggregates from telemetry service (ENG-9152) using a fixed set of dimensions (tenant_id, route_id, cohort, region). For this PR, evaluation is done per-region, then combined using a conservative rule: if any region breaches, trigger action.
- Threshold semantics:
  - latency_p95_regression: triggers when canary_p95 > baseline_p95 * (1 + relative_regression) AND canary_p95 > baseline_p95 + absolute_ms
  - error_rate_5xx_regression: triggers when canary_5xx_rate > baseline_5xx_rate + absolute_pp OR canary_5xx_rate > baseline_5xx_rate * (1 + relative_regression)
  - timeout_rate_regression: same structure as 5xx
- State machine changes are additive and backwards compatible: stop-condition actions only apply to steps with `stop_conditions` configured; otherwise behavior is unchanged.

Testing
- Unit tests for threshold comparisons and min-sample logic
- Orchestrator state machine tests:
  - SOAKING -> AUTO_PAUSED
  - SOAKING -> AUTO_ROLLED_BACK
  - No action when below min sample/window
- Integration test in staging (manual) using synthetic error injection in canary cohort

Rollout / risk
- Feature-flagged behind `hosted_canary_auto_stop_enabled` (default off) and only enabled for beta tenants.
- PagerDuty alerting is additionally gated behind `hosted_canary_auto_stop_paging_enabled` to avoid beta alert storms.

Follow-ups
- Add evaluation timeout handling + retries (currently evaluator returns an error and we keep soaking; will tighten before GA)
- Expose stop-condition configuration UI in Console wizard (currently API-only; Console shows read-only reason/events)

Refs
- Linear: ENG-9158
- Related PRs: pr-28788 (orchestrator), pr-28819 (cohort tagging), pr-28910 (dashboards/templates)
- Runbook draft: confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/runbook-rollout-stuck-or-bad-split

title: Add top-k tail-risk canary detector + adaptive quorum rollout guard
body:
Add top-k tail-risk canary detector + adaptive quorum rollout guard

Context and motivation: We have recurring incidents where small fractions of traffic exhibit severe tail latency (p99.99+) after model or runtime changes. Existing detectors (percentile fusion, temporal cohorts) flag broad regressions but often miss concentrated tail risk that affects a tiny slice yet can cause downstream failures. This PR introduces a Top-K Tail-Risk detector that explicitly measures concentrated extreme latency events across stratified traffic slices and an adaptive quorum rollout guard that requires a configurable fraction of slices to agree on degradation before blocking a rollout.

What this change does: Implements a probabilistic tail-risk scoring algorithm (inspired by EVT-style peak-over-threshold combined with Top-K frequency aggregation) that: 1) computes per-slice extreme-event counts over time windows, 2) normalizes by baseline traffic to surface concentrated bursts, and 3) produces a confidence score and suggested mitigation severity. The adaptive quorum guard consumes these signals and enforces policy rules in the rollout controller: quorum policies are configurable by SLO weight, minimum-slice coverage, and hysteresis cooldown.

Why this approach: Concentrated tail events (e.g., 0.1% of requests with very long latencies) can cascade into queuing amplification and throughput collapse when retries or autoscaling kicks in. By focusing on the Top-K extreme samples and requiring cross-slice consensus, we reduce false positives from noisy single-slice blips while catching real, high-impact regressions earlier.

Compatibility and scope: The detector plugs into the existing perf-canary pipeline (ingest -> slice-aggregator -> detectors -> orchestrator). No changes to runtime inference path are required. Defaults are conservative: detector disabled by default for non-critical deployments and enabled for Dedicated + Private by the rollout config.

title: Hybrid signal-attn kernel with rotary-sparsity fusion and KV prefetch scheduler
body:
Hybrid signal-attn kernel with rotary-sparsity fusion and KV prefetch scheduler

Motivation: Production workloads exhibit mixed sequence length distributions and intermittent sparsity from rotary/rope quantization artifacts. Existing Flash-style kernels are high-throughput for dense attention but underutilize opportunities where token locality and structured sparsity exist. This PR introduces 'signal-attn', a hybrid kernel that combines a fast-path Flash-like matmul for dense regions and a lightweight sparse-merge engine for rotary-sparsity lanes. The kernel integrates with the serving runtime scheduler using a signal-driven prefetch heuristic for the KV cache and a continuous-batching hint that reduces tail latency without sacrificing throughput.

Summary: Implement a new attention kernel and scheduler hooks that: 1) Detect per-batch rotary-sparsity patterns (simple entropy+mask heuristics) and route attention work to either dense or hybrid execution path. 2) Fuse rotary/rope application into the QKV projection pipeline to avoid an extra transpose+allocate in the hot path. 3) Add KV prefetch scheduler hints that prioritize hot shards and stagger prefetch to avoid PCIe contention under bursty arrival patterns. 4) Expose a runtime config flag to tune the hybrid threshold and continuous-batcher latency budget.

Benchmarks: Microbenchmarks run on p4d-like instance (A100 style) with representative models: - 7B dense: 15% throughput increase, 12% median latency reduction, 9% p99 reduction. - 13B mixed-length: 22% throughput increase, 17% median latency reduction, 18% p99 reduction. - 70B semi-sparse eval (synth rope sparsity): 25% throughput uplift on best-effort routing, 23% p99 reduction after warm-up. End-to-end synthetic RLHF workload saw a 14% token-cost reduction due to fewer recomputations and better batching. Full benchmark logs attached in artifacts.

Commits: single continuous-string summary of commits in this PR: "commit 1: core: add signal-attn kernel and hybrid exec path; commit 2: runtime: KV prefetch scheduler hints, continuous-batcher integration; commit 3: bindings: python and ts exposed config, tests and docs; commit 4: perf: microbench harness and regression tests; commit 5: fix: lint and CI fixes after review"

title: econ-sandbox: introduce autotune sandbox CLI for batch/cache/quant defaults
body:
econ-sandbox: introduce autotune sandbox CLI for batch/cache/quant defaults

Title: econ-sandbox: introduce autotune sandbox CLI for batch/cache/quant defaults.
Summary: Adds a developer-facing CLI and small platform hooks to run a fast, local 'econ sandbox' that simulates tenant request shapes against candidate batching, cache warmup, and quantization profiles and outputs recommended defaults and unit-econ estimates.
Motivation: Teams repeatedly run ad-hoc scripts to tune batching, cache prefill, and quantization for new tenants. This PR formalizes a lightweight sandbox that codifies the heuristics we use in production autotuners so engineers can iterate faster and generate reproducible suggestions tailored to tenant traffic patterns. The tool is intended to accelerate onboarding of Dedicated/Private customers and reduce manual tuning work that currently costs engineering time and leads to suboptimal unit economics.
What this changes: 1) New CLI command: redwood econ sandbox run --profile=<yaml> --dry-run|--apply which loads a small YAML workload signature and candidate profile list, runs a fast probabilistic simulation and returns ranked recommendations with estimated token-cost and p95 latency impact. 2) New config schema: /configs/econ/sandbox-profiles/*.yaml (three sample profiles added: conservative, balanced, aggressive). 3) Telemetry additions: econ.sandbox.recommendation_score, econ.sandbox.simulated_p50_ms, econ.sandbox.simulated_p95_ms, econ.sandbox.estimated_cost_tokens. 4) Safety gate: recommendations flagged with a latency-risk tag if simulated p95 exceeds the target SLO; these recommendations are excluded from --apply unless --force is passed. 5) Small API surface: a sandbox runner library under pkg/econ/sandbox that can be reused by the existing autotuner and by integration tests. 6) E2E smoke test and a new unit-econ regression test in ci/econ that validates scoring stability over a canonical trace.
Implementation notes: The simulator is intentionally approximate: it uses an event-driven, light-weight replay that models batching dynamics, KV-cache hit rates (with configurable prefix skew), and quantization model latency profiles (sampled from per-device latency histograms). It supports 'dry-run' mode that emits a JSON recommendation bundle and a human-readable summary. The CLI also supports --compare <baseline-id> to diff the proposed defaults against an existing tenant profile.
Commits (summary): initial scaffold and CLI wiring; sandbox runner core simulation and workload YAML parser; three sample profiles and docs; telemetry probes and metric docs; e2e smoke test and CI job; address review fixes and test flakiness; polish and squash for merge.
Files touched (high-level): pkg/econ/sandbox/{runner.go,simulator.go,profile.go} (new); cmd/redwood/econ_sandbox.go (new CLI wiring); configs/econ/sandbox-profiles/{conservative.yaml,balanced.yaml,aggressive.yaml} (new sample profiles); internal/telemetry/metrics.go (added metrics and docs string constants); ci/econ/smoke_test.sh (new); docs/ops/econ-sandbox.md (new). Diffs are intentionally focused on orchestration/config and the sandbox library; no runtime kernel changes included.
Testing and CI: Added a small e2e smoke test that runs the CLI in dry-run against a canned trace; unit tests for scoring and p95 estimation; CI job added to the econ test matrix with a 10m timeout. The CI run for this PR initially failed due to a flaky telemetry mock; a follow-up commit stabilizes the mock and CI greened. The final CI status is pass across linux/amd64 unit and e2e matrices.
Review thread (high level): - Liam Chen (reviewer): "Nice. Please add more explicit p95 budget examples and make it obvious when a recommendation trades cost for latency." Author reply: "Added latency-risk tagging and explicit example in the docs; updated CLI help to show cost/latency tradeoff table." - Diego Rivera: "Can the sampler handle multi-tenant bursty shapes? Also please ensure telemetry cardinality is bounded." Author reply: "Sampler supports configurable burst distributions; limited metric labels to profile_id and tenant_class to avoid cardinality explosion. Added note in metrics docs." - Marta Gomez: "Unit tests look good but one e2e flaked on GH runner - saw occasional timeouts" Author reply: "Added retry and smaller trace for CI e2e; left the larger trace for local runs only." - Security (inline): "Tool runs only on authorized operator CLI; ensure apply path requires RBAC check." Author reply: "CLI apply path checks operator role via existing auth hook; added unit test asserting unauthorized apply is rejected."
Requested changes prior to approval: include latency-risk safety gate, bound telemetry labels, stabilize e2e smoke test, and add example tenant profile. All requested items were addressed in follow-ups.
Post-review approvals: Liam Chen approved after docs added; Diego approved after sampler changes; Marta approved after e2e stabilization.
Merge: Squash merge to main.
Migration/Operational notes: - New metrics emitted by the sandbox are low-frequency and behind a feature flag econ.sandbox.enabled which defaults to off in production config. - Sample profiles are shipped with clear disclaimers; operators should run the sandbox and validate before applying to production tenants. - Docs added at docs/ops/econ-sandbox.md with example workflows and recommended guardrails.
Backwards compatibility: None of the changes alter runtime serving behavior unless an operator explicitly uses the CLI to apply recommendations. The package API is additive.
Rollout plan: Feature flagged in config; enable for internal SRE and solutions teams first; collect telemetry and iterate on scoring.
Release notes: Adds econ sandbox CLI for local autotune simulation with sample profiles and safety gates; suitable for engineering and solutions workflows.
Known limitations and follow-ups: - Current simulator does not model multi-device cross-shard sharding penalties precisely; follow-up ticket ENG-4999 to extend the simulator with shard-aware latency profiles. - Recommend a follow-up to add a 'batch-size ladder' visualizer (ENG-5002) and an autotuner connector that pipes sandbox recommendations into the existing autotune pipeline (ENG-5003).
Add new econ-sandbox CLI to simulate tenant workloads and propose batching/caching/quant defaults; includes e2e smoke, safety gates for latency SLOs, and documentation; non-breaking

title: thresholded-shadow-canary-orchestration-with-quarantine
body:
thresholded-shadow-canary-orchestration-with-quarantine

Motivation: production model promotion needs deterministic, metric-driven promotion and a lightweight quarantine path for problematic variants without full rollback noise. This PR implements a thresholded shadow->canary promotion flow and a quarantine first-class primitive that isolates models showing drift or error spikes. Changes include: new rollout controller state machine, metric threshold DSL, quarantine API surface, deterministic warmup windows, and end-to-end integration with the observability stack and canary alerts. Design highlights: 1) Shadow priming stage: route mirrored traffic to candidate model while keeping responses hidden; automatic delta metrics (latency, token-err, perplexity, hallucination-score) computed over sampling windows. 2) Threshold evaluation: a compact DSL in rollout config allows percentage and absolute thresholds with lookback windows (e.g., latency_p95<120ms AND token_err_rate_delta<0.5%). 3) Canary promotion: automated gradual traffic bump with hold windows and automated rollback if thresholds violated. 4) Quarantine: when a threshold breach occurs during shadow or canary, the controller moves the variant to 'quarantined' state, which preserves logs, stops routing live traffic, and spins a lightweight readonly debug endpoint for replaying failing traces. 5) Safety: automatic cooldowns, explicit owner notifications, and a manual override to promote from quarantine after investigation. This description includes the user-visible rollout configuration changes and the operational playbook.
Arjun Patel (2026-02-12): Left a few nit comments on the threshold DSL parsing; suggest clearer error messages when thresholds are malformed.
Marisol Vega (2026-02-12): Addressed parsing errors and added explicit user-facing messages in rollout_config_errors.ts
Leila Morgan (2026-02-15): Concern about metric cardinality — will delta pipeline tolerate high-cardinality user ids? Recommend sampling by customer_id hash.
Marisol Vega (2026-02-16): Updated delta_metrics processor to aggregate by customer_id hash and added config knob to adjust sample rate.
Dmitri Kovalev (2026-02-18): Verified quarantine replay endpoint is read-only and cannot issue side-effecting downstream calls. Approved after minor test additions.
CI Bot (2026-02-20): e2e-canary failed on first run due to infra race; rerun passed. All checks green.
Leila Morgan (2026-02-22): Approved — leaving a follow-up request to add rate-limited alerts in console (ENG-1158).
Add thresholded shadow-to-canary promotion flow and a quarantine lifecycle for model variants. Operators can now configure metric thresholds to trigger automated rollback and quarantine, inspect quarantined variants via console, and replay traces for debugging. Includes new rollout schema and example configs.
Unit tests cover DSL parsing and state transitions; integration tests exercise mirrored traffic, delta metrics, and quarantine transitions. E2E harness runs realistic traffic patterns to validate canary bumping and automated rollback. Manual QA: run shadow example config against staging, verify quarantined variant is isolated and replay works.
Ship behind feature flag. Stage 1: enable shadow mirroring for internal customers only (1 week). Stage 2: enable automated threshold evaluation and quarantine alerts in staging. Stage 3: activate automated canary promotion with conservative steps (0.5% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20%) and hold windows. Monitor p95, token_err_rate and hallucination-score deltas; any threshold breach moves candidate to quarantine. Provide manual override path for owners.
Shadow mirroring adds a small async forwarding cost; observed 0.7% overall CPU increase in staging under representative load. Deterministic warmups reduce cold-start variance; no material latency regression for primary path.
ENG-1158 — add rate-limited quarantine alerts and console throttling
ENG-1164 — tune default threshold templates for chat vs. completion workloads
ENG-1171 — expose quarantine replay API to SRE runbooks
DOC-89 — add quickstart for quarantine-led incident triage

title: stream-facade-lightweight-cred-fallback-and-backoff-profiles
body:
stream-facade-lightweight-cred-fallback-and-backoff-profiles

Context and motivation: Multiple downstream teams reported friction when migrating from push-based stream handlers to more ergonomic pull-iterators and when rotating short-lived credentials in multi-tenant setups. This PR introduces a small, pluggable streaming facade (pull-iterator API) surfaced by the redwood runtime and SDK adapters, a credential-fallback mesh that lets SDKs fall back through a prioritized chain (env -> host-proxy -> refresh-token-provider) without surface changes to application code, and a set of named backoff profiles (fast/standard/steady) to simplify retry ergonomics. Checklist: - [x] Implement pull-style streaming facade in the runtime shim - [x] Add thin adapter implementations in go/ts/python SDK layers - [x] Credential fallback chain with clear opt-out - [x] Add named backoff profiles + telemetry hooks - [x] Update docs, examples, and changelog - [x] Cross-SDK integration tests and local e2e run Commits summary: commit 1: add streaming facade interface and initial runtime bridge; commit 2: implement credential fallback mesh and priority resolver; commit 3: add backoff profile registry and default policy; commit 4: SDK adapters (go/ts/python) and small portability shims; commit 5: tests, docs, and changelog updates. Changed areas/files (high level): - runtime/streaming/facade.go: new lightweight facade and interface adapters - runtime/auth/fallback_resolver.go: prioritized credential chain - sdk/go/adapter/pullstream.go: go-side adapter and examples - sdk/ts/src/pullIteratorAdapter.ts: typescript adapter + typed examples - sdk/python/redwood/pull_stream.py: python pull iterator shim - docs/sdk/streaming.md: design and migration guide - tests/integration/stream_pull_e2e: cross-sdk e2e harness Notable implementation details: the facade is intentionally minimal (Next()/peek token semantics) to avoid coupling to transport changes; the credential mesh resolves providers in order and only uses the next provider if the previous returns a 401 or expired-token sentinel; backoff profiles are parameterized (initial_ms, max_ms, multiplier, jitter) and registered centrally to ensure parity across SDKs. Review conversation highlights: - Sofia: "Can we avoid implicit blocking on Next() for sync SDKs?" Author reply: "The adapter exposes both async and sync wrappers; sync callers get a small bounded worker that buffers 1 item to avoid unbounded blocking." - Miguel: "Telemetry hooks need callsite labels for batching vs single-token flows." Author: "Added 'stream.kind' tag and unit tests." - Ava: "Do we risk credential leakage when proxying fallback providers?" Author: "The mesh enforces a single in-memory token cache per request scope and optionally emits audit events; documented and opt-outtable." CI and testing: initial CI run flagged lint failures in the TS adapter; those were fixed in commit 4. Integration matrix run passed across go1.21, node18, python3.11 matrices. Flaky test observed in e2e harness (stream termination race) and mitigated by adding a small grace window and idempotent close semantics. Performance and compatibility notes: microbenchmarks show the facade adds ~0.8-1.4% CPU overhead on steady throughput but simplifies caller code and avoids complex coroutine juggling. Compatibility layer ensures existing push-based streaming clients continue to work; new API is additive. Migration notes: documented step-by-step guide in docs/sdk/streaming.md and added small examples in sdk/*/examples/pullstream. Security and privacy: credential fallback respects KMS boundaries and never logs token material; audit events are opt-in. Release plan: included in next patch SDK release cycle; manual migration guidance and an automated codemod for TypeScript added under tools/codemods. Merge outcome: PR was approved by all reviewers and merged via squash on 2026-03-04 after green CI. Related work: follows up on ENG-7541 (stream ergonomics spike) and pairs with a future runtime scheduling change (ENG-9620).
Introduce a lightweight streaming facade that unifies pull-style iterators across Go/TS/Python, adds a credential fallback mesh for short-lived tokens, and exposes configurable backoff profiles for ergonomic defaults.

title: Introduce RBACv2 policy synthesizer, KMS usage reviewer, and audit reconciliation job
body:
Introduce RBACv2 policy synthesizer, KMS usage reviewer, and audit reconciliation job

Motivation: Recent support tickets (SUP-903) and internal postmortem identified two recurring pain points: (1) RBACv2 rollouts often over-provisioned operator bindings leading to unexpected KMS calls crossing geo boundaries; (2) audit logs and KMS access records were not reconciled, making longitudinal investigations slow. This PR ships a three-part solution: a policy synthesizer that emits minimal effective RBAC patches, a KMS usage reviewer that tags KMS calls with derived decision traces and residency flags, and an audit-reconciliation job that cross-checks authz decisions, KMS events, and immutable audit envelopes to flag inconsistencies.

Design summary: - policy/synthesizer: a deterministic pass that consumes role-presets + service-claim annotations and outputs minimal allow-lists (keeps deny semantics untouched). It is implemented as an idempotent compiler stage used by the policy orchestrator during canaries. - kms/reviewer: sidecar-style aggregator (service behind /internal/kms-review) that enriches KMS telemetry with policy-decision-ids, tenant-residency, and operator-scope to enable quota/residency checks. - audit/reconciler: periodic job (configurable cadence) which performs joins across authz_decisions, kms_access_log, and audit_envelopes to produce a per-tenant discrepancy report written to compliance.reconciliations. The job includes a lightweight dedupe and fingerprint algorithm to avoid noisy alerts.

Implementation notes/changes: - new package: internal/policy/synthesizer (Go) with unit tests and fakes for operator presets. - new service: services/kms-reviewer (small Go HTTP service + Prometheus metrics), deployed as a singleton per-region. - migration: add reconciliations table (+ schema v43) to postgres; migration includes backfill script limited to 30 days. - observability: new metrics policy_synth_runs_total, kms_reviewer_calls, reconciler_discrepancies_by_type; tags include tenant_id and region. - ops: added a cron manifest at deploy/cron/reconciler.yaml and a Helm values section to opt-in for high-compliance tenants.

Checklist:
- [x] Unit tests for synthesizer compiler logic
- [x] Integration tests for kms-reviewer enrichment route
- [x] Migration and backfill tested on staging
- [x] Metrics and logs instrumented
- [x] Documentation: docs/rbac/policy-synthesizer.md and docs/ops/reconciler-runbook.md
- [x] Security scan (snyk/gosec) passed after fixing two low-severity findings

Commits (high level): - 1) add synthesizer core + tests - 2) implement kms reviewer service and client shim - 3) add reconciler job + migration - 4) add Helm charts + deploy manifests - 5) docs and runbook - 6) fixes from reviewers (metrics labels, retry tuning)

Changed areas (high level): - internal/policy/synthesizer/* - services/kms-reviewer/{cmd,handlers,metrics} - jobs/reconciler/* - cmd/infra/migrations/043_add_reconciliations.sql - deploy/helm/redwood/templates/cron-reconciler.yaml - docs/rbac/policy-synthesizer.md - docs/ops/reconciler-runbook.md

Review conversation (summary): - Ethan Chu: "Can we avoid an N^2 policy expansion in the synthesizer?" Reply: added a constraint-sweep that limits expansion to cross-service grants only; added tests and a benchmark fixture. - Marta Kaczmarek: "Metrics need tenant and region labels for SLO slicing." Reply: added tenant_id and region labels, instrumented with cardinality guard and sample rate. - Samir Patel: "Make migration backward-compatible for mixed-version clusters." Reply: reconciler backfill is guarded by a feature flag and uses a read-path fallback when reconciliations table is not present.

CI summary: - unit: pass - integration: pass (flaky test fixed in commit 5) - lint: pass - e2e: pass on staging deployment - security-scan: initial fail (gosec findings) -> patched -> pass. Full pipeline passed on rerun.

Operational notes: - Default deployment is opt-in for enterprise tenants via Helm values `reconciler.enabled`. - KMS reviewer runs as a regional singleton to keep cross-tenant telemetry coalesced. - To troubleshoot mismatches, use the new /internal/debug/reconciler endpoint (RBAC-protected) which returns sample joined artifacts for a reconciliation ID.

Merge outcome: Squashed and merged to main. Post-merge: run migration v43 during next maintenance window; operators on Dedicated/Private should coordinate with infra for opt-in. Release note included. If any tenant relies on implicit operator bindings, they should schedule a canary with policy.synth.enabled=false to avoid immediate rollbacks.
Added RBACv2 policy synthesizer (auto-minimization), KMS usage reviewer service, and periodic audit reconciliation job. No API changes to public endpoints. Ops: add new cronjob and a small DB migration.
This PR was intentionally split into small commits to make the security review easier; product/ops are informed. No public SDK changes.

title: standby-router + adaptive-slo-thermostat: regional soft-eviction hotpatch
body:
standby-router + adaptive-slo-thermostat: regional soft-eviction hotpatch

Motivation: In a recent incident (SUP-1291) we observed noisy evictions when a regional egress bottleneck caused aggressive tenant-level shedding. This PR introduces a standby-router that preserves inflight KV prefixes for tenants during regional reroutes, and an adaptive SLO thermostat that smooths eviction thresholds based on short-term KV pressure and latency quantiles. The goal is graceful degradation with fewer oscillations and faster recovery after transient egress spikes.

Changes in this PR (summary):
- New standby routing component: router/standby_router.go (coordination for transparent regional handoff, keeps per-tenant KV hold indices).
- Adaptive SLO thermostat: scheduler/thermostat.go (exponential cool-down + minimum hold window to prevent flapping).
- Telemetry hooks and backpressure marshal: telemetry/backpressure_marshal.go (adds histogram of KV pressure + tenant stay counts).
- Config knobs: configs/standby.yaml and defaults.yaml (tunable windows and memory caps).
- Integration test: tests/integration/regional_failover_standby_test.go (simulates bursty egress with tenant mixes).
- Minor docs: docs/operation/standby-router.md (operational runbook).

Commit summary: (3 commits, squashed on merge)
- 1) introduce standby router skeleton, initial tests, config schema
- 2) implement adaptive thermostat and integrate with serving runtime; add telemetry, add e2e toggles
- 3) fix race in KV hold map, add backpressure histogram labels, address lint failures

Files changed (high level):
- router/standby_router.go (+210 additions)
- scheduler/thermostat.go (+150 additions)
- telemetry/backpressure_marshal.go (+32 additions, +4 deletions)
- configs/standby.yaml (+10 additions)
- docs/operation/standby-router.md (+8 additions)
- tests/integration/regional_failover_standby_test.go (+20 additions)
- go.mod/go.sum (dep bumps for prometheus client)

Testing & CI notes:
- CI initially failed on unit tests in scheduler/thermostat.go due to a nondeterministic goroutine ordering; added a deterministic clock interface and re-ran.
- Lint complained about exported docstrings; fixed formatting in docs/operation/standby-router.md.
- Telemetry e2e asserts flaked in one run (timing dependent) so integration test was hardened to poll for histogram convergence instead of strict timing. Final CI result: all checks passed (build, unit, integration, lint).

Review conversation (high level):
- Priya Menon: "High-level: I like keeping standby state lightweight, but can we ensure per-tenant memory is bounded? Suggest adding per-tenant TTL + eviction priority. Also please add a small benchmark to confirm cost under normal traffic."
- Author (Evan): "Addressed: enforced per-tenant maxHoldBytes and default TTL=30s in configs/standby.yaml. Added microbenchmark router/bench/standby_bench_test.go (lightweight) and included results in the PR description."
- Sanjay Patel: "Concern about circuit interaction: thermostat changes thresholds; how does it play with our existing tenant-level circuit-breaker?"
- Author (Evan): "Thermostat exposes a `slo_inhibit` flag that temporarily raises threshold but consults the tenant circuit state before permitting any soft-eviction; added unit tests to validate the consult path. Kept behavior additive (no override of hard-circuit)."
- Karen O'Neill: "Telemetry labels are important — please ensure tenant id is redacted in metrics exported to external sinks."
- Author (Evan): "Telemetry now exports tenant cohort (hash bucket) rather than raw IDs; clarified in telemetry/backpressure_marshal.go and in docs. Added note to runbook about how to map cohorts for on-call context."
- Priya (after changes): "Approving pending one minor comment about constant naming style."

Risk assessment & rollout plan: "Low-to-moderate risk. Feature gated behind runtime flag `enable_standby_router` (disabled by default). Thermostat enabled behind `adaptive_slo_thermostat` flag; thermostat defaults mimic previous static thresholds. Rollout plan: canary in one non-production region for 24h -> small production cohort (5% of traffic) for 6h -> 25% for 6h -> full rollout. Runbook includes emergency toggle to force immediate disable (console + API)."

Operational notes and metrics to watch (added to runbook):
- tenant_evictions_count (should decrease for transient bursts)
- kv_pressure_histogram (tail should compress, watch p95/p99)
- standby_hold_memory_bytes (per-region gauge; ensure below configured caps)
- thermostat_reopen_events (should show reduced reopen oscillations)

Why this is different from prior work: Prior PRs tuned eviction aggressiveness or added simple backoff. This PR is focused on short-lived state preservation during regional handoffs and an adaptive control loop (thermostat) that respects tenant hard-circuits and reduces oscillatory behavior while still providing SLO safeguards. The standby-router keeps only lightweight KV hold indices and uses cohorting + TTL to bound memory.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Priya and Sanjay and green CI. Changelog entry included and the hotfix scheduled in 2026.02.24 patch.

Notes for follow-ups (tracked as ENG tickets):
- ENG-4923: stronger memory accounting per-tenant and cross-region replica pruning
- ENG-4924: prometheus exporter scrubber for cohorts to support SAML-PII requirement
- ENG-4925: stress test harness for long-running standby_router with mixed tenant churn

Benchmarks (post-change micro-bench on c5-sim): "standby router overhead ~+2.1% CPU at 99th traffic case; eviction oscillation reduced by 48% in synthetic burst test compared to baseline."

If reverting: disable feature flags and deploy a rollback; standby state expires within TTL so rollback is soft.

End of PR description.
Backported standby routing for regional failover and added adaptive SLO thermostat to reduce oscillatory evictions under bursty KV pressure. Hotfix to be included in 2026.02.24 patch release.
Benchmarked and canary plan attached to Linear ENG-4821
Hotfix included in 2026.02.24 release train

title: Multi-sequence primer and deterministic warmup replayer
body:
Multi-sequence primer and deterministic warmup replayer

Context: Long-tail latency spikes in steady-state runs were traced to nondeterministic warmup phases where sequence primer ordering and random trace replay caused noisy p95/p99 shifts. This PR introduces a deterministic warmup replayer plus a multi-sequence primer that lets workload runners reliably prime KV caches, prefix caches, and attention cache states for repeatable steady-state benchmarking. Motivation: Reduce noise in regression signals from warmup variance and make perf baselines reproducible across runs and CI shards. Goal is not to micro-optimize runtime, but to provide a reproducible priming path and a light-weight validation harness that guarantees same sequence ordering and timing semantics across hosts. Changes: - New bench/runner/deterministic_replayer.py: replay engine that accepts normalized traces and deterministic timing profiles. - New bench/runner/multi_sequence_primer.py: orchestrates interleaved sequences, supports prefix merging and synthetic token insertion for realistic priming. - bench/configs/deterministic_warmup.yaml: configuration presets (short/medium/long) used by CI and local profiling. - bench/utils/trace_normalizer.py: converts collected traces into canonical forms (canonical tokenization, anonymization of IDs, consistent timestamp deltas). - tests/integration/test_primer_replayer.py: integration coverage for determinism assertions across 3 seeds and 2 host types. - ci/workflows/bench.yml: adds a deterministic bench job that runs the warmup-only profile on PRs labeled "benchmark". Implementation notes: - Determinism is enforced by a combination of normalized traces and fixed rng seeds; we avoid global state where possible and expose a ReplayContext object to the runner. - The replayer can run in two modes: strict (asserts identical sequence of emitted tokens) and tolerant (allows whitespace/tokenizer variants but asserts same token ids after normalization). - The primer supports interleaving policy strategies (round-robin, weighted) to simulate multiplexed tenant scenarios. Performance impact: baseline warmup-only runs show p95 reduction variance from ±9.8% to ±2.1% over 20 repeated runs (local VM), and end-to-end benchmark CI runs show improved stability of baseline metrics (p95 confidence interval width reduced by ~3.6x). Checklist: - [x] Design doc walkthrough with ENG-7122 stakeholders - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] CI job added and green - [x] Benchmarks added to baseline runbook - [x] Release notes drafted How to exercise locally: 1) python -m bench.runner.deterministic_replayer --config bench/configs/deterministic_warmup.yaml --trace samples/short_coldstart.trace 2) python -m bench.runner.multi_sequence_primer --mode strict --policy round-robin --runs 20 Notes and limitations: - This does not change serving runtime batching logic; it's purely a workload/priming harness. - Determinism guarantees apply only after trace normalization; traces collected from different tokenizer versions must be normalized first. - The replayer is intentionally lightweight; future work (ENG-7210) will add a golden-trace repository and artifact signing. title: model-family kernel picker + GQA/MQA tuning + Qwen KV-cache stride fix
body:
model-family kernel picker + GQA/MQA tuning + Qwen KV-cache stride fix

Context: we observed higher tail latency and sporadic OOMs when serving mixed workloads containing Mistral, Qwen and Llama family models. Root causes were: (1) suboptimal kernel selection for fused rotary/attention on Mistral and some Llama variants, (2) misaligned group-quantization (GQA) code paths that spilled to host under certain MQA layouts, and (3) a KV-cache pointer/stride bug in Qwen cache layout that created fragmentation under continuous batching. This PR introduces a model-family aware kernel picker (heuristics based on model_family, hidden_size, seq_dist) that prefers fused-rotary + threaded attention kernels for Mistral/Llama; adds quantization-aware attention execution paths to handle GQA/MQA edge cases (avoids fp16->host spills by switching to a compact packed layout when group sizes mismatch); fixes Qwen KV-cache stride/pointer arithmetic and compacts cache layout to reduce working set; and adjusts continuous-batcher thresholds and micro-batch sizing per-model to prevent cross-model OOMs. Also includes unit/integration tests, perf microbench harness updates, and a staged rollout plan (canary -> 30% -> global). Motivation and impact: these are production-facing fixes that improve latency and stability without requiring model rewrites. Backwards-compatible toggles are exposed as runtime knobs (kernel_picker.mode, quant.tune_mode, kvcache.compact_layout) that default to safe behavior. Rollout notes: start with canary in us-west-2 for 48 hours, monitor token-level latency and OOM counts, then 30% for 72 hours before global.

Ava Chen: Added deterministic workload harness and results in perf_benchmarks, also wired CI perf check to run with fixed seeds.
Priya Kapoor: The quant fallback looks safe but please call out any additional mem overhead. Also prefer a feature flag for 30-day grace.
Ava Chen: quant.tune_mode default uses compact-packed only when group sizes misalign; documented expected ~0.6-1.4% peak memory overhead in worst-case and added a runtime flag quant.tune_mode=off for emergency rollback.
Ethan Li: Verified that fused_rotary path is a pure opt for Mistral-7B and doesn't regress Llama-7B; approved after smoke tests on dedicated pools.
Improved model-family kernel selection for Mistral/Llama, fixed Qwen KV-cache stride fragmentation, and added GQA/MQA-safe quantization fallback. Result: lower p50/p95 latency and fewer OOMs under mixed workloads. Exposed runtime knobs for gradual rollout and rollback.
Repro: mixed-workload harness (Mistral-7B, Llama-13B, Qwen-14B) ran for 100k requests with deterministic seeds. Added CI perf job that runs 3x stable-seed trials. Canary in us-west-2 for 48h with observed telemetry; then 30% for 72h. No regressions in unit/integration suites.

Llama-13B mixed prompt workload: p50 token latency -8%, p95 -19%, throughput +12%

title: Add KMS metrics + tracing spans for standardized wrapper calls
body:
Add KMS metrics + tracing spans for standardized wrapper calls

Summary: Instruments all KMS operations invoked via the new shared wrapper with metrics and trace spans following Redwood telemetry conventions. Adds latency histograms, request/error counters (tagged by canonical error taxonomy), and a consistent tracing span shape so on-call can correlate KMS degradation to elevated 5xx/latency. Motivation: As we harden KMS integration paths (ENG-4821), we need consistent KMS dependency signals across control-plane and data-plane components. Recent support cases and a throttling-related incident (SUP-19377) showed we lacked enough granularity to quickly answer: (1) which operation is failing, (2) whether it’s retry amplification, (3) what error class dominates, and (4) which region/provider is impacted. This PR builds on pr-18421’s wrapper API and wires metrics/spans at the wrapper boundary (single place, consistent tags). What’s included: Metrics (emitted on every wrapper call): 1) redwood.kms.request.count (counter) tags: operation, provider, region, result (success|error), error_category (when error). 2) redwood.kms.request.latency_ms (histogram) tags: operation, provider, region, result. 3) redwood.kms.retries.count (counter) tags: operation, provider, region, error_category. 4) redwood.kms.throttled.count (counter) tags: provider, region (incremented for throttling-class responses, including SDK-specific throttle codes mapped into the canonical taxonomy). Tracing: Adds a span around each KMS wrapper call: span name: kms.<operation> (e.g., kms.decrypt, kms.encrypt, kms.generate_data_key, kms.describe_key) attributes: kms.operation, kms.provider, cloud.region, kms.key_ref (redacted; alias name when present, otherwise stable hash), kms.retry_attempt (per attempt), kms.error_category (when error), kms.http_status (when available from SDK metadata), and kms.request_id (when provided by provider SDK). Notes: we explicitly do not attach raw key ARNs or plaintext key IDs; key references are sanitized. Error taxonomy mapping: Uses the canonical categories discussed in ENG-4822 and the eng-security thread (AccessDenied, NotFound, Throttling, Timeout, InvalidCiphertext, DependencyUnavailable, Unknown). Mapping is implemented in kms/telemetry/error_mapping.go and shared by metrics + span attributes + logs. Sampling: Spans respect existing tracing sampling decisions (no new always-on sampling); metrics are always emitted. This is intentional so we can alert on dependency health even when traces are sampled. Changed areas (high level): - pkg/security/kms/wrapper/*: inject TelemetryReporter into wrapper client; emit metrics + spans; ensure metrics are recorded for success/failure and for each attempt where relevant. - pkg/telemetry/metrics/registry.go: registers KMS meters and canonical tag keys (prevents ad-hoc tag drift). - pkg/telemetry/tracing/spans.go: helper to build KMS spans with consistent attribute names and safe key redaction. - pkg/security/kms/providers/aws.go, gcp.go, azure.go: normalizes provider-specific error codes into canonical error categories; plumbs request-id and status metadata when available. - docs/internal/observability/metrics.md: adds KMS metric names + tag glossary (internal only). Example metric/tag conventions (for reviewers): - operation values: decrypt | encrypt | generate_data_key | describe_key | reencrypt - provider values: aws | gcp | azure - error_category values: AccessDenied | NotFound | Throttling | Timeout | InvalidCiphertext | DependencyUnavailable | Unknown - region values: us-east-1, etc. (or provider equivalent) Testing: - Unit tests for error mapping across providers (golden table tests). - Unit tests verifying tag sets (ensures we don’t regress into high-cardinality tags). - Local smoke: ran data-plane integration tests against the KMS stub; verified metrics emission via in-process exporter. Rollout / follow-ups: - SRE will add dashboards/alerts in a separate PR (observability-pack/pr-844). - Once wrapper migration is complete across remaining call sites, we can remove legacy ad-hoc KMS logging in services. Checklist: - [x] No sensitive data in metrics/tags (no key ARNs, no account IDs) - [x] Error taxonomy matches ENG-4822 - [x] Metrics follow Redwood naming + tagging conventions - [x] Traces use consistent span naming/attributes - [x] Unit tests for mapping and tag set validation
Allison Grant (requested changes): Please align metric tag keys with existing conventions; avoid key_id as a tag; add explicit note about high-cardinality prevention. Nadia Rahman (author): Updated registry to centralize allowed tags; renamed tag from key_id -> key_ref (sanitized alias/hash); added a unit test asserting no raw ARNs; expanded docs/internal/observability/metrics.md with cardinality guidelines. Kevin Osei: Looks good; please ensure error_category is present only when result=error and that success paths don’t emit empty/unknown values. Nadia: Adjusted instrumentation to omit error_category on success; added test. Sean Gallagher: Can we also emit a retries counter so we can spot retry storms early? Nadia: Added redwood.kms.retries.count tagged by operation/provider/region/error_category. Ethan Park: Confirmed wrapper boundary is correct place; thanks for not leaking ARNs. Caleb Johnson: Span naming/attributes match tracing guidelines; approved. Final approvals: Allison Grant, Kevin Osei, Sean Gallagher, Caleb Johnson. Merged via squash.

title: Add cohort stability index and alert weave for long-tail token variance
body:
Add cohort stability index and alert weave for long-tail token variance

Context: Long-tail spikes in per-request token cost and tail latency have been producing noisy alerts that are hard to triage. Root cause analysis shows that the noise frequently correlates with small, coherent cohorts (prompt shapes, tenant routing, or certain model variants) that briefly diverge. Motivation: introduce an explicit cohort-level stability signal that (1) surfaces which cohorts are driving long-tail variance, (2) powers an alert-weave that groups and suppresses short-lived noise, and (3) enables prioritized sampling for post-incident trace capture. This PR implements: - Cohort Stability Index (CSI): a bounded [0..1] score computed per cohort/window that combines normalized token-cost variance, tail-latency skew, and recent alert frequency. CSI is computed in the metrics service as a rolling sketch to control memory and cardinality. - Alert Weave: a policy layer that uses CSI to group alerts and apply short-circuit suppression for cohorts with transient instability (CSI spikes under configured duration), while still escalating sustained cohort regressions. - Dashboard + Heatmap: new 'Cohort Stability' dashboard that shows CSI sparklines, cohort membership counts, and a token-cost delta heatmap for quick root-cause triangulation. - Sampler seeding: when CSI crosses threshold, we increase sampled trace rate for affected cohorts via the sampling controller to capture KV cache state, kernel queue traces, and request headers. Implementation notes: - Metrics path: services/observability/metrics/cohort_index.go implements a compact bfloat sketch followed by a dampening window to avoid flapping. CSI tags: model_variant, route, tenant_id (tenant_id is optional and high-cardinality guarded by a cardinality cap). - Alerting path: services/alerting/policies/weave_policy.go implements grouping keys and suppression windows; default policy is non-breaking and opt-in per alertrule. - Dashboard: dashboards/cohort-stability.json includes preconfigured queries and example cohort selectors. - Backwards compatibility: all new metrics are additive. The default behavior preserves existing alerting; customers must opt-in to enable cohort-aware suppression via feature flag. Rollout plan: 1) Feature gated rollout for internal telemetry team; 2) Monitor false-negative risk with an internal runbook; 3) Expand opt-in to selected tenants; 4) Gradual on-by-default if no regression. Checklist: - [x] Core CSI computation implemented and unit-tested - [x] Alert weave policy AND feature flag - [x] Dashboard and runbook - [x] Sampling integration (seeded) - [x] Docs added (observability/cohort-stability.md) - [x] E2E smoke in staging Tests: unit + integration; synthetic workload in perf-lab to validate non-flapping behavior. Related: ENG-3245 (reduce alert churn), ENG-3310 (prefetch sampling improvements).
Marta: Can we bound the tenant_id cardinality? Suggest adding a capped LRU and exposing an opt-out for enterprise tenants. Jonah: The suppression window feels risky; what are our false-negative SLAs? Please add an explicit fallback that escalates if suppression removes all alerts for >5m. Priya: tests look good overall; please add a small integration test that runs a synthetic spike to confirm sampling kicks in. Author (Evan): Added LRU cap and telemetry for eviction, tightened suppression policy to require sustained CSI>0.7 for >=2 windows before escalation is suppressed, added integration test in perf-lab. Marta: Thanks, lgtm pending CI. Jonah: Approved. Priya: Approved with comment about dashboard labels; addressed. Final approvers: Marta Ruiz (approve), Jonah Kim (approve), Priya Shah (approve).
Introduce Cohort Stability Index (CSI) metric and opt-in Alert Weave policy. CSI helps cluster long-tail token-cost and latency variance by cohort, reduces alert noise via transient suppression, and seeds higher sampling rates for affected cohorts. Feature is gated; enable via helm values.featureFlags.cohortStability=true. No breaking changes.
If alert volume drops after enabling Alert Weave, check the cohort_stability.eviction_rate and suppressed_alerts.time_series. Fallback toggle: disable feature flag to revert to legacy alerting. Run the provided synthetic spike job in perf-lab to validate sampling if traces are missing.

title: Batch Guardian: adaptive defaults and quantization profile templates
body:
Batch Guardian: adaptive defaults and quantization profile templates

Motivation: Tenant onboarding and first-run defaults have been a frequent source of overruns in unit economics (ENG-6421). Teams often pick safe-but-expensive defaults (large batch/over-quantized models) or hand-tune per-tenant, producing unpredictable tail costs. This PR introduces the 'Batch Guardian' subsystem: an automated suggestion/orchestration layer that proposes tenant-specific batching/caching defaults and a curated set of quantization profiles. The goal is to reduce per-token cost by default while keeping latency within SLOs and providing safe fallbacks.

What this PR adds (single-string body): - A lightweight heuristic engine that consumes tenant profile (QPS, 95th-latency target, avg sequence length) and suggests a defaults bundle (batch_size, max_prefill, cache_window_ms, quant_profile). - A catalog of quantization profile templates (Q4_0, Q4_1, Q5_0 variants with metadata describing supported ops and expected memory savings). - Console/UI hooks and a CLI 'redwood defaults apply --dry-run' mode to preview suggested defaults. - Telemetry events and histograms for suggested vs applied configs, and a regression guard that flags quality regressions for canarying. - Unit economics estimator that projects token-cost delta and an estimated warmup budget for dedicated capacity. - Canary rollout orchestration: canary->tiered rollout->full apply with automatic rollback on regression signals.

Design notes: - The engine is intentionally conservative: suggestions include a confidence score and a compatibility matrix for model families. It prefers smaller batch increases but larger cache windows where beneficial. - Quant profiles are saved as YAML templates under optimizer/quant_templates/ with machine-readable metadata so downstream runtime can pick compatible kernels. - Safety: every suggested change is accompanied by a simulated-cost report and a test harness that runs a small sample of customer prompts (if tenant-approved) to check quality-preservation heuristics. - Integration: this PR only generates suggestions by default; auto-apply mode is behind a feature flag and an enterprise opt-in.

Checklist: - [x] Heuristic engine and scoring logic (src/optimizer/batch_guardian.py) - [x] Quant template YAMLs (src/optimizer/quant_templates/) - [x] Console preview and CLI dry-run (webapp/src/components/DefaultsPreview, cli/redwood_defaults.py) - [x] Telemetry hooks and metrics (telemetry/events.py, prometheus/metrics.yaml) - [x] Unit economics estimator (src/optimizer/unit_econ_estimator.py) - [x] Tests: unit + benchmark sim runner (tests/unit/, tests/bench/) - [x] Documentation: operator guide + changelog (docs/operator/batch-guardian.md)

Testing & results: - Local bench sim with 95th-latency target=200ms, avg seq=128, QPS=25: suggested default reduced estimated per-token spend by ~21% vs current conservative defaults, with median latency change of +4ms and 95th latency within SLO. - End-to-end internal canary run (tenant: internal-dev): applied suggestions to 5% traffic for 24h: cost savings observed ~18% with no detected quality regressions based on token-level perplexity and a small holdout prompt-set.

Rollout plan: - Merge to main behind feature flag FLAG_BATCH_GUARDIAN. - Enable dry-run and console preview for internal tenants. - Run staged canaries (2%, 10%, 50%) with automated rollback on: >1% increase in rejection rate OR >5% increase in end-to-end latency at 95th.

Backward compatibility & safety: - All suggestions are additive metadata; runtime ignores unknown quant flags. - Auto-apply needs explicit opt-in per tenant.

Related: ENG-6421 (defaults stabilization), ENG-6609 (budget-aware prefill).

title: Introduce prefill-decode arbiter with token-slip resolver to reduce tail latency in interleaved microbatches
body:
Introduce prefill-decode arbiter with token-slip resolver to reduce tail latency in interleaved microbatches

Motivation: In high-concurrency interactive workloads we see tail latency caused by mismatch between prefill completion and decode pipeline admission (especially with interleaved microbatches and KV snapshots). This PR implements a lightweight prefill-decode arbiter and a token-slip resolver that together reduce tail amplification when prefill fragments finish out-of-order. Design summary: 1) Arbiter: a per-GPU token-budgeted admission controller that tracks inflight prefill fragments and decode lanes; it enforces a soft budget per microstripe and prioritizes decode admission based on token age, model priority, and observed KV readiness. 2) Token-slip resolver: when a prefill fragment finishes earlier or later than its paired decode window, the resolver computes a minimal token-alignment correction (slip) to avoid unnecessary decode stalls or duplicated KV priming. The resolver prefers KV reuse over redundant priming where safe. 3) Snapshotted KV hints: integrate a lightweight KV snapshot tag with prefill fragments to allow decode to select warm KV lanes without full re-prime. Implementation notes: arbiter implemented in runtime/scheduler/arbiter.py as ~250LOC modular component; it exposes a tiny admission API (request_admit, release_tokens, prioritize) and a metrics surface (arbiter.requests, arbiter.rejected, arbiter.slips). Token-slip resolver implemented in runtime/inference/pipeline.py and runtime/kv/kv_snapshotter.cc; it attaches a 64-bit snapshot tag to prefill responses and allows decode to consult tag->slot mapping before priming. Feature gated behind feature-flag "prefill_decode_arbiter" and rolled out under canary. Benchmarks: microbatch interleave workload (grp: chat-heavy, model: rw-7b, seq_len: 2048) shows p95 generation latency down 18% (from 412ms to 337ms), mean token throughput up 6%, and token CPU-equivalent cost down ~3% when arbiter enabled and snapshot reuse occurs. Tail scenarios with high KV churn show p99 improvement 11%. Tests: unit tests for arbiter logic, deterministic token-slip cases, and an integration perf harness that simulates out-of-order prefill completions. CI: added perf-check and a synthetic e2e streaming run; perf-check is run on a pinned hw node in CI. Compatibility/caveats: arbiter assumes decode kernels can accept a soft-aligned token window; some extremely latency-sensitive models with strict kernel tiling may need per-model opt-out. The KV snapshot tag is intentionally conservative to avoid stale reads; snapshot reuse is only allowed when model pins match and token prefix is deterministic. Rollout plan: 1) feature-flag canary on 5% of traffic for 72h, 2) expand to 25% with increased tracing and cost telemetry, 3) full rollout after 7d if regressions absent. Observability: new dashboards in Console: arbiter/admit-rate, arbiter/slip-count, kv/snapshot-reuse-rate and a per-model breakdown. Related work: builds on ENG-6492 (continuous-batching improvements) and complements earlier prefetch efforts; differs by focusing on admission arbitration and token-level alignment rather than kernel fusion. Checklist: [x] unit tests, [x] perf harness, [x] feature flag, [x] docs, [x] canary plan, [x] rollout observability. Requests for reviewers: sanity-check admission fairness under synthetic skew, validate snapshot correctness for non-deterministic prefix transforms, confirm perf numbers on internal bench farm.

Sofia Nguyen: The resolver checks snapshot tag + model pin; duplication is possible only when model config differs mid-request, which we explicitly disallow — added assert and a metric to catch regressions.

Sofia Nguyen: Initial CI job attempted to run on a non-pinned runner; fixed perf-check workflow to use gpu-pinned executor, rerun passed.

title: quarantine-sse-chunks-and-delimiter-healing-for-partial-json
body:
quarantine-sse-chunks-and-delimiter-healing-for-partial-json

Context and motivation: We observed intermittent client-side crashes and invalid JSON errors when streaming long chat responses through the OpenAI-compat SSE adapter. Root cause: a mix of small TCP packet boundaries, server-side aggressive chunking, and occasional delimiter bytes embedded in model token escapes resulted in mid-JSON fragments being emitted without clear boundaries. Prior fixes focused on delimiting heuristics but still allowed tight races where a fragment split removed the terminal '}' or a tool-call sentinel.

This PR implements a two-part strategy: (1) a quarantining window for suspect fragments so the parser doesn't emit partial JSON to higher layers until it has greater confidence; (2) a delimiter-healing state machine that uses lightweight delimiter fingerprints, sequence-checkpoint hints, and backoff/hedging to reconstruct or request missing spans where possible. Together these reduce spurious parse errors, avoid delivering truncated structured outputs to callers, and maintain OpenAI-compat behavior for function/tool calling.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced pkg/sse/healer.go: quarantine buffer, delimiter fingerprinting, and a non-blocking repair loop that attempts local reassembly before escalating to a retry/hedge policy.
- Parser changes in pkg/sse/parser.go: tag suspicious chunks with a quarantine flag, defer JSON emission until healer signals a boundary-safe span. Added hooks for seq checkpoints emitted by the runtime.
- Compatibility adapter update in api/openai/compat/streaming_adapter.go: preserve original event ordering and ensure function-call sentinel handoff is only exposed after heal/commit.
- New unit and fuzz tests in pkg/sse/healer_test.go covering: escaped delimiter collisions, UTF-8 split across frames, and synthetic out-of-order fragment arrivals.
- Added an e2e scenario harness tests/e2e/sse_partial_json.yaml to reproduce previous customer-visible failure.
- Documentation: docs/streaming-framing.md expands the guidance on quarantine behavior and rollout knobs.

Implementation notes and heuristics:
- Quarantine window is size-bounded (config default 4KB, configurable per-route) and time-bounded (default 500ms). Suspicious fragments are identified by checksum mismatch of delimiter fingerprint and by trailing-token heuristics (incomplete UTF-8, unbalanced braces, dangling tool-call sentinel).
- Delimiter fingerprint: a tiny canonicalization of trailing bytes and escape context to detect fragmented delimiters without maintaining full tokenization state. This allows cheap detection and grouping of fragments that likely belong to the same logical JSON span.
- Healing flow: local coalescing -> fingerprint match -> emit; if local coalescing fails within the window we fall back to issuing a hedged request for the missing tail from the model-serving layer (configurable; default off in hosted to avoid duplicate billing).
- Backpressure: create a soft-fence that slows downstream delivery if quarantine occupancy grows; integrates with scheduler to prioritize completing suspect spans.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests added for all heuristics and edge cases. Fuzz harness included to stress UTF-8 splits and delimiter collisions.
- E2E harness reproduces the customer failure vector and shows the new parser reduces invalid-JSON delivery rate from 0.9% to <0.01% under synthetic congestion.
- CI: lint + unit + e2e (the e2e job is gated behind an opt-in label in CI to keep default runs fast).

Rollout and compatibility:
- Feature gated behind experimental flag 'sse_quarantine_healer' controlled at route-level in the config. Default: off for non-Redwood dedicated/private until a quiet period of 72 hours in canary.
- No breaking API changes. The adapter preserves OpenAI stream semantics but delays commit of structured outputs until the fragment is healed; client-visible behavior only differs by fewer parse errors and a bounded (~500ms) potential additional delay when quarantine heuristics trigger.

Checklist:
- [x] Parser q/o quarantine flag
- [x] Healer state machine + unit tests
- [x] Integration tests for function-call sentinel ordering
- [x] Fuzz tests for UTF-8 and delimiter collisions
- [x] Docs update and rollout notes
- [x] CI green (with opt-in e2e)

Notes and follow-ups:
- Instrumentation: added metrics sse.quarantine.size, sse.heal.attempts, sse.heal.success_rate for the console. Follow-up: add trace tags to token-level traces for postmortems (ENG-4527).
- Consider exposing a per-tenant hedging opt-in for Dedicated customers; this is tracked as ENG-4579.

Related work: references prior SSE fixes but takes a different approach by quarantining ambiguous fragments instead of immediate delimiter-normalization. This is complementary to the checksum/seq approaches in earlier PRs and reduces noisy false-positives in structured output parsing.

title: Console: marketplace onboarding entrypoint + improved entitlement error handling
body:
Console: marketplace onboarding entrypoint + improved entitlement error handling

Summary: Adds a marketplace-specific entrypoint to the Console onboarding flow (AWS/GCP) with clearer states for entitlement linking and improved error handling/retry guidance. Motivation: Marketplace buyers are currently landing in the generic signup flow and getting stuck on entitlement propagation and “already has org” edge cases; this PR adds a dedicated path and maps entitlement verification errors to actionable UX. Scope: (1) New /onboarding/marketplace route and “Continue from AWS/GCP Marketplace” CTA on the signup screen behind feature flag console.marketplaceOnboardingEntrypoint. (2) Marketplace-specific stepper screens: Connect subscription → Link or create Redwood org → Create first API key → Next steps. (3) Error mapping for entitlement verification endpoint responses (from PR #19875) with user-facing copy, retry timers, and support handoff. (4) Edge-case handling: existing orgs (prompt to link), multiple subscriptions per org (select subscription), delayed entitlement propagation (retry + status), and “wrong cloud” subscriptions (AWS vs GCP mismatch). (5) Adds instrumentation hooks for funnel stages (events used by ENG-22114/PR #19877), but does not ship dashboards here. UX notes: Includes design review changes requested in DES-912 (copy, button labels, and layout adjustments) and a persistent “Need help?” panel linking to marketplace onboarding docs + support. Testing: Added unit tests for error mapping + integration-ish tests for the stepper transitions; manual QA performed in staging with mocked entitlement responses. Rollout: Feature flag default OFF; enable in staging immediately; production ramp planned after entitlement sync job hardening (PR #19878).
Key UI flow: Users coming from Marketplace select AWS or GCP (or we pre-fill via query param provider=aws|gcp). We call /api/marketplace/entitlements/verify and render one of: Verified (continue), Pending (retry + explain propagation), NotFound (ask to confirm subscription + provider), Forbidden (tell user to ensure correct marketplace account/permissions), Conflict (subscription already linked to another org), or ServerError (retry + contact support). Error handling strategy: Centralized mapping in marketplaceEntitlementErrors.ts with stable error codes used in UI + telemetry; avoids leaking raw backend error strings. Retry guidance: For pending states we show “This can take a few minutes after purchase” with a 30s retry button and automatic background refresh (max 10 attempts, then suggest contacting support with correlation id). Existing org linking: If user is already authenticated, we route them to “Link subscription to current org” with an org selector if they have access to multiple orgs; if not authenticated we proceed with signup then ask to link/create org. Multi-subscription: When verify returns multiple entitlements, we show a select list with product/SKU label + cloud account id + purchase date; selection is persisted through the session to avoid bouncing. Accessibility: Stepper is keyboard navigable; all error states include ARIA live region updates; checked color contrast after design tweaks. Security/privacy: UI avoids showing full cloud account identifiers; truncates to last 4 and stores full id only server-side. Support handoff: “Contact support” link pre-fills subject and includes correlation id + entitlement verification request id to speed up triage (SUP-4821 learnings).
