title: implement-federated-signal-normalizer-and-granular-cutover-policy
body:
implement-federated-signal-normalizer-and-granular-cutover-policy

Motivation: Recent rollouts showed transient baseline shifts across regions and tenant cohorts that caused noisy canary signals and premature rollbacks. This PR adds a federated signal normalizer to reduce cohort-level baseline variance and a granular cutover policy to enforce phased traffic migration with rollback budget accounting.

What this changes: Implements a normalization stage that consumes per-cohort latency and throughput fingerprints, fits a lightweight robust linear transform (median-based) per-slice, and exposes a normalized delta used by the canary evaluator. Adds a new CutoverPolicy primitive that accepts traffic tiers, staged percentages, cooldown windows, and a rollback-credit budget. The canary orchestrator now uses normalized metrics to compute regression scores and consults the CutoverPolicy before advancing traffic.

Design notes: The federated normalizer operates at two time resolutions: fast (1m) and slow (1h) rolling windows. Each cohort contributes a sketch (p50/p90/p99, qps) to the aggregator; the transform is computed using a robust estimator to avoid being dominated by bursts. The normalized delta is the difference between candidate and baseline after applying cohort transforms and a global shrinkage factor to control sensitivity. CutoverPolicy enforces minimum-successful-probe-counts per stage, consumes rollback-credit on failed stages, and supports emergency-abort hooks.

Backward compatibility: New behavior is gated behind a config flag perf.canary.federated_normalizer=false by default in existing deployments. The CutoverPolicy is available to rollout plans but does not replace existing simple cutover configs.

Testing: Unit tests for transform math and edge cases (empty cohorts, zero traffic) included. Integration harness added that replays historical traffic traces (prod replay + synthetic drift) to validate reduced false-positive rate. End-to-end canary sim shows a 42% reduction in noisy rollbacks on our historical dataset.

Migration & rollout: Feature flagged. Plan: enable in canary lab for two weeks on non-critical namespaces, then enable for low-traffic customers, monitor stability dashboards and rollback budget consumption metrics.

Checklist:
- [x] Algorithm implementation
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] Integration replay tests
- [x] Config gating and docs
- [x] Observability (new metrics + dashboards)

Related: ENG-4210 (reduce noisy canary rollbacks), SUP-9123 (customer incident analysis), ENG-4302 (cutover policy RFC)
Sanjay Rao: Can you clarify how the shrinkage factor is computed? Looks like a tunable hyperparameter - suggest adding a sensible default and a brief comment about tradeoffs.
Rina Kapoor: Added comment and default (0.6). The shrinkage is AggShrink = max(0.1, min(1.0, median_scale * 0.6)). Updated docs section with rationale.
Marta Liu: Integration tests are failing intermittently in CI; seems related to replay trace ordering. Can we ensure deterministic seed in synthetic generator?
Rina Kapoor: Fixed seed and added additional assertions to the replay harness. Re-ran CI - green.
Ethan Brooks: Approving after verifying metrics emission and dashboards. One nit: move the metric name prefix to 'perf_canary.'
Rina Kapoor: Applied rename and force-pushed. Thanks!
- Add federated signal normalizer to reduce cohort baseline noise for canary evaluations.
- Introduce CutoverPolicy for staged traffic migrations and rollback-credit accounting.
- Feature gated behind perf.canary.federated_normalizer flag (disabled by default).

title: Stabilize tool selection precedence and stream-safe message framing for OpenAI compatibility
body:
Stabilize tool selection precedence and stream-safe message framing for OpenAI compatibility

Background: Customers integrating the OpenAI-compatible function/tool calling surface observed nondeterministic tool selection when multiple candidates matched a schema and intermittent corruption of framed streaming messages during rapid tool handoffs. This PR stabilizes selection precedence semantics and introduces a stream-safe framing coordinator to prevent partial-message leakage during tool invocation fallbacks. Motivation: Reduce customer-visible variance in tool_choice outcomes (affecting telemetry and deterministic evals) and stop streaming clients from receiving malformed chunks when we switch to a fallback tool mid-stream. Design summary: 1) Selection precedence: introduce an explicit, layered precedence model evaluated deterministically: exact signature match > schema-subset match > proto-compatible aliasing > fuzzy name match. The resolver now emits a deterministic tie-break key (deterministic hash of normalized signature+schema path) which is used to choose among candidates. 2) Message framing coordinator: add a stream_coordinator that tracks outstanding tool frame boundaries, drains partial frames before switching, and inserts clear boundary markers ("<|tool-start|>","<|tool-end|>") when processing OpenAI-compatible deltas. These markers are stripped by downstream SDKs but are preserved in server-side telemetry to aid debugging. 3) Backpressure and retry: when a fallback is required mid-stream, the coordinator initiates a short (configurable) drain window (default 50ms) to allow in-flight fragments to complete. If fragments do not arrive, coordinator emits a soft-fill token to close the last frame and starts the fallback tool's frame. 4) Compatibility: the change is additive for clients that do not rely on exact chunk contents; for strict byte-level consumers we provide a config flag to disable boundary markers and keep previous behavior. Checklist: - [x] Define deterministic precedence algorithm and deterministic tie-break key - [x] Implement resolver changes and unit tests - [x] Implement stream_coordinator and message markers - [x] Add integration tests for mid-stream fallback scenarios - [x] Update telemetry to record candidate list and selected strategy - [x] End-to-end testing against openai-compat SDK harness - [x] Docs note + migration guidance (see release_notes) Commit summary: 5 commits, largest changes are resolver rewrite and new framing coordinator with tests. CI: flakes on initial run (integration timeout in qemu build); re-ran and all checks passed (unit, linters, e2e). Observability: telemetry now emits tool_choice.candidate_count, tool_choice.selected_key, framing.drain_ms, and framing.boundary_inserted boolean. Files changed (high-level): - pkg/openai_compat/tool_resolver.go: replace ad-hoc matching with layered precedence and deterministic hash key; add extensive unit tests and mocks. - pkg/stream/framing/stream_coordinator.go: new coordinator implementing drain windows and fallback-safe switching. - pkg/stream/framing/message_marker.go: marker insertion/removal logic; feature flag gate. - pkg/api/handlers/tool_invoke_handler.go: integrate coordinator into invoke flow; ensure responses to streaming clients include marker sanitization unless opt-in. - pkg/telemetry/tool_choice_events.go: emit structured events for candidates and selected strategy. - tests/integration/toolcall_streaming_test.go: new scenarios for mid-stream tool switch, partial fragment arrival, and marker-preservation assertions. Migration notes: By default behavior is backward-compatible. Teams with custom byte-level parsers should either opt-in to the legacy no-marker mode by setting OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT_CHUNKS=true or update their SDKs to strip markers; we recommend updating since markers aid debugging. Release notes: "Stabilized OpenAI-compatible tool selection precedence and added stream-safe framing to prevent partial-fragment leakage during mid-stream tool fallbacks. Adds telemetry for tool_choice decisions." Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag openai_compat.stream_safe_framing and enabled for canary clusters for 48 hours before global rollout. Impact and risk: Medium; main risk is clients that perform exact-contents matching on stream chunks. We validated with canary tests and no regressions in latency beyond a median +2ms framing overhead. Support runbook: included in linked_linear ENG-2137; quick mitigation is to toggle OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT_CHUNKS to revert to legacy framing if a customer reports issues.
Hannah Li (reviewer): Can we avoid adding markers by default? Concern about breaking some older SDKs. Author reply: We gate markers behind a feature flag and provide a strict-chunks env var for legacy behavior.
Priya Raman (reviewer): The deterministic hash depends on schema ordering—make sure we canonicalize. Author reply: Resolver now canonicalizes field order and normalizes type aliases before hashing.
Eric Novak (reviewer): Need benchmark of extra latency. Author reply: Added microbench and canary results; median +2ms overhead, p95 unchanged.
Unit tests added for precedence, hashing, and markers (pkg/openai_compat/*). Integration test validates mid-stream fallback and marker stripping. E2E run against compat harness passed after CI rerun. Local perf benchmark included in pr artifacts.
Stabilized OpenAI-compatible tool selection precedence; added stream-safe framing and boundary markers for tool handoffs. Default behavior remains backward-compatible; opt-out via OPENAI_COMPAT_STRICT_CHUNKS.
Enable openai_compat.stream_safe_framing on canary for 48h; monitor tool_choice.candidate_count and framing.boundary_inserted metrics. Document SDK changes in compat guide.

title: decompose-ci-hooks-to-go-plugins-and-update-license-headers
body:
decompose-ci-hooks-to-go-plugins-and-update-license-headers

Motivation: Our presubmit hooks and release preflight are implemented as a mix of bash entrypoints and GitHub Actions composites. This has led to several flakes (subshell quoting, inconsistent PATHs), poor testability, and slow iteration for repo-standard tooling. This PR decomposes core CI hooks into small, versioned Go-based actions (ci-toolchain-bootstrap, ci-lint-adapter, ci-release-smoke) and updates repository license headers to a standard SPDX header for legal compliance.

What changed (high level):
- Introduced a lightweight Go-based action runner under infra/ci/plugins/ that replaces the long-running bash entrypoints. These are intentionally single-responsibility CLIs that read JSON config from stdin for easier testing.
- Bootstrapping: moved toolchain bootstrap logic into ci-toolchain-bootstrap (pins go/node/python versions and provides a hermetic toolcache path). This reduces matrix size by detecting host capabilities at runtime and avoiding unnecessary matrix axes.
- Lint/test adapters: added ci-lint-adapter which normalizes linter invocation across repos and acts as a compatibility shim for legacy configs. This allowed us to simplify the workflow files to a single lint job with sharding hints.
- Release smoke: added ci-release-smoke, a small action used by the release workflow to run a minimal end-to-end smoke test (deploy to staging, run sanity prompts, validate response shape) before signing artifacts.
- License headers: standardized SPDX license headers across changed files and added a simple license-check step to the precommit flow.
- CI changes: updated .github/workflows/ci.yml to use the new actions, trimmed the test matrix by consolidating platform axes, and introduced a fastpath presubmit lane for changes limited to docs and examples.

Why Go actions: Go binaries are hermetic across runners, compile to a single artifact, and are easier to unit test compared to shell scripts. They also avoid frequent quoting and environment issues we saw in bash-based hooks.

Checklist:
- [x] Add Go action sources + build scripts
- [x] Update workflow YAML to use new actions
- [x] Add license header updates and license-check job
- [x] Run full CI and fix resulting lint/test regressions
- [x] Smoke-tested release workflow in staging

Testing notes / validation steps:
1) Local: make -C infra/ci/plugins/ build && ./bin/ci-toolchain-bootstrap --dry-run
2) CI: confirm GitHub Actions 'ci/build' and 'ci/lint' pass (they now exercise the Go binaries via action wrapper)
3) Release smoke: tested on staging tag v2026.02.28-smoke and validated failure/fallback behavior

Related work: ENG-4821 (ci-era modernization), ENG-4999 (release reliability). Also follows-up on past bash-to-go experiments in infra/ci (see PRs: refactor/ci-go-experiment).

title: enforce-rbacv2-ttls-add-auditlink-hmac-and-kms-region-affinity-validator
body:
enforce-rbacv2-ttls-add-auditlink-hmac-and-kms-region-affinity-validator

Motivation: several operational incidents exposed long-lived delegation grants and unverifiable audit links when operators replayed requests across regions. This change introduces three coordinated pieces: 1) an RBACv2 policy TTL enforcement layer that rejects or soft-expunges stale delegation bindings; 2) an audit-link HMAC signing scheme so downstream consumers can validate event continuity without exposing key material; and 3) a KMS region-affinity validator that checks KMS wrap/unwrap requests against the tenant's declared region pins and fails fast when mismatches are detected. The work here is intentionally conservative: enforcement is gated behind a feature flag and we ship a migration helper to identify bindings that would be impacted. Checklist: - [x] implement policy TTL validator with unit tests - [x] wire TTL checks into policy evaluation path (non-blocking mode behind flag) - [x] implement audit-link signing middleware and verification util - [x] implement KMS region-affinity validator and attach to crypto-proxy - [x] add migration script to identify stale bindings and generate a remediation plan - [x] add e2e tests exercising an operator delegation lifecycle across regions - [x] update docs and runbook snippets - [x] telemetry: policy_denied_ttl, auditlink_verify_ok, kms_affinity_mismatch KB/Linear references: ENG-4891 (policy TTL enforcement), SEC-102 (audit-link design), SRE-317 (kms affinity checks). Rollout plan: 1) deploy to staging with feature flags OFF. 2) run migration scanner (tools/bin/scan-stale-bindings) against a snapshot and produce remediation CSV. 3) enable TTL soft-deny mode (record metrics and allow override via operator flag) for two weeks. 4) enable hard deny for tenant groups with low risk. 5) enable HMAC signing and rotate audit verification keys via the key-manager endpoint. 6) enable KMS affinity validator in read-only mode (log+metric only) for 1 week then hard-fail. Backwards compatibility: audit-link signing uses an optional header (X-Audit-Link-Signature). Legacy consumers ignoring the header will continue to receive events. The RBACv2 evaluation path accepts both TTL-marked bindings and legacy bindings; the migration script annotates bindings that require attention. Security considerations: the HMAC secret is stored in KMS-scoped secrets; verification keys are published to the internal key-discovery service with ACLs. The KMS validator only checks location tags and does not change crypto operations. Migration tool: tools/migration/identify_stale_rbac_bindings.py ships in this PR and produces CSV (tenant_id, binding_id, expiry, last_seen, recommended_action). Testing: unit tests for validator logic (policy, auditlink, kms) included; e2e uses a local crypto-proxy test harness and a vm-simulated multi-region runner. Follow-ups: tie TTL metrics to Optimize so customers get suggestions for binding pruning; add a remediation UI in Console; and add an operator CLI to bulk-revoke stale bindings.

Ethan Liu: approved after one follow-up fix.
Enforced TTLs for delegations (opt-in -> soft-deny -> hard-deny rollout), introduced audit-link HMAC signing for verifiable audit continuity, added KMS region-affinity validator and a migration scanner to identify stale bindings. See docs/runbooks/policy-ttl-migration.md for migration steps.

title: Hotfix: fix metric cardinality regression in overload events
body:
Hotfix: fix metric cardinality regression in overload events

Context: During the hot-route capacity protection rollout we introduced new overload event metrics (shed/admission_control) that were intended to be low-cardinality (route_group, tier, region, reason). In the last merge window we accidentally started emitting per-request / per-tenant labels on the overload event counters due to a tag plumbing change in the gateway -> telemetry bridge. This caused a rapid increase in series count in Prometheus and intermittent ingestion backpressure, and it also made the SRE dashboards noisy/slow to load. What changed: (1) Add a strict label allowlist for overload event metrics in the telemetry emitter and drop/ignore all non-allowed labels (e.g., tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, api_key_id, user_agent, model_revision). (2) Split the old overloaded "overload_event" into two metrics: redwood_overload_shed_total and redwood_overload_admission_denied_total with a stable label set {route_group, tier, region, reason}. (3) Add a lightweight counter redwood_overload_labels_dropped_total{metric_name,label_key} to make future regressions visible without paging the fleet. (4) Update dashboard queries to use the new metrics and remove the accidental group-by on tenant_id. Notes: This is intentionally conservative and enforces invariants close to the emitter to avoid future regressions from upstream tag propagation. This does not change overload behavior itself; only metric emission. Validation: Verified in staging by replaying overload simulation traffic and confirming series count stays flat; production canary (us-east) shows series count returning to baseline within ~30 minutes after rollout. Checklist: [x] Unit tests for allowlist behavior + label drop accounting [x] Update dashboards/recording rules in monorepo bundle [x] Backwards-compat shim: keep the old metric name as an alias for 7 days (deprecated) to avoid alert breakage during rollout [x] Added runbook note: "If series count spikes, check labels_dropped_total". Rollout plan: Merge + deploy with standard gateway release train; no flag required. Monitoring: prometheus_remote_write_queue, series_count by job=telemetry, and the hot-route protection dashboards (ENG-4926).
Logan Wright (review): Can we guarantee we never re-introduce tenant_id via shared context tags? The code path currently merges request-scoped tags by default in a couple places.
Nadia Rahman (author): Yep — this change applies the allowlist at the last possible step (right before emit). Even if upstream merges request context tags, they’ll be dropped for these metric names. Added a unit test that simulates request tags containing tenant_id/request_id/trace_id to ensure they never make it through.
Allison Grant (review): Please keep naming consistent with the metrics standard doc: *_total suffix and reason label values should be stable enums. Also avoid label_key cardinality explosion in labels_dropped_total.
Nadia Rahman (author): Updated metric names to *_total and normalized reason values to the existing enum set (quota, overload, capacity, circuit_open, unknown). For labels_dropped_total, label_key is limited to a small allowlist of known-problem keys (tenant_id, request_id, trace_id, api_key_id, user_agent, model_revision) to keep it bounded.
Rafael Mendes (review): For SRE: will this break existing alerts today? We had a paging storm risk if panels fail to load during an event.
Nadia Rahman (author): Added a 7-day alias gauge/counter mapping (old name emits the same value with the same stable labels) and updated dashboards/recording rules in this PR. Alerts should continue to work immediately, but they’ll use the new rules once deployed.
Caleb Johnson (review): Any evidence this fixes remote_write lag? Also, can we add a note to the runbook on how to confirm cardinality is back to baseline?
Nadia Rahman (author): Added staging evidence to the PR description and included a runbook snippet pointing to series_count{job="api-gateway"} and top label keys via promtool/cardinality panel; also added labels_dropped_total to the dashboard so on-call can confirm the guardrail is working.

title: Tool fanout result coalescer + idempotent retry semantics, OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments
body:
Tool fanout result coalescer + idempotent retry semantics, OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments

Motivation: Multi-tool call ergonomics have been a recurring source of edge cases in production: duplicated side-effects when retries occur, inconsistent result injection order when tools run in parallel, and poor streaming behavior for OpenAI-compatible clients when tool outputs are interleaved. This PR implements a small surface and runtime contract to make parallel tool execution idempotent-safe and to provide deterministic result coalescing while preserving streaming semantics for OpenAI-compat streaming endpoints.

What this changes (single-string summary): Adds a lightweight 'fanout coalescer' in the call_executor to collect tool outputs, canonicalize ordering, and attach deterministic metadata (call-id, attempt-id) so retries are recognized and dropped when duplicate. Introduces an idempotency key into the tool invocation layer; retries with same key now produce deduplicated results at the injector. Adjusts streaming adapter in the OpenAI compatibility layer so that streaming events for tool outputs are emitted as a consistent, monotonic sequence and include a new 'tool_chunk' envelope for downstream SDKs to reassemble. Updates SDK TypeScript helper to surface tool attempt metadata to application code and adds end-to-end integration tests.

Design notes: The coalescer maintains per-request transient state in memory (bounded map keyed by tool-call-id) and attaches an ordinal slot for each tool invocation based on the logical call graph generated during planning. When a tool returns, its output is buffered briefly (100ms by default) to allow aligned arrival of parallel calls; this avoids janky interleaving in the streaming API while keeping latency impact small for common workloads. The idempotency key is generated by the platform caller (or can be provided by the SDK) and is propagated through the public API headers. On receiving a retry, the coalescer checks (tool-call-id, idempotency-key, attempt-id) triple to determine uniqueness.

OpenAI-compat streaming adjustments: Previously, tool outputs interleaved raw tokens into the top-level event stream which caused downstream reassembly problems for clients expecting coherent 'tool' blocks. This patch adds a lightweight 'tool_chunk' event envelope: {"type":"tool_chunk","tool_id":"...","offset":123,"attempt_id":"...","data":"..."} so SDKs can accumulate chunks and publish a single 'tool_result' once coalesced. The server still emits partial results as streaming chunks but tags them explicitly to avoid confusion with assistant tokens. The compatibility adapter also upgrades connection-level metadata so that older SDKs still receive assistant tokens unchanged if they do not understand the 'tool_chunk' envelope (backwards compatible).

Developer ergonomics and API surface: - New header: X-Redwood-Tool-Idempotency: <opaque-key> (optional). If omitted, the platform synthesizes one per request. - Tool call metadata available in streaming events and final result: attempt_id, idempotency_key, call_index. - Behavior guarantees: a single final tool_result will be injected per (tool-call-id, idempotency_key) pair, even with multiple attempts.

Testing and validation: Added integration tests that simulate parallel tool fanout with intentional delays and generated retries. Tests cover: deterministic ordering, deduplication on retries, streaming chunk reassembly, and fallback to legacy stream behavior for old clients. Load microbenchmarks show median end-to-end add-on latency of +8ms for typical 2-tool fanout and worst-case +43ms for bursty 8-tool scenarios (configurable buffer window reduced for latency-sensitive tenants).

Migration: No breaking changes. SDKs updated but older SDKs continue to work: they will receive chunked tool outputs as additional assistant tokens (compat path). We recommend SDK upgrades to take advantage of attempt metadata for safer side-effect handling.

Operational concerns: The coalescer uses an in-memory bounded cache with TTL; in Dedicated/Private deployments this stays node-local. For strict cross-node idempotency (rare), we added a toggle to persist minimal idempotency markers to the global metadata store (disabled by default). Metrics: new counters for tool_coalesce_count, tool_dedupe_count, tool_stream_chunk_bytes; new alert when tool_dedupe_rate > 5% over 5m.

title: E2E: Hosted canary rollout workflow (create/start/step/pause/rollback + approvals)
body:
E2E: Hosted canary rollout workflow (create/start/step/pause/rollback + approvals)

Context: As part of Hosted canary rollouts GA, we need reliable end-to-end coverage across Console → orchestrator → policy engine → routing enforcement → telemetry. This PR adds Playwright-based E2E tests that exercise the happy path and the high-risk control paths (pause/rollback, approvals required, and SLO auto-stop). The suite is written to run in CI against the shared staging environment using dedicated test tenants/routes, and is structured to minimize flakiness (deterministic cohorting assertions, eventual consistency waits, and tighter network mocking where appropriate). Scope: (1) Create rollout via Console wizard: pick Hosted route, select baseline vs canary model version, define traffic schedule (1% → 5% → 25%), configure guardrails. (2) Start rollout and validate routing split enforcement: verify request cohort assignment stickiness and that approximate canary traffic matches config within tolerance (per region + aggregate). (3) Progress steps with soak-time handling: verify step cannot be advanced before min soak unless privileged override; verify audit activity entries appear for each action. (4) Pause and resume: verify can pause during a soak, traffic split freezes, and resume continues from the paused step. (5) Rollback: verify rollback sets split back to 0% canary and routes to baseline; confirm activity timeline shows rollback action and reason. (6) Approval-required flow: verify policy engine blocks step change without approver; verify approver user can approve; verify audit log event emitted with actor + diff. (7) Auto-stop/rollback wiring (smoke): simulate SLO breach signal via test-only metrics hook and assert rollout transitions to paused/rollback per policy, and the UI shows the stop reason. Notes/assumptions: - Uses TEST_ONLY endpoints guarded behind env var + allowlisted tenant to set synthetic metrics and accelerate soak time in staging CI. - Makes no assertions about chart rendering details (covered by unit tests); instead asserts the underlying cohort metrics API returns expected series labels and non-empty values. - All tests tag created rollouts with run_id and perform cleanup to reduce test pollution. Follow-ups: - Expand multi-region coverage to include ap-southeast during GA hardening (blocked on staging capacity). - Add “retry + streaming request” cohort stickiness test once streaming retry semantics land (see ADR cohorting + PR-28741).
Dylan Brooks: This is the coverage we needed for GA. Two questions: (1) can we avoid relying on chart UI selectors? (2) what’s the expected tolerance on traffic split assertions? Leila Farouk (author): (1) Yep—updated to assert cohort metrics API payload + the presence of the cohort labels instead of reading chart DOM. UI selectors are now only for wizard navigation + action buttons. (2) Added helper assertSplitApprox(split, tolerance=0.08) with min sample size guard; in staging we send 400 requests per step, so tolerance is stable. Chloe Martin: I’m a bit nervous about the TEST_ONLY metrics hook. Is it tenant-allowlisted and off by default? Leila Farouk: Yes—guarded behind ROLLOUT_TEST_ONLY_HOOKS=1 and allowlists the e2e tenant id; endpoints return 404 otherwise. Also added a unit test to ensure the allowlist check is enforced. Mina Haddad: For routing enforcement, the test currently hits a single region. Can we at least validate that the cohort key stays sticky across retries? Leila Farouk: Added a stickiness assertion where the same request_id hashed key stays canary/baseline across 20 requests; for cross-region we still only assert aggregate because staging doesn’t have consistent ap-southeast capacity in CI. Added follow-up note in description. Sean Gallagher: Please add guardrails to prevent alert spam in staging (we’ve seen e2e cause noisy dashboards). Leila Farouk: Updated the synthetic breach to use the test-only signal path that does not emit customer-facing alerts; it only flips orchestrator state. Also added tags rollout_test_run=true so we can filter dashboards. Connor O'Brien: CI flaked twice on the step soak wait. Can we reduce wall time and tighten eventual waits? Leila Farouk: Changed to use accelerated soak in staging (test-only) and replaced fixed sleeps with eventually() polling + deadline. Reduced suite runtime from ~18m to ~9m. Chloe Martin: One more: approvals flow should verify audit event actor + diff. Leila Farouk: Added assertion that activity timeline includes APPROVAL_GRANTED with actor email and step_percent change diff. Approved. Mina Haddad: Approved with the note that we should add streaming retry coverage later. Sean Gallagher: Approved; thanks for the staging noise guard. Dylan Brooks: LGTM. Merge after green.
2025-04-22 — PR opened by Leila Farouk; initial suite added for create/start/step/pause/rollback. 2025-04-24 — First CI run shows flake in soak-time step progression; rerun passes; reviewers request eventual waits + reduced reliance on UI selectors. 2025-04-25 — Added metrics API assertions and replaced sleep with polling; introduced test-only accelerated soak and allowlist guard for staging. 2025-04-26 — Added approval-required flow assertions including audit timeline diff/actor checks; sharded CI workflow. 2025-04-28 — All checks green; approvals from Console, Routing, and SRE; merged via squash.
Internal: Adds GA-critical E2E coverage for Hosted canary rollout workflow including approvals and rollback paths; improves confidence in routing split enforcement and orchestrator policy wiring.

title: Adaptive shadow fusion with staged canary promotion and rollback mitigator
body:
Adaptive shadow fusion with staged canary promotion and rollback mitigator

Summary: This PR implements an adaptive 'shadow fusion' controller that continuously evaluates shadow traffic fidelity and can promote traffic slices to a staged canary when a multi-metric confidence threshold is met. It ships a 'rollback mitigator' subsystem that generates and validates dry-run rollback plans (snapshots + quick-rewind playbook) to reduce mean time to recover when regressions are detected. Motivation: Customers running shadow validations before canary promotion wanted fewer manual gating steps and faster recovery options. This change reduces manual toil, shortens promotion windows, and makes rollbacks reproducible and auditable.

What changed (high level):
- New controller: controller/promotion/shadow_fusion_controller.go — fusion logic evaluates grouped shadow traces, computes a fused fidelity score across latency/cls/semantic drift metrics, and coordinates staged promotions.
- Rollback mitigator: server/rollback/mitigator.go + docs/runbooks/rollback-mitigator.md — builds dry-run rollback plans, snapshots model pins, and verifies replays in a sandboxed dry-run.
- Telemetry federation: telemetry/federation_collector.go — aggregates short-lived session histograms from shadow lanes to compute cohort-level fidelity without sampling bias.
- Small API: api/rollouts/v1/promote.proto + api/rollouts/handlers.go — expose a PromotePreview endpoint that returns a promotion score and a precomputed rollback plan id.
- E2E tests: tests/e2e/shadow_fusion.spec.ts + tests/unit/mitigator_test.go — cover fusion scoring, smoke promotion, and rollback dry-runs.

Design notes and safety gates:
- Fusion scoring is ensemble-based: a weighted median of normalized metrics (p95 latency delta, token-level perplexity proxy, semantic embedding cosine drift, error-rate uplift). We enforce a quorum (>=3 of 4 metric bands must be within configured thresholds) to avoid single-metric flapping.
- Promotion is staged: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50%. Each stage requires the fusion score to remain above the acceptance threshold for a stability window (configurable; default 10 minutes).
- Rollback mitigator creates an immutable rollback plan (snapshot of model version, routing table, KV-cache checkpoint) and runs a dry-run replay in a sandbox. The mitigator scores the rollback plan for safety and time-to-recover and attaches cost/time estimates to the PromotePreview response.

Example usage (PromotePreview):
- Client: POST /v1/rollouts/preview with target model and cohort selector
- Response: {"fusion_score": 0.92, "quorum": true, "rollback_plan_id": "rb-20260218-89af", "estimated_recovery_minutes": 3}

Small code snippet (fusion heuristic):
- normalized := map[string]float64{"latency": norm(p95Delta), "perplexity": norm(ppDelta), "embed": norm(1-cosineDrift), "errors": norm(errorUplift)}
- scores := values(normalized)
- fusionScore := median(scores) * quorumFactor(scores, thresholds)

Testing and CI: All unit tests and e2e runs pass in the CI job. Added targeted flake-resistant tests that exercise time windows using the testclock in controller/testutil. CI job summary: build: pass, unit: pass, integration: pass, e2e: pass.

Rollout plan and observability:
- Default rollout policy uses the new fusion controller. Operators can opt out by setting annotation rollout.strategy=legacy.
- Console: new per-rollout panel (Console -> Rollouts) shows fusion score, contributing metrics, rollback plan id, and sandbox replay outcome.
- Alerts: two rule templates added: rollout-fusion-drop and rollback-mitigator-failure.

Backward compatibility and migration:
- No breaking API changes; new PromotePreview endpoint is additive.
- Existing rollouts remain on the stable promotion controller until annotated.

Risk and mitigation:
- Risk: improper weighting could bias promotions. Mitigation: default weights conservative, staged increases small, and PromotePreview surfaces the plan for manual review.
- Risk: rollback dry-run could be slow for very large models. Mitigation: mitigator supports fast-path lightweight snapshots and prioritizes KV/cache-less reverts when full snapshot is costly.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implementation of fusion controller and rollback mitigator
- [x] Unit tests for fusion heuristics and mitigator planner
- [x] E2E shadow->canary smoke tests
- [x] Console panel + runbook entry
- [x] Linear tasks updated (ENG-2345, ENG-9876)

Commits summary: see commit list.

Related work: builds on prior shadow-promote efforts but differs by producing an explicit, runnable rollback plan and scoring promotions with a fused, quorum-driven metric. Links: Linear/ENG-2345, Runbook link: docs/runbooks/rollback-mitigator.md

Notes for reviewers: focus on the fusion thresholds (controller/promotion/shadow_fusion_controller.go) and mitigator sandbox isolation (server/rollback/mitigator.go). The mitigator intentionally keeps the dry-run environment resource-limited to avoid noisy neighbour effects.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main after CI green and approvals.

Introduces an adaptive shadow->canary promotion flow with an automated rollback mitigator. Adds telemetry federation for fidelity scoring and a dry-run rollback planner for faster, safer reverts.
Raj Patel (reviewer): Could the quorum requirement be relaxed for low-traffic cohorts? Concerned about overfitting to noisy embedding signals.
Maya Chen (author): We added a per-cohort override — low-traffic cohorts use a longer stability window and a lower quorum threshold; documented in the controller config. Also added a unit test for the longer window behavior.
Elena Gomez (reviewer): The mitigator's sandbox needs a hard CPU/memory cap to avoid interfering with production. Where is that enforced?
Maya Chen (author): Sandbox limiter is enforced in server/rollback/sandbox_manager.go (new file) — it's configured via rollout.sandbox.* flags. I included the default caps in docs/runbooks/rollback-mitigator.md.
Ibrahim Noor (approver): Verified e2e smoke locally with the staging cluster; fusion scores behave as expected. Approving.

title: Introduce Elasticity Scribe and Deferred Burst Signing
body:
Introduce Elasticity Scribe and Deferred Burst Signing

Motivation: Fleet autoscaling decisions are currently opaque to SRE/finance and hard to replay for incident postmortems. Bursts are granted by runtime heuristics without a signed provenance; downstream gateways cannot reliably attribute temporary capacity to a formal commitment. This PR introduces two related components: (1) Elasticity Scribe: an append-only, compact audit trail of autoscaler decisions (scale up/down, prewarm, deferred decommit) that captures inputs, chosen action, and rationale; (2) Deferred Burst Signing: a lightweight signing service that issues short-lived cryptographic tokens when the autoscaler authorizes temporary burst capacity. The signed token includes tenant id, committed delta, expiry, and a decision_id that links to the scribe entry. Design highlights: - Elasticity Scribe writes protobuff-style records to a configurable backend (default: compressed protobufs to the existing fleet-telemetry bucket). Records include timestamp, decision_id (UUID), contributors (utilization, queued tokens, headroom, prediction), chosen action, and confidence score. - Deferred Burst Signing exposes an internal-only gRPC endpoint used by the autoscaler; tokens are signed using the cluster key in KMS and include a verifiable HMAC and simple nonce to prevent replay. Gateways validate tokens before honoring burst capacity. - New CRD FleetElasticityPolicy: opt-in fields for scribe retention window, burst-signing enabled, and max-deferred-burst-duration. - Telemetry: counters/gauges (redwood_elasticity_decisions_total, redwood_elasticity_decision_latency_seconds, redwood_burst_signatures_issued_total, redwood_burst_signature_validation_failure_total) and labels to correlate tenant, pool, and decision_type. - Observability: Grafana dashboard and a LogQL quick query for postmortem analysis (decision timeline, queue correlation). Rollout plan: 1) Feature-gate off by default. 2) Canary in internal dedicated fleet for two weeks with scribe only (no enforced gating). 3) Enable burst signing in a single region with gateways updated to validate tokens for a subset of tenants (10% traffic). 4) Fleet-wide enable after 3 successful canaries and one incident-free billing cycle. Checklist: - [x] Prototype scribe writer and minimal storage adapter - [x] Deferred burst signing API + KMS integration - [x] Unit tests for scribe encoding/decoding and token validation - [x] E2E test in perf-canary harness (stable for 48 hours) - [x] Telemetry and dashboard definitions - [x] Docs: operations and upgrade notes - [x] Security review (key rotation and token TTL constraints) Backwards compatibility: Gateways that do not validate tokens will ignore the signed burst header; signing is additive and controlled by FleetElasticityPolicy. Impact to billing: this PR provides better attribution and does not change billing behavior until accounting hooks are switched on in a follow-up. Related: ENG-1839 (decision replay tooling), ENG-1942 (burst accounting schema).
Add Elasticity Scribe (audit trail for autoscaler decisions) and Deferred Burst Signing (cryptographically-signed temporary burst tokens). Backward compatible; opt-in via FleetElasticityPolicy CRD. Includes telemetry and dashboards for decision reasoning and burst accounting.

title: Introduce contextual token-latency drilldown, kernel-queue sampler, and alert squelcher
body:
Introduce contextual token-latency drilldown, kernel-queue sampler, and alert squelcher

Context and motivation: We frequently see sporadic tail latency spikes attributed to kernel queueing and cross-route warmup effects. Existing dashboards surface aggregate token latency, but lack an anchored, per-invocation drilldown that attributes time to phases (network, KV lookup, kernel queue, decode). This PR adds: 1) a kernel-queue sampler metric that captures queue depth/inflight-per-gpu-bucket and correlates with token latency; 2) a token-latency drilldown dashboard (per-route, per-model, per-sequence-shape) with phase attribution and example trace links; 3) an "alert squelcher" operator for noisy token-latency alerts that applies quiet windows and cross-invocation deduplication to reduce pager churn. Approach: metric instrumentation is lightweight (O(1) per scheduling tick) and uses reservoir sampling for representative trace correlation. Dashboard changes are additive JSON panels; backend changes include a sampler and an alerting middleware that can be toggled per-team. Migration notes: this adds a new metric (redwood.kernel_queue.depth_bucket) and a new label on token latency spans (token_phase). Consumers must opt in to the alert-squelcher via config. Rollback is safe: metric emission guarded by feature-flag; dashboard panels are additive. Checklist:
- [x] Metric instrumentation and unit tests
- [x] Dashboard panels + drilldown links to trace UI
- [x] Integration tests that validate sampler correlation with traces
- [x] Alert squelcher with config and docs
- [x] Release notes and ops runbook snippets

Files modified / high level changes: see changed_files. Testing and validation: local unit tests included (sampler, dedup logic), integration test that simulates kernel queue pressure and verifies correlation spans are attached, CI run green after fixing a flaky logic path in the reservoir sampler. Performance impact: measured ~0.4% added CPU on scheduling hotpath under 95th percentile load in our perf lab; metric emission is batched to telemetry writer. Backwards compatibility: dashboards and alerts are additive. Operators can disable instrumentation by setting FEATURE_FLAG_OBS_LATENCY_DRILLDOWN=false. Related: Linear ENG-3142 (latency triage UX), ENG-3201 (alert fatigue reduction), internal runbook at docs/internal/obs/latency-drilldown.md.

Maya Chen (author): Reworked the sampler test to avoid sleeps; CI rerun green.

title: Add model metadata schema v1 + JSON Schema validation (with fixtures)
body:
Add model metadata schema v1 + JSON Schema validation (with fixtures)

Summary: Introduces Model Metadata Schema v1 (JSON Schema) as the single contract for served models/variants/quantization profiles, and adds CI validation to prevent invalid/unsafe metadata from landing in the registry. Includes representative fixtures for common model families and quantization profiles that downstream systems (control plane, changelog generator, Console, docs) can rely on for integration testing.

Motivation: Today we have model/version info spread across registry records, runtime config, and docs. This PR establishes a strict, machine-validated contract so we can (a) generate consistent customer-visible release notes and (b) support safe rollout policies with clear compatibility + deprecation semantics.

What’s included:
- Schema v1: `schemas/model-metadata/v1/model_metadata.schema.json`
  - Required identifiers (model_key, version, variant, quantization_profile)
  - SemVer rules and normalization (x.y.z, optional build metadata for internal) with explicit “display_version” for customer-facing surfaces
  - Compatibility constraints (tokenizer, runtime, API feature flags like tool calling / structured output)
  - Safety + quality notes (public/internal separation; public must be non-sensitive)
  - Deprecation block with timeline fields and replacement pointers
  - Rollout eligibility hints (gated fields intended for policy engine; marked as internal-only)
  - Availability matrix by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), with optional region scoping
- Validation tooling:
  - `tools/validate-metadata.ts` validates:
    - JSON Schema conformance
    - invariants we can’t express cleanly in schema (e.g., version monotonicity per model_key+variant, deprecation date ordering, and “public_notes” redaction rules)
  - CI job: `ci/metadata-validation.yml` runs on PRs and blocks merges on:
    - schema invalidity
    - fixtures invalidity
    - breaking schema changes without `SCHEMA_CHANGELOG.md` entry (lightweight guardrail for downstream teams)
- Fixtures:

  - `fixtures/v1/mistral-instruct.fp16.json`

  - `internal.*` (never exported to public release notes; can be used for audit/support)

title: Shadow scoring/ingestion: backpressure + circuit breaker (fail-open) with SRE metrics
body:
Shadow scoring/ingestion: backpressure + circuit breaker (fail-open) with SRE metrics

## Context
During internal dogfood we saw two correlated issues:
1) When scoring workers fall behind (GPU/CPU contention), the scoring queue lag grows and we keep accepting mirrored events at the same rate.
2) When ingestion is degraded (consumer lag / downstream write slowness), we amplify pressure by continuing to emit high-volume shadow artifacts.

This PR adds explicit backpressure + circuit breaker behavior for the shadow pipeline. Importantly: the user/control path must remain unaffected (fail-open).

## What this changes
### 1) Backpressure at the scoring enqueue boundary
- Adds a bounded in-memory admission controller in `shadow-score-dispatcher` (per-tenant + global):
  - `max_in_flight` semaphore for scoring jobs
  - overflow behavior: drop shadow scoring job + emit `dropped_reason` metric/event
  - optional sampling downshift (progressive) when we are near capacity
- Adds dedupe for (request_fingerprint, rubric_version, shadow_variant) within a short TTL to avoid re-scoring duplicate traffic during retry storms.

### 2) Circuit breaker when ingestion/scoring is unhealthy
- Adds a circuit breaker to the shadow artifact emit path (telemetry producer):
  - Opens when either:
    - scoring queue lag exceeds threshold (based on queue depth + moving average service rate), OR
    - ingestion consumer lag exceeds threshold (Kafka consumer lag proxy), OR
    - downstream write error rate > threshold over rolling window
  - When open:
    - routing continues to execute control request normally
    - shadow mirroring remains enabled at policy level, but artifacts are not emitted (effectively: shadow disabled) until breaker half-opens
  - Half-open: allow 1% of shadow events for 60s; close on success, reopen on lag regression.
- All breaker state changes are rate-limited and written to audit-ish operational logs (not customer-visible audit log; that’s separate work).

### 3) SRE-requested metrics (+ default alerts for internal tenants)
New metrics (all cardinality-safe; tenant is bucketed for internal only):
- `shadow_scoring_queue_lag_seconds{env,region}` (gauge)
- `shadow_scoring_admission_in_flight{env,region}` (gauge)
- `shadow_scoring_admission_dropped_total{env,region,reason}` (counter; reason is enum)
- `shadow_ingest_consumer_lag{env,region,topic}` (gauge; topic is allowlisted)
- `shadow_pipeline_circuit_breaker_state{env,region,component}` (gauge: 0 closed / 1 half-open / 2 open)
- `shadow_pipeline_circuit_breaker_open_total{env,region,component,cause}` (counter; cause is enum)

Alerts (internal pack only; tuned for dogfood):
- Page: breaker open > 10m in any region (shadow pipeline unavailable)
- Ticket: drop rate > 1% for 30m (capacity pressure)
- Ticket: scoring lag p95 > 15m for 1h (needs scaling / regression)

## Why this approach
- Keeps hard guarantees: user response is returned from control path regardless of shadow health.
- Avoids cascading failure into telemetry + storage.
- Provides clear signals for oncall: is it lag, drops, or breaker open.

## Testing

  - breaker state transitions (closed -> open -> half-open -> closed)
  - dedupe TTL behavior
- Integration tests (local):

  - ensures router continues to serve control path while breaker open
- Load test notes: on staging, breaker prevents queue growth under forced GPU starvation; control p99 unchanged within noise (+0.2ms on router threads).

## Rollout plan
- Feature flags:
  - `shadow_pipeline_backpressure_enabled` (default: on for internal)
  - `shadow_pipeline_circuit_breaker_enabled` (default: on for internal)
- Start with internal tenants + 1 Dedicated beta tenant after SRE signoff.

## Follow-ups

- Align external alert thresholds per Dedicated/Private defaults (PM/SRE review)

title: Introduce cohort fingerprinting and concise release-note drafter
body:
Introduce cohort fingerprinting and concise release-note drafter

Motivation: teams onboarding models need compact, stable release notes plus reproducible sample cohorts for targeted performance calibration. This PR adds two coordinated pieces: (1) a cohort fingerprint generator that produces stable cohort ids from sampled probe outputs and dataset seed metadata, and (2) a concise release-note drafter that synthesizes short machine-readable + human-friendly release briefs from profile diffs and cohort-level impact metrics.

What this delivers: a reproducible fingerprint used to tag profiling runs and to group telemetry by cohort; and an automated release-note writer that consumes profile deltas, sample cohort summaries, and a template bank to create brief, reviewer-ready release notes for model onboarding. The drafter favors one-line impact statements and a short bulleted summary optimized for engineering change logs.

Changes included (summary): bump profile schema to v1beta3 (backwards compatible with migration path), add cohort_fingerprint module (python), add release_drafter CLI and a templating hook for onboarding pipelines, integrate cohort ids into the profile manifest and the telemetry export schema, add unit/integration tests and a small end-to-end example in examples/registry/drafter_demo.

title: staggered-kv-warmup-and-decode-handshake-to-reduce-prefill-burst-jitter
body:
staggered-kv-warmup-and-decode-handshake-to-reduce-prefill-burst-jitter

Motivation: production workloads show intermittent token-level tail spikes when many concurrent prefill requests attempt to hot-prime the KV cache at the same time. Spiky KV priming increases decode jitter and occasionally pushes requests over latency SLOs. Goal: reduce prefill burst jitter without increasing mean latency or adding heavy serialization.

What this PR does (single-string summary): introduce a staggered per-microbatch KV warmup offset, add a lightweight decode-handshake (2-token soft barrier) that enables safe interleaving of prefill and decode stages, and extend the scheduler with a small credit-based backpressure knob that prefers staggered prefill windows for latency-sensitive routes.

Design notes and rationale: the approach intentionally avoids strict serialization between prefill and decode; instead we: 1) compute a deterministic offset for each microbatch using request hash + configurable stride to scatter KV priming across a small time window (default 6-12ms) so that multiple prefill-heavy arrivals aren’t synchronized; 2) add a non-blocking handshake where the prefill stage returns an early 'ready-for-decode' token after priming critical prefixes (first 2 tokens), allowing the decode stage to start generating while the KV warmup continues in the background for long contexts; 3) expose a scheduler hint (prefill_stagger_ratio) and a credit token mechanism per route so critical low-p99 routes get preferentially staggered windows and credits avoid accidental reentrancy bursts.

Implementation highlights: changes touch the serving scheduler, runtime prefill pipeline, kernel priming logic, and observability hooks. Key new modules: scheduler/prefill_staggerer (algorithm + config), runtime/kv_warmup/offset_priming (deterministic offset generator + randomized jitter fallback), runtime/decode/handshake (soft barrier and token exchange), and metrics/runtime_prefill_jitter and metrics/scheduler_prefill_stagger_ratio.

Compatibility and safety: default behavior is conservative (staggering disabled for routes with very short sequence lengths). All knobs are runtime-configurable via the existing route config proto; safe defaults chosen after internal perf runs. Added unit and integration tests cover deterministic offset behavior and handshake timeout/fast-paths.

Benchmark summary: microbenchmarks on p4d (internal harness) show 8-18% reduction in 99th token latency for mixed prefill+decode workloads at 75% load with no regression in median latency or throughput. KV priming CPU overhead is +1.9% on average due to offset accounting; scheduler overhead is negligible (microsecond-scale).

Operational notes: added two new metrics and one debug flag (enable_prefill_staggering) available via runtime flags. Recommended rollout: enable staging with enable_prefill_staggering=false for canary, then flip on for specific low-p99 routes and monitor metrics/runtime_prefill_jitter and per-route cost.

Related: this complements earlier work on kv-prefetch strategies and prefill windowing; see ENG-3149 for rollout plan and ENG-3161 for dashboarding.

Checklist:
- [x] scheduler and runtime changes implemented
- [x] unit tests for offset generator and handshake timeout
- [x] integration tests for mixed prefill/decode flows
- [x] basic perf runs attached to PR
- [x] runtime flag and route config knobs

title: Introduce connection-shelter orchestrator and deferred-circuit-unwind hotpatch
body:
Introduce connection-shelter orchestrator and deferred-circuit-unwind hotpatch

Hotpatch: add connection-shelter orchestrator to smooth circuit transitions and reduce SLO violations during regional failover; automatic deferred unwind and telemetry anchor. No customer-facing API changes.
Context: During a recent regional failover incident (SUP-4827) we observed abrupt circuit flips causing a spike in 95th/99th latency and a short SLO breach for some tenant classes. This PR implements a lightweight runtime 'connection-shelter' and a deferred-circuit-unwind policy that: 1) preserves in-flight requests in a bounded shelter while circuit state transitions are computed; 2) defers circuit reopen/unwind for a short, telemetry-anchored window to avoid oscillation; 3) exposes per-tenant shelter metrics for SLO accounting. Motivation: provide a pragmatic, low-risk hotpatch that reduces tail spikes and gives the autoscaler and failover path time to stabilize before routes are forcibly reset. Checklist: - [x] implement shelter allocator and bounded queue with per-tenant caps - [x] wire deferred-unwind decision path into circuit manager with a small hysteresis window - [x] add telemetry (shelter_depth, shelter_drain_time, deferred_unwind_count) - [x] unit tests for boundary conditions and race windows - [x] integration test in perf-canary that simulates regional egress flaps Changes (high level): - runtime/circuit/connection_shelter.go: new in-memory shelter with eviction policy and drain hook - runtime/circuit/manager.go: integrate deferred-unwind policy, add decision hooks and metrics - infra/telemetry/metrics_registry.yaml: register new metrics and dashboards notes - perf-canary/scenarios/shelter_drain.yaml: new canary scenario that replays regional disconnects - docs/operational/connection-shelter.md: short runbook and roll-back instructions Commits (summary): - Add connection shelter allocator and per-tenant caps - Integrate shelter with circuit manager and add deferred-unwind window - Add metrics, dashboards, and canary scenario - Tests: unit+integration for race and boundary cases - Fix: reduce default shelter time-to-drain from 5s -> 2s after perf tests Review summary: - Jared Kim (SRE) requested stronger telemetry and an opt-out flag per-tenant; author added tenant opt-out in manager config and extra metrics (shelter_evictions_total) - Lucia Moreno requested that the shelter not exceed connection memory budget; added dynamic cap based on process memory headroom and a safe-guard to force immediate unwind if memory pressure is critical - Evan Brooks asked for a clearer rollback path and a shorter default drain; author reduced default and added a feature-flag gating the behavior for immediate rollback if we see regressions Discussion thread ( high level): - Jared: "Can we get a histogram of shelter_drain_time by tenant tier?" - Aisha: "Added histogram and dashboard; also added a Linear card for SRE to monitor the 95th during canary." - Lucia: "Under memory pressure, we should prefer immediate unwind over OOM risk." - Aisha: "Added memory-pressure fast-path; documented in runbook." CI and validation: - Initial CI run had a flaky integration failure in perf-canary (timeout on scenario orchestration). Re-ran the canary job with extended timeout; all checks passed. - perf-canary run (staging) shows 30-40% reduction in transient 99th latency spikes for affected route samples. Canary verdict: passed with no regressions in throughput. Rollout plan: - Rollout to Dedicated in a canary tranche (2 pools) for 2 hours, monitor shelter_* metrics and 99th latency - If canary is healthy, lift gate to 25% of traffic for 6 hours, then full rollout. Hotpatch notes: this is intended as a low-risk runtime change with a feature flag (runtime.feature.connection_shelter) enabled by default for SRE and disabled per tenant unless opted-in. Merge: squash and merge after approvals. This PR addresses SUP-4827 and should reduce oscillatory reopen events observed during the incident.

title: microbudget-granulator and adaptive-quant-minimizer: tenant-aware cost smoothing
body:
microbudget-granulator and adaptive-quant-minimizer: tenant-aware cost smoothing

Motivation: Customers running multi-tenant workloads report noisy unit economics when small tenants intermittently spike, causing autoscaler thrash and suboptimal quantization choices. This PR implements a microbudget-granulator that smooths tenant-level cost profiles into stable budgeting curves and an adaptive-quant-minimizer that picks the least-aggressive quant tier that meets SLO-delivered quality metrics. The change reduces churn in batching and cache warmups while preserving tail latency. What changed: 1) runtime/prefill/granulator: new microbudget smoothing component that consumes tenant telemetry and emits short-term budget curves used by the batching scheduler. 2) runtime/quant/adaptive_minimizer: decision engine that ranks quant tiers based on simulated-loss impact and recent eval traces, with a safety net to revert if quality drift is detected. 3) admin/cli: add `rw econ profile --dryrun` to preview granulator output and quant recommendations per tenant. 4) telemetry: new metrics tenant.budget_curve.stability, quant.minimizer.rank_distribution, and alerts for quant rollback rate. Design notes: the granulator uses exponential smoothing with per-tenant alpha tuned from historical burstiness percentiles; budgeting windows default to 3m/15m/1h rollups. The quant-minimizer runs ensemble heuristics: a cheap static cost model, a light-weight loss proxy on sampled responses, and a safety evaluator that watches production evals before a recommended change is applied. Rollout plan: feature flag default-off; staged rollout to internal prod, then 10% of tenants for 48h, then full enablement. A/B experiment has been set up to validate unit-econ improvements and key quality metrics. Testing: added unit tests for smoothing math, integration tests for decision flow, and a small e2e against the batcher using a synthetic tenant workload. Related: ENG-1459 tracks follow-up to expose tenant tuning knobs in Console. title: Introduce invocation deja-vu index and alert replay gateway
body:
Introduce invocation deja-vu index and alert replay gateway

Motivation: We frequently see noisy, one-off token-cost/latency incidents that are hard to reproduce and tune alerts for. Ops needs a compact, privacy-safe snapshot that can be replayed (in a sandboxed path) to validate alert thresholds, fallback policies, and model routing behavior. This PR implements a reproducible invocation fingerprint (the 'Deja-Vu Index') and an Alert Replay Gateway to drive deterministic replays of sampled invocations through the serving stack.

What this PR adds (high level):
- a Deja-Vu Index generator that computes a stable fingerprint for an invocation using prompt-shape hash, token-phase histogram, model variant, KV-cache hit profile, and lightweight kernel-queue signature; designed to be stable across minimal tokenization/whitespace differences
- a compact Invocation Snapshot format (sanitized, pseudonymous) that stores the Deja-Vu ID, truncated prompts, token shape metrics, KV cache markers, and a replay hint bundle
- an Alert Replay Gateway service (internal only) that can accept a snapshot and execute a deterministic replay path through a dedicated canary runtime with replay-only tracing hooks
- three Grafana dashboards: DejaVu Explorer, Alert Replay Runs, and Replayed SLO Deltas
- metric and span tags: invocation.deja_vu_id, alert_replay.run_id, replay.trace_phase
- a sampled-log compactor that keeps a delimited, privacy-safe excerpt for each snapshot for human triage
- migration that registers the new metric names and adds a lightweight retention TTL for snapshots.

Why it's safe: Snapshots are sanitized: full user PII is redacted, embeddings are not stored, and prompt payloads are truncated and hashed. The replay path is constrained to dedicated canaries and does not feed outputs back into production logs or billing pipelines. Access to replay snapshots gated by RBAC and audit-logged.

Checklist:
- [x] Deja-Vu Index algorithm and unit tests
- [x] Snapshot format + encoder/decoder
- [x] Replay gateway prototype + integration tests (uses canary runtime)
- [x] Dashboards and example alert-run (example run attached)
- [x] CI: unit/integration/e2e (replay e2e runs in sandbox)
- [x] Docs: docs/observability/deja-vu-replay.md
- [x] Migration: metrics registration and retention TTL

Notes & follow-ups:
- Performance: index computation adds ~120us median overhead per invocation in the fast path; we sample 0.5% by default. We can move to async sidecar if overhead becomes problematic.
- This PR intentionally avoids storing full prompt text; product requested hashed + truncated payloads to allow meaningful triage without exposing PII.
- Next steps: add a replay-run A/B harness to automatically attempt replays for high-confidence SLO regressions and surface suggested alert threshold edits.
Jonas Patel: Nice approach. Two asks: (1) can we add a deterministic seed in the index so replays are bit-identical where possible? (2) please confirm storage TTL and deletion path for snapshots so compliance can sign off.
Maya Chen: Reply to Jonas - added deterministic seed (falls back to zero if unavailable) and added migration + admin API to purge snapshots older than TTL. Updated docs with retention and RBAC notes.
Evelyn Ruiz: Integration tests look good. Found one flaky test on macOS CI (test_replay_gateway::test_replay_path) — looks like a timing assert. Suggest switching to event-driven sync in test harness.

title: credential-prefetch-and-async-generator-ergonomics-bump
body:
credential-prefetch-and-async-generator-ergonomics-bump

Motivation: users report awkward ergonomics when combining credential prefetching with async generator based streaming in the TS SDK; parity gaps vs Go/Python lead to different failure modes under token rotation and transient network retries. This PR introduces a compact credential prefetch adaptor and ergonomic async-generator helpers that unify the lifecycle between TS/Go/Py SDKs while keeping backward-compatible call sites. Changes include: 1) CredentialPrefetcher: a small async factory that preloads short-lived tokens slightly early (configurable grace window) and exposes a lightweight lease object to the generator consumer so callers can opt into pinned credentials for critical sections. 2) AsyncGeneratorAdapter: two helpers (wrapAsyncGenerator and withPrefetch) that make it trivial to attach credential leases and deterministic retry hooks to existing streaming generators without changing upstream code shape. 3) Retry predicate enhancements: add a typed RetryHint returned by the adapter so callers can fine-tune backoff vs fast-fail semantics. 4) Cross-SDK parity shim: minimal API knobs added to the transport layer so Go/Py counterparts can match semantics in follow-up PRs. Compatibility: defaults preserve previous behavior; new helpers are opt-in. Testing: unit tests for lease lifecycle, simulated token rotation, and end-to-end integration using the local mock transport. Also includes updates to docs and a migration note. Impact: small bundle size increase (+2KB gzipped) but meaningful reduction in stream-level race conditions during reauth and fewer transient 401 surface errors in internal canaries.

title: Console UI: add Optimization Suggestions (beta) view behind feature flag
body:
Console UI: add Optimization Suggestions (beta) view behind feature flag

Summary: Implements the new Console page for Redwood Optimize → Optimization suggestions (beta). This is the list + details experience for batching/caching suggestions only. The UI is gated behind a feature flag (optimize_suggestions_beta) and a read permission (optimize:suggestions:read). The page presents estimated savings ($/day + %) and estimated latency deltas (p50/p95), plus a Low/Medium/High risk badge with explanatory copy. Includes list/table layout with filtering/sorting, pagination, a details drawer with assumptions + guardrails, and complete empty/error states. Context: This is the frontend half of the beta Suggestions experience described in PM-842 / ENG-19358. API contract work landed separately (see pr-21934). Risk badge component is shared and comes from pr-21983. Telemetry events are intentionally limited here to basic page-view instrumentation; full funnel events are tracked in pr-22011. Feature gating: (1) Feature flag: optimize_suggestions_beta (org-scoped, remote-config driven). (2) Permission: optimize:suggestions:read (RBAC; UI hides nav + blocks route when missing). When the feature flag is off: the navigation entry is hidden and direct-route access redirects to /optimize (with a toast). When permission is missing: render AccessDenied with a link to internal docs for requesting access (kept behind isInternal guard in prod builds). UX overview: Entry point is Optimize → Suggestions. Default view is a table grouped by Route + Model (not hard-grouped, but those are primary columns). Columns: Suggestion (type: batching/caching), Estimated savings (primary metric, sortable), Risk (badge + tooltip), Confidence (chip), Updated (stale indicator + timestamp). Filters: Model, Route, Region, Suggestion type (Batching / Caching), Risk (Low/Med/High), and a toggle to show dismissed (beta-only; hidden unless ?debugSuggestions=1). Sorting: savings desc (default), savings asc, risk, updated_at. Pagination: server-driven cursor pagination; table supports page size 25/50 (default 25). Details drawer: Clicking a row opens a right-side drawer with: (a) What we recommend (human-readable title), (b) Why we recommend this (top signals, e.g., concurrency, cache hit rate, sequence length distribution), (c) Estimated impact (savings + latency delta with confidence band), (d) Risk & guardrails (explain that risk is performance/reliability risk; not security risk), (e) How to enable (deep links to batching/caching config pages + docs). Drawer also surfaces suggestion_id and stale_as_of timestamp for support/debug. Empty + error states: Added 4 distinct empty states per design spec: No suggestions yet (but telemetry present) → show onboarding text + links; Insufficient telemetry → show requirements (min window + signals) and link to telemetry setup; Feature not enabled → show request access CTA (beta); API error → show retry and status text, plus a small disclosure for request id. Also added skeleton loading for initial fetch and drawer fetch. Implementation details: New route: /optimize/suggestions (lazy-loaded bundle). Data layer: console-web uses the typed REST client; added OptimizeSuggestionsClient with getSuggestions({ filters, sort, cursor, limit }). Normalizes response into table rows; uses suggestion_id as the stable key. State management: useUrlState hook for filters/sort/pagination so the view is shareable and persists across reloads; drawer open state uses suggestion_id in querystring (?sid=...). Accessibility: Table supports keyboard row focus + Enter to open drawer; drawer traps focus; risk badge tooltips are keyboard accessible. Added mocked API fixtures for: insufficient_telemetry, no_suggestions, permission_denied, stale_suggestions. title: Introduce subnet label-driven peering and DNS policy engine
body:
Introduce subnet label-driven peering and DNS policy engine

Motivation: Provide an idempotent, label-driven reconciliation engine that automates VPC peering, subnet ownership assignments, conditional security group attachments, and Route53 private DNS policy wiring for control plane private deployments. Many installers required manual peering and ad-hoc route updates during multi-account and multi-AZ rollouts; this PR introduces a declarative label surface (subnet:role=controlplane|egress|workload and subnet:owner=region/zone/team) and a controller that creates deterministic peering attachments, route propagation, and DNS forwarding records with safe rollback hooks. High-level changes: 1) Terraform module updates to network module to accept subnet labels and to expose peering resource metadata for external controllers; 2) New lightweight reconciler binary (installer/reconciler) that reads desired subnet labels from TF state or cluster config and performs peering/route53 actions via AWS APIs with exponential backoff and state checkpoints; 3) Helm chart changes to controlplane to add DNS glue environment and a readiness probe that verifies private-hosted-zone delegation before advertising endpoints; 4) Upgrade/rollback tooling: terraform plan integration with --dry-run reconciliation mode, a staged canary rollout for peering attachments, and a 'peering-safeclean' command that performs non-destructive teardown and verifies route/classic-record removal; 5) Acceptance and e2e smoke tests that simulate cross-account peering and conditional sg injection. The description below summarizes design, commits, files touched, testing, rollout and rollback instructions, and outstanding follow-ups. Checklist: [x] Add subnet label TF variables and outputs [x] Implement reconciler CLI + unit tests [x] Helm chart: add dnsGlue config + probe [x] Add smoke/e2e tests in perf-canary harness [x] Document runbook and rollback steps [x] CI passing on integration runner. Commits summary: feat(tf): add subnet labels and peering metadata outputs; feat(reconciler): initial controller + checkpointing; fix(reconciler): backoff & idempotency on duplicate attachments; feat(helm): dns-glue env + readiness probe; test(e2e): add cross-account peering smoke; docs: runbook and upgrade notes. Files changed (high level): installer/terraform/modules/network/variables.tf, installer/terraform/modules/network/outputs.tf, installer/terraform/modules/network/peering.tf, installer/reconciler/main.go, installer/reconciler/checkpoint.go, installer/reconciler/aws_client.go, installer/helm/charts/controlplane/values.yaml, installer/helm/charts/controlplane/templates/dns-glue-configmap.yaml, installer/helm/charts/controlplane/templates/readiness-probe.yaml, tests/perf-canary/e2e/peering_smoke_test.go, docs/runbooks/private-controlplane-peering.md, scripts/peering-safeclean.sh, ci/integration/reconciler_integration.yml. Testing performed: unit tests for reconciler (covering duplicate-peering, transient API failures), integration job against a long-running dev AWS account (peering create/accept/route-sync), Helm chart acceptance where readiness probe blocks traffic until DNS glue is present, and an e2e smoke that validated Route53 resolver rules in a shared-hosted-zone configuration. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy TF changes with --target module.network and capture outputs; 2) Run reconciler in --dry-run mode to assert intended peering actions; 3) Rollout reconciler as pre-deploy job to create peering attachments; 4) Deploy controlplane Helm chart (first canary AZ, then global) and validate readiness; 5) Promote reconciler to 'managed' mode to perform route and DNS record updates. Rollback plan: reconciler supports --reconcile-mode=dry|apply|revert; to revert, run --reconcile-mode=revert which performs non-destructive withdrawal of routes and peering attachments while preserving checkpoints to avoid accidently removing shared resources. Security notes: peers are created with restricted security groups and a deterministic tag format (redwood:peering=<cluster>-<env>) so automated cleanup and billing attribution works. Migration notes: Existing installs without subnet labels are supported via a discovery mode (reconciler infers role by CIDR -> az mapping) but will log a migration suggestion to add labels. Outstanding follow-ups: add GCP/Azure provider adapters (tracked ENG-1903), expand RBAC around reconciler KMS usage, and add more granular CircuitBreaker controls in the reconciler to avoid mass-peering during region faults. Merge rationale: validated in integration, adds safe rollback paths and non-breaking terraform outputs; decided to squash merge to keep tf history compact.
Marcus Liu: Can the reconciler avoid creating peering across accounts that are in a billing relationship edge-case? Please add a guard and a dry-run abort on suspicious cross-account pairings.
Author (Ananya Rao): Added a preflight guard that checks allowed-account-list, and reconciler now emits a high-severity log and requires --force to proceed if accounts are not in allowlist.
Helen Park: Helm readiness probe looks good, but add a tolerance for eventual DNS propagation delays (60s -> 300s).
Author (Ananya Rao): Increased probe timeout to 300s and added a toggleable environment variable 'DNS_PROBE_TIMEOUT' to values.yaml.
Add label-driven subnet peering automation and DNS policy engine. Terraform exposes new subnet label inputs and peering metadata outputs. New reconciler binary performs idempotent peering, route and private-hosted-zone wiring with dry-run and revert modes. Helm controlplane chart gets DNS glue and readiness probe. Rollback-safe with 'revert' reconcile mode and peering-safeclean helper.

title: Predictive Headroom Scheduler for Dedicated Fleets
body:
Predictive Headroom Scheduler for Dedicated Fleets

Introduce a predictive headroom scheduler that reserves and releases dedicated fleet capacity based on short-term traffic forecasts and tenant-level SLO intents. Motivation: current reactive autoscalers oscillate under bursty traffic and either overprovision (wasting committed capacity) or underprovision (breaching throughput SLAs). This PR implements an EWMA-based short window predictor augmented with anomaly suppression, a configurable confidence margin, and soft caps for burst-bank integration so tenants keep predictable burst behavior while preserving long-term utilization. Key user-visible behavior: new fleet config fields (prediction_window_seconds, confidence_margin_pct, warmup_duration_seconds, anomaly_backoff) and a per-tenant score that maps predicted QPS to an allocation delta. The scheduler integrates with existing burst token pool logic but prefers predictive headroom for gradual scale-up and falls back to immediate burst tokens only when prediction error is high. Also adds telemetry: predicted_vs_actual_qps histogram, headroom_reservations_gauge, and prediction_error_rate alert. Implementation notes: scheduler service running as part of fleet-controller selects scale actions every 5s by default; uses historical 60s sliding window for EWMA with optional ARIMA feature-flag for customers who opt in on Dedicated. The rollout is gated: config flag predictive_headroom.enabled default false; rollout plan includes Canary on two low-risk fleets, blue/green for Dedicated control plane, and a kill-switch that reverts to legacy autoscaler if error_rate > 5% for 10m. Includes unit and integration tests, new e2e perf canary scenario, and operator docs for tuning margins and warmup. Backwards compatibility: existing autoscaler configs remain valid; predictive configs are additive. See Linear ENG-6291 for acceptance criteria and metrics targets.
Lucas Chen: Overall looks good. Please add a short note on worst-case CPU/GPU footprint of the predictor when run fleet-wide.
Ava Martinez: Added a note and micro-benchmarks in predictive_headroom.go comments and a small CPU budget check in the controller loop.
Priya Nair: Request change: tighten default confidence_margin_pct from 25 to 15 for lower-median tenants; updated defaults in helm values.
Marcus Bell: Approved after verifying telemetry metrics and canary results in staging. Left one optional nit about doc phrasing.
Merged after canary validation; no rollback needed. Enabled behind feature flag; dedicated customers must opt in. Canary showed 12% reduction in short-term overprovisioning on test fleets and maintained 99.9% throughput SLO during burst windows.
Introduce predictive headroom scheduler for Dedicated fleets (opt-in). Improves short-term provisioning accuracy to reduce wasted reserved capacity and maintains burst guarantees. Operator tuning guide added.
